techniques.why: sawtooth wave -- the canonical bright analogue waveform: every harmonic present, decaying 1/h; the raw material of brass-like, string-like and lead sounds
techniques.code:
kskew   = 0.02                              ; skew [0.02..0.5]: 0.5 a symmetric triangle, 0.02 a sawtooth
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.00245, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kdty0   poscil 0.0042, 0.057     ; age: shape/duty wobble on kpw
kpw0s0   = kskew + kdty0
aao0s0u0  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 4, kpw0s0, 0   ; wave seg0 imode4 copy 0
acln0   = aao0s0u0 * 1.000000    ; clean oscillator (pre-drive)
adrv0   = acln0                     ; drive 0: clean, no saturator stage
kagw0   oscili 0.0105, 0.7        ; age: amplitude wobble
asig    = adrv0 * (1 + kagw0)

skew.note: how far the symmetric triangle is skewed towards a sawtooth. One `vco2 imode 4` call does the whole travel and converges EXACTLY on `imode 0`'s saw spectrum at 0.02, which is measured in LCO_CONCEPT §5 and is why `triangle` and `saw` are the same body with different defaults rather than two instruments. Centroid 759 -> 2467 Hz and odd/even +39.9 -> +3.3 dB: a triangle has almost only odd harmonics, a saw has all of them, and the axis is the continuous path between. Comb contrast holds near 110 dB throughout -- both ends are exact waveforms, not filtered ones. Loudness 0.01 dB over the whole range.

leaning.gloss: just off symmetric, a little bite

techniques.why: square wave -- odd harmonics only, decaying 1/h: hollow and woody, the clarinet and stopped-organ-pipe family of colour
techniques.code:
kduty   = 0.5                               ; duty [0.05..0.5]: the ON fraction of the cycle
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.00245, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kdty0   poscil 0.0042, 0.057     ; age: shape/duty wobble on kpw
kpw0s0   = kduty + kdty0
aao0s0u0  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 2, kpw0s0, 0   ; wave seg0 imode2 copy 0
acln0   = aao0s0u0 * 0.578000    ; clean oscillator (pre-drive)
adrv0   = acln0                     ; drive 0: clean, no saturator stage
kagw0   oscili 0.0105, 0.7        ; age: amplitude wobble
asig    = adrv0 * (1 + kagw0)

duty.note: the ON fraction of the cycle, which is what duty means. This is the axis BJ's own example asks for — sharp at one duty, hollow at another — and it was impossible while the width was a structural constant. Its objective mark is the odd/even balance, not the centroid: at 0.5 the even harmonics are absent and odd/even reads +29.4 dB (that IS a square), and by 0.05 they are level with the odd ones at +0.8 dB. The centroid is deliberately NOT monotone with it (6304, 5398, 5262, 5148, 5373 Hz at 0.50, 0.35, 0.25, 0.15, 0.05) because a narrowing pulse first loses its top and then spreads energy back up. `vco2 imode 2` holds the level itself: 0.01 dB over the whole range, with no compensation applied.

fat.gloss: just off square, the evens creeping in

reedy.gloss: a quarter cycle -- reedy and forward

sharp.gloss: a spike -- bright, papery, almost a click

techniques.why: pulse-width modulation -- classic PWM: the duty cycle sweeps continuously from 80% down to 20% and back, ~2 s per round trip by default (1 s per half-cycle); slow/fast stretch or compress it to 4 s / 1 s, so the tone hollows out and fills back in
techniques.code:
krate   = 0.5                               ; rate [0.1..8]: how fast the duty sweeps, in Hz
klfo0    oscili 0.5, krate           ; -0.5..0.5, one half-cycle per 1/rate seconds
kpw0     = 0.5 + 0.6 * klfo0     ; duty 0.20..0.80, square at centre
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
apw0     vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 2, kpw0 ; imode 2 = pulse, kpw = width
asig    = apw0 - 0.6 * (2 * kpw0 - 1) ; remove the duty's DC offset, A*(2d-1)

rate.note: how fast the duty sweeps, in Hz. Restored: the parked emitter carried this axis and the harvest dropped it, so `pwm` shipped as a fixed 0.5 Hz sweep. Its signature is the BEAT and not the colour, and the beat comes back at exactly TWICE the rate -- 0.5 Hz reads 1.00, 1.0 reads 2.00, 8.0 reads 16.00 -- because the sweep is symmetric about the square, so the brightness peaks on both sides of every cycle. Depth is constant at 0.22 from 0.5 Hz up. Loudness 0.41 dB across the axis and 0.60 dB crossed with the register; the 0.1 Hz end reads 0.4 dB quieter only because less than half a cycle fits in a four-second render.

slow.gloss: a long breathing sweep, one pass a note

fast.gloss: a visible wobble, four brightness peaks a second

vibrato.gloss: at tremolo speed -- the duty as a texture

techniques.why: pure sine -- a single partial and no harmonic content at all: the reference tone, and the body of a whistle, a tuning fork or a sub-bass
techniques.code: asig    poscil 0.6, (kfreq * koct1)            ; pure tone

techniques.why: additive harmonic stack -- the general-purpose way to build any harmonic instrument colour: a seven-harmonic gbuzz stack doubled by a twin three cents above, so the pair beats slowly; knh sets how many partials, kmul how fast they fall away
techniques.code:
kbright   = 0.68                     ; bright [0.35..0.90]: gbuzz rolloff kmul, both stacks (twin keeps -0.04)
kpartials = 7                       ; partials [3..16]: harmonic count knh, both stacks
kmul1     = kbright
kmul2     = kbright - 0.04
; knh is a harmonic COUNT: quantised to an integer before use, so a fractional
; kpartials (a continuous sweep lands on one) cannot mismatch gbuzz's own integer
; knh against knrm's -- measured, leaving it fractional put a 0.86 dB bump at every
; half-integer (gbuzz's real amplitude does not follow the continuous formula there).
kpi       = int(kpartials)
; gbuzz normalises to PEAK: knrm holds each stack's own loudness as kbright/kpartials
; move, referenced to its value at today's defaults (kbright=0.68, kpartials=7) so the
; ratio is exactly 1 there and today's sound is untouched.
knrm1     = ((1-kmul1^kpi)/(1-kmul1)) / sqrt((1-kmul1^(2*kpi))/(1-kmul1*kmul1)*0.5)
knrm2     = ((1-kmul2^kpi)/(1-kmul2)) / sqrt((1-kmul2^(2*kpi))/(1-kmul2*kmul2)*0.5)
; the two stacks beat (twin +3 cents): each harmonic pair beats at its own rate, so a
; short RMS window catches a different slice of a many-rate beat as kbright moves the
; balance -- and that slice is DIFFERENT at different registers (the absolute beat
; rates scale with the note), so the same fix at 220 hz alone left 1.52 db at 110 hz.
; kbrf is the register in octaves from 220 hz, clamped to the 110-880 hz span this was
; measured over (koct1 -1..2) so the fit is never extrapolated past what was checked;
; ktap fades the correction back to zero over one further octave each side, so a note
; below 55 hz or above 1760 hz reverts to the small, uncorrected raw excess (0.43 db)
; rather than an extrapolated curve fighting a register it was never fitted on.
; kc1r/kc2r hold the excess-vs-bright quadratic's own two coefficients as a further
; quadratic in kbrf, least-squares fit over the raw (uncompensated) excess measured
; at 110/220/440/880 hz (dark=-0.33, bright=+0.22 from the 0.68 default):
;   110 hz: -1.14 / +0.89 db   220 hz: -0.21 / +0.13 db
;   440 hz: +0.09 / -0.12 db   880 hz: +0.08 / -0.07 db  (sign flips between the pairs)
kbrf0     = log2((kfreq * koct1) / 220)
kbrf      = limit(kbrf0, -1, 2)
ktap      = limit(1 - abs(kbrf0 - kbrf), 0, 1)
kc1r      = 0.7758 - 2.2262 * kbrf + 0.8586 * kbrf * kbrf
kc2r      = -0.0680 - 0.8019 * kbrf + 0.3831 * kbrf * kbrf
kbx       = kbright - 0.68
kbexc     = ktap * (kc1r * kbx + kc2r * kbx * kbx)
kbcomp    = 10^(-kbexc/20)
kad0    poscil 0.0004, 0.053         ; slow drift, upper stack
aa10    gbuzz 0.52 * (knrm1 / 3.0293745376), (kfreq * koct1), kpi, 1, kmul1, giCos          ; harmonic stack
aa20    gbuzz 0.34 * (knrm2 / 2.8885033039), (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0018 + kad0), kpi, 1, kmul2, giCos ; twin, +3 cents
asig    = (aa10 + aa20) * kbcomp

bright.note: how bright the two stacks are: gbuzz's own rolloff (kmul) moved together on both, the twin kept 0.04 below the main stack as today. gbuzz normalises to peak, not rms, so knrm holds each stack's own loudness as kmul moves. the two stacks beat (twin +3 cents), and a short rms window catches a different slice of that many-rate beat as the balance shifts -- and that slice is different at different registers: the same compensation that held 220 hz flat (0.17 db) left 1.52 db of excess at 110 hz, 0.73 at 440, 0.66 at 880, because the beat's leak has one sign at 110/220 hz and the opposite sign at 440/880 hz (measured raw, uncompensated: -1.14/+0.89 db at 110 hz, -0.21/+0.13 at 220, +0.09/-0.12 at 440, +0.08/-0.07 at 880, for dark/bright relative to today's default). the fix adds a second fit in the register itself (kfreq*koct1, read as log2 octaves from 220 hz, clamped to the 110-880 hz span this was measured over and faded back to no correction one octave beyond it) so the compensation is a surface in bright and register, not a single curve reused everywhere. loudness now holds to 0.09 db at 220 hz and 0.03/0.08/0.03 db at 110/440/880 hz across the whole range -- down from 0.17/1.52/0.73/0.66 db before this fix. centroid at 220 hz runs 340 -> 798 hz.

dark.gloss: a dull, rounded stack, low harmonics only

bright.gloss: a hard, buzzy stack, the upper harmonics forward

partials.note: the harmonic count (knh) on both stacks, used directly rather than through a 0..1 knob since it is a physical count. quantised to a whole number before use: measured, a fractional knh does not follow the same amplitude law gbuzz uses for an integer one, so leaving it fractional put a 0.86 db bump at every half-integer -- the axis would have been a fader by accident at half its own range. with the count rounded down at the source, knrm holds the loudness as it moves: measured spread 0.03 db at 220 hz and 0.20/0.03/0.02 db at 110/440/880 across the whole 3-16 range -- unaffected by the bright fix above, since bright sits at its own default (kbx=0) while this axis sweeps. centroid at 220 hz runs 394 -> 672 hz.

sparse.gloss: a plain, thin buzz, few harmonics

techniques.why: plain 2-operator FM (ratio 2, index 1.5) -- a carrier and one modulator, sidebands spreading as the index rises: the neutral FM starting point and the root of every DX-family timbre

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

kindex  = 0.200000                ; index [0..1]: how many sidebands -- how bright
kring   = 0.333333                ; ring [0..1]: how long the bright attack rings
kdetune = 0.600000                ; detune [0..1]: the doublet's offset, in Hz
ktm0    init 0
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then

endif

techniques.why: electric piano / rhodes / wurlitzer / dx piano: a struck tine or reed body with a metallic attack that fades back into it; ting = how much metal is in the strike, ring = how long it rings, hollowness = full body to hollow reed, strike = how hard the hammer hits

ting.note: the metallic 'ting' of the attack. this is the single feature that separates an electric piano from a plain fm tone; at 0 the instrument is only its wooden body. the ting fades back into the body as the note is held -- it loses its brightness, never its loudness.

none.gloss: no metal at all, just the woody body

soft.gloss: a faint chime on the attack

clangy.gloss: a hard bright metallic clang on every note

ring.note: how long the metallic part keeps ringing before it settles into the body. short is a quick struck-tine click, long is a sustained metallic buzz that stays through the note. both ends are taken from real electric pianos: the short end is a rhodes-like tine, the long end a wurlitzer-like reed. it is the RATE the tine's own index decays at, keyed to `knote` so it restarts with every note -- an amplitude decay would be pointless, since the host owns the release. measured: the colour travels 211 Hz over the note at short and 1257 Hz at long, at one loudness within 0.02 dB.

short.gloss: a quick click, gone almost at once

long.gloss: a metallic buzz that stays through the note

hollowness.note: the body's character, from full to hollow. Low keeps every harmonic and sounds broad and piano-like; high keeps only the odd ones, which is what makes a reed sound hollow and nasal. 'tine' is where a classic electric piano sits. Its mark is the odd/even ratio and NOT the centroid, which is why both are reported: measured, odd over even goes +7.2 -> +77.4 dB across the axis while the centroid moves 53 Hz and the comb 1.0 dB. At the top the even harmonics are gone exactly, not merely quiet. Loudness 0.01 dB.

full.gloss: broad and full, every harmonic present

tine.gloss: the classic tine electric piano body

reed.gloss: hollow and nasal, a reed rather than a tine

strike.note: how hard the hammer hits: how bright the body STARTS before it softens. This shapes the tone, not the volume -- a hard strike is brighter, not louder (measured: 252 Hz of colour, 4.5 dB of comb, 0.06 dB of loudness), and the colour movement inside the note more than doubles along it. A soft strike still starts brighter than it settles, and that floor is not cosmetic: with it at zero, a soft strike on a body with no metal in it (`ting` 0) has no colour movement left at all and three corners of the cube FAIL the movement gate.

soft.gloss: mellow and round from the first moment

hard.gloss: struck hard, bright and biting before it settles

techniques.code:
kting   = 0.55                              ; ting [0..1]: how much metal in the strike
khollow = 0.75                              ; hollowness [0..1]: every harmonic, or odd only
kstrike = 0.64                              ; strike [0..1]: how bright the body STARTS
kring   = 0.25                              ; ring [0..1]: how long the metal keeps ringing
ktngr   = 12.0 * exp(-3.784080 * kring)     ; 12/s at short, 4.66 at the default, 0.27 at long
kbdx0   = 1.302 + (0.6 + 3.5906 * kstrike) * (1 - min(knote / 1.6, 1)) ; strike -> mellow, then holds
ktng0   = (1.5 + 1.0 * kting) * exp(-knote * ktngr) ; the metal fades out of the tone, over `ring`
ktr0    limit 14.2, 1, sr * 0.45 / (kfreq * koct1) ; tine ratio, capped below Nyquist (see docstring: a cap, not a fix)
aevn0   foscili 0.12 * (1 - khollow), (kfreq * koct1), 1, 3, kbdx0, giSine ; body, even + odd harmonics
aodd0   foscili 0.30 - 0.12 * (1 - khollow), (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2, kbdx0, giSine ; body, odd harmonics only
atin0   foscili 0.30 * kting ^ 0.65, (kfreq * koct1), 1, ktr0, ktng0, giSine ; the inharmonic ting
asum0   = aevn0 + aodd0 + atin0
aref0   poscil 0.5, (kfreq * koct1)
asig    balance asum0, aref0, 10 ; colour travels, loudness holds

techniques.why: drum head / tom / timpani / taiko / conga / djembe: a stretched membrane resonating, whose partials are NOT a harmonic series -- that is what makes a drum a drum; pitched = indefinite tom to definite kettledrum, spot = struck in the centre or at the rim, tension = slack and dull to tight and bright, damping = ringing open or muffled to a thud

pitched.note: how definite the pitch is. an ideal stretched membrane rings at spacings that are not whole-number multiples, so it has no clear note -- that is a tom. loading the head with air in a kettle pulls those spacings towards whole numbers until a real pitch appears -- that is a timpani. this is the deepest thing about the instrument, not a tuning offset: the played pitch itself never changes here, only whether the drum sounds like it HAS one.

tom.gloss: no clear note, just a low woody thump

mixed.gloss: a note starts to emerge from the thump

timpani.gloss: a real singing pitch, a tuned kettledrum

strikepos.note: where the head is struck. dead centre wakes only the modes that breathe evenly across the whole skin, which is round and deep; nearer the rim wakes the ones that ripple around it, which is thinner, harder and more sharply coloured. a real player uses this constantly.

tension.note: how tightly the head is stretched, heard as which partials carry the sound rather than as pitch. slack leaves only the lowest ones and sounds dull and floppy; tight brings the upper ones up and sounds bright and taut.

damping.note: how freely the head is allowed to ring, as with a hand or a felt ring on the skin. open leaves narrow clear resonances that sing; muffled broadens them until the drum reads as a thud with a colour rather than a tone.

muffled.gloss: dead and thuddy, a cloth on the skin

techniques.code:
; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE
; A noise-rung resonator bank, not a sustained tone with a rate.
; Eight membrane modes under a continuous noise exciter -- the worst reading in
; the library (72 failing anchor-register pairs), and every one of them fails on
; COHERENCE rather than on span: `pitched=timpani` travels 1753 cents at 55 Hz,
; 29x the gate. Declared by BJ 2026-07-25 for this family.
aexq0   rand 0.07, 0.5, 1          ; continuous exciter -- the skin is driven, a held note stands (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
kpitch  = 0.25   ; pitched [0..1]: a tom with no note, to a tuned kettledrum
kpos    = 0.35   ; strikepos [0..1]: dead centre, to close to the rim
ktens   = 0.5    ; tension [0..1]: slack and dull, to taut and bright
kdamp   = 0.35   ; damping [0..1]: ringing freely, to a cloth on the skin
; The head's modes are the ideal circular membrane's (Bessel zeros of (0,1),
; (1,1), (2,1), (0,2), (3,1), (1,2), (4,1), (2,2)) pulled towards whole-number
; spacings by `pitched` -- that is what a kettle of air under the skin does, and
; it is the difference between a tom and a timpani, not a tuning offset.
ktilt   = 1.6 * (ktens - 0.5)       ; tension: a spectral tilt, flat at 0.5
kQ      = exp(1.05 - 3.0 * kdamp)   ; damping: 2.86x the Q wide open, 0.14x muffled
; `strikepos` is the real strike-point excitation |J_m(z*r)|: at the centre only
; the m=0 modes are awake (round and deep), and the ripple modes come up as the
; strike moves out. Two straight segments through the physical values at r=0.02,
; 0.35 and 0.70 -- the head is clamped at the rim, where every mode is zero, so
; the axis stops at 0.70 where a player actually strikes.
k0qr0   = 1.0000      ; mode 1, (0,1)
k0qw0   = kpos < 0.35 ? 1.203 + (kpos / 0.35) * -0.203 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * -0.509
k0qf0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr0, 20, 15000
k0qg0   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr0 < 15000 ? (0.0710 +0.0940 * kpitch -0.0320 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw0 * (k0qr0 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q0   mode aexq0, k0qf0, 20.0 * kQ
k0qr1   = (1.5940 + -0.0940 * kpitch)      ; mode 2, (1,1)
k0qw1   = kpos < 0.35 ? 0.072 + (kpos / 0.35) * +0.928 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * -0.158
k0qf1   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr1, 20, 15000
k0qg1   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr1 < 15000 ? (0.1010 -0.0100 * kpitch -0.0080 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw1 * (k0qr1 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q1   mode aexq0, k0qf1, 18.1 * kQ
k0qr2   = (2.1360 + -0.1460 * kpitch)      ; mode 3, (2,1)
k0qw2   = kpos < 0.35 ? 0.004 + (kpos / 0.35) * +0.996 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * +0.458
k0qf2   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr2, 20, 15000
k0qg2   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr2 < 15000 ? (0.0850 -0.0090 * kpitch -0.0060 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw2 * (k0qr2 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q2   mode aexq0, k0qf2, 16.2 * kQ
k0qr3   = (2.2960 + +0.1440 * kpitch)      ; mode 4, (0,2)
k0qw3   = kpos < 0.35 ? 3.788 + (kpos / 0.35) * -2.788 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * +0.529
k0qf3   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr3, 20, 15000
k0qg3   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr3 < 15000 ? (0.0880 -0.0180 * kpitch -0.0040 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw3 * (k0qr3 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q3   mode aexq0, k0qf3, 14.4 * kQ
k0qr4   = (2.6530 + +0.2370 * kpitch)      ; mode 5, (3,1)
k0qw4   = kpos < 0.35 ? 0.000 + (kpos / 0.35) * +1.000 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * +1.539
k0qf4   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr4, 20, 15000
k0qg4   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr4 < 15000 ? (0.0810 -0.0090 * kpitch -0.0060 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw4 * (k0qr4 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q4   mode aexq0, k0qf4, 12.5 * kQ
k0qr5   = (2.9180 + +0.4120 * kpitch)      ; mode 6, (1,2)
k0qw5   = kpos < 0.35 ? 0.138 + (kpos / 0.35) * +0.862 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * -0.377
k0qf5   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr5, 20, 15000
k0qg5   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr5 < 15000 ? (0.0830 -0.0090 * kpitch -0.0060 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw5 * (k0qr5 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q5   mode aexq0, k0qf5, 10.7 * kQ
k0qr6   = (3.1560 + +0.6140 * kpitch)      ; mode 7, (4,1)
k0qw6   = kpos < 0.35 ? 0.000 + (kpos / 0.35) * +1.000 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * +3.438
k0qf6   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr6, 20, 15000
k0qg6   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr6 < 15000 ? (0.0870 -0.0120 * kpitch -0.0040 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw6 * (k0qr6 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q6   mode aexq0, k0qf6, 8.8 * kQ
k0qr7   = (3.5010 + +0.7090 * kpitch)      ; mode 8, (2,2)
k0qw7   = kpos < 0.35 ? 0.007 + (kpos / 0.35) * +0.993 : 1.000 + ((kpos - 0.35) / 0.65) * -0.546
k0qf7   limit (kfreq * koct1) * k0qr7, 20, 15000
k0qg7   = ((kfreq * koct1) * k0qr7 < 15000 ? (0.0910 -0.0110 * kpitch -0.0060 * kpitch * kpitch) * k0qw7 * (k0qr7 ^ ktilt) : 0)
a0q7   mode aexq0, k0qf7, 7.0 * kQ
kmuf    = limit((kdamp - 0.35) / 0.65, 0, 1)   ; a cloth is a lowpass, and only above the default
amix0   = (a0q0 * k0qg0 + a0q1 * k0qg1 + a0q2 * k0qg2 + a0q3 * k0qg3 + a0q4 * k0qg4 + a0q5 * k0qg5 + a0q6 * k0qg6 + a0q7 * k0qg7) * 3.500
; The keyboard is not a volume control, and a `mode` bank on flat noise is one by
; default: measured, a single `mode` falls -2.91 dB/octave at Q 20 and -1.72 at
; Q 900, so a bank with mixed Qs has no one exponent that levels it and levelling
; at a single pitch left 9.0 dB of tilt over 110-880 Hz. `balance` needs no law.
; It is safe here because this body STANDS rather than decays -- on a real decay
; envelope a slow follower would flatten the decay itself. It also holds all four
; axes to one loudness, which is what a colour control has to be.
amufd   tone amix0, 2.5 * (kfreq * koct1)
amix    = amix0 * (1 - kmuf) + amufd * kmuf
aref    poscil 0.3203, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: gong / tam-tam / anvil / singing bowl / metallic percussion: true inharmonic metal partials (h 1.73/3.19/4.51) written as 2-operator FM at a 2.41 ratio

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

techniques.code:
kindex  = 0.533333                ; index [0..1]: how many sidebands -- how bright
kring   = 0.555556                ; ring [0..1]: how long the bright attack rings
kdetune = 0.650000                ; detune [0..1]: the doublet's offset, in Hz
ktm0    init 0
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  ktm0   = 0
endif
ktm0    = ktm0 + 1/kr           ; seconds since this strike
kbmx0   limit (sr * 0.45 / (kfreq * koct1) - 1) / 2.41 - 1, 0, 40 ; sideband room
kbtp0   min 1.0 + 15.0 * kindex, kbmx0   ; brightest the band allows
kbnx0   = kbtp0 * (0.3333 + 0.6667 * (1 - min(ktm0 / (0.5 + 4.5 * kring), 1))) ; darkens as it rings
abl0    foscili 0.37, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2.41, kbnx0, giSine ; the bell
abt0    foscili 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) + 2.0 * kdetune, 1, 2.41, kbnx0 * 0.94, giSine ; its doublet
abs0    = abl0 + abt0       ; the pair beats
abr0    poscil 0.44, (kfreq * koct1)        ; steady level reference
asig    balance abs0, abr0, 1 ; loudness held, beat kept

techniques.why: tuned struck metal bar -- glockenspiel / music box / celesta / kalimba: ideal free-free bar partials (h 2.76/5.4/8.93/13.34), brighter and thinner than a big bell, rung by a continuous noise exciter through a bank of high-Q resonators Two axes: `strike` is how far from the middle it is hit, which is the single biggest thing about a struck bar (centroid 641 -> 1789 Hz), and `ring` is how long it is left to sound (T60 2.15 s to 36 s).
techniques.code:
; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE
; A noise-rung resonator bank, not a sustained tone with a rate.
; The bar's five Q-900+ modes are rung by continuous noise, so the colour's
; travel is the exciter's dither and has no rate. Declared by BJ 2026-07-25 for
; this family. Note this is NOT a statement about pitch: the bar keeps its mode
; on the played note, because a glockenspiel has a definite pitch.
kstrike = 0.45     ; strike [0..1]: how far from the middle of the bar it is struck
kring   = 0.50     ; ring [0..1]: how long the metal is left to ring
aexq0   rand 0.06, 0.5, 1          ; continuous exciter -> the metal is driven, a held note stands (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
; `strike` re-tilts the mode gains geometrically and `ring` scales every Q. Both are
; exactly 1 at their defaults, so this entry still renders the sound it shipped with.
; The trailing `balance` is what makes both of them colour and not level: it holds the
; RMS against a fixed reference whatever the modes do, at every register.
kstk    = 0.55 + 1.00 * kstrike               ; 0.55 (the middle) .. 1.55 (the edge)
krng    = 4.0 ^ (2 * kring - 1)               ; a quarter of the Q .. four times it
k0qf0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000, 20, 15000
k0qg0   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 < 15000 ? 0.850 : 0)
a0q0   mode aexq0, k0qf0, 900 * krng      ; mode 1 @ x1.00, Q 900, Q x krng
k0qf1   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 2.7600, 20, 15000
k0qg1   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 2.7600 < 15000 ? 0.700 * kstk : 0)
a0q1   mode aexq0, k0qf1, 1025 * krng      ; mode 2 @ x2.76, Q 1025, Q x krng
k0qf2   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 5.4000, 20, 15000
k0qg2   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 5.4000 < 15000 ? 0.500 * kstk ^ 2 : 0)
a0q2   mode aexq0, k0qf2, 1150 * krng      ; mode 3 @ x5.40, Q 1150, Q x krng
k0qf3   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 8.9300, 20, 15000
k0qg3   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 8.9300 < 15000 ? 0.320 * kstk ^ 3 : 0)
a0q3   mode aexq0, k0qf3, 1275 * krng      ; mode 4 @ x8.93, Q 1275, Q x krng
k0qf4   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 13.3400, 20, 15000
k0qg4   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 13.3400 < 15000 ? 0.180 * kstk ^ 4 : 0)
a0q4   mode aexq0, k0qf4, 1400 * krng      ; mode 5 @ x13.34, Q 1400, Q x krng
amix    = (a0q0 * k0qg0 + a0q1 * k0qg1 + a0q2 * k0qg2 + a0q3 * k0qg3 + a0q4 * k0qg4) * 0.150
; The keyboard is not a volume control, and a `mode` bank on flat noise is one by
; default: measured, a single `mode` falls -2.91 dB/octave at Q 20 and -1.72 at
; Q 900, so a bank with mixed Qs has no one exponent that levels it and levelling
; at a single pitch left 5.2 dB of tilt over 110-880 Hz. `balance` needs no law.
; It is safe here because this body STANDS rather than decays -- on a real decay
; envelope a slow follower would flatten the decay itself. The reference holds
; this entry's own 220 Hz level, so nothing but the tilt changes.
aref    poscil 0.3986, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

strike.note: how far from the middle of the bar it is struck. Where a bar is hit decides which modes take energy: at the middle the fundamental dominates and the high modes are nearly absent, toward the end they carry it. This re-tilts the mode gains geometrically, gain_n * r^(n-1), which is the dominant term of that and needs no invented mode-shape formula -- and the shipped gains are ALREADY such a tilt (0.850 0.700 0.500 0.320 0.180), so the axis moves the one number the template already chose. Centroid 641 -> 1789 Hz and motion 361 -> 1499, at 0.26 dB of loudness. This is the axis to reach for on this entry: a music box struck at the middle and a glockenspiel struck near the end are the same bar.

at the middle.gloss: almost only the fundamental: round and soft

off centre.gloss: a little of the upper metal

near the end.gloss: the high modes carrying it: hard and bright

damped.gloss: a felt on the bar: short and dry

left open.gloss: held as long as you want it

ring.note: how long the metal is left to ring -- a quarter of every mode's Q at one end and four times it at the other. A mode's ring time is Q/(pi*f), so this IS the decay: gated off and measured without `balance` in the way, T60 follows Q/(pi*f)*ln(1000) to a tenth of a second (2.15 s at a quarter of the Q, 4.39 at half, and past 36 s at four times). Its mark is the COMB and not the centroid -- 16.5 -> 35.5 dB, because a narrower resonance lets less of the exciter's noise through and the modes speak more purely, while the centroid moves 90 Hz. The trailing `balance` is why this is colour and not level: it holds the RMS against a fixed reference whatever the Qs do, at every register. Do NOT read `sustain` as the ring time here -- it FALLS as Q rises (0.870 -> 0.721 on the bar), which is `balance` over-boosting a high-Q body's slow build-up and not the decay getting shorter.

techniques.why: cymbal / crash / ride / hi-hat / splash: a struck metal plate -- a dense bank of high-Q resonators, all off the harmonic grid, rung by a noise exciter. There is NO mode on the note played, because a cymbal has no definite pitch: it is tuned by its diameter and its thickness, so it follows the keyboard (a small splash rings higher than a big crash) without ever sounding a fundamental. The eight partials sit at x2.6081 2.8627 3.5167 5.4061 7.4448 8.1893 9.434 14.069 of the note. For metal that IS pitched -- glockenspiel, celesta, music box -- use `struck_bar`, and for a pitched glass bell `glass`. Two axes: `strike` runs from the bell to the edge and is the strongest control here, and `ring` runs from a choked splash to a full open wash.

krng    = 4.0 ^ (2 * kring - 1)               ; a quarter of the Q .. four times it

techniques.why: ring modulation / AM at a 2:1 ratio -- carrier f times modulator 2f, so sum and difference land on f and 3f: a hollow ODD-harmonic tone (square-adjacent), with a drifting diode imbalance and carrier leak for the metallic edge
techniques.code:
kleak   = 0.10   ; leak [0.0..1.0]: carrier survival -- 0 is pure ring modulation, the top is closer to plain AM
  kratio  = 2.0    ; ratio [1.0..4.0]: the modulator's ratio to the carrier
  krmw0   poscil 0.004, 0.091          ; modulator drift, ~7 cents
  krlk0   poscil 0.03, 0.037           ; diode imbalance, drifting
  acar0   poscil 0.8, (kfreq * koct1)
  amod0   poscil 1.0, (kfreq * koct1) * (kratio + krmw0)
  ; leak raises the average level of the (amod0*0.88 + leak) term substantially
  ; as it grows -- undo it with a measured cubic fit of the excess (max
  ; residual 0.05 db against the real render), zeroed exactly at the default
  kleakexc = -4.883057018950165*kleak^3 + 9.486347806338067*kleak^2 + 1.0273443131386866*kleak - 0.19271485235829916
  kleakcomp = 10 ^ (-kleakexc / 20)
  asig    = kleakcomp * acar0 * (amod0 * 0.88 + kleak + krlk0) ; ring mod + carrier leak

leak.note: how much of the unmodulated carrier survives under the ring-modulated product: at 0 the output holds no carrier frequency at all, only the sum and difference tones (the pure ring); raising it lets the carrier itself back through and the sound moves toward plain am, with the original pitch audible again under the metallic product. today's 0.10 is a trace of carrier. brightness FALLS as the carrier comes back, because the carrier sits below its own sidebands: at 220 hz the centroid runs 439 -> 427 -> 332 hz over the three anchors (110 hz: 221 -> 215 -> 167; 440 hz: 878 -> 838 -> 654; 880 hz: 1752 -> 1680 -> 1339), and the power-weighted reading agrees (441 -> 437 -> 283 at 220 hz). comb contrast moves 4.5 db. uncompensated the axis raises level by up to 5.5 db; a cubic fit of the excess (max residual 0.05 db) zeroed at the shipped default holds it flat: loudness spread measured 0.20/0.05/0.11/0.09/0.07 db at 110/220/440/880/1760 hz. AT 55 HZ IT DOES NOT, AND THAT IS THE ENTRY'S OWN BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN THIS AXIS'S. the anchors read 2.06 db apart in a 3 s note there, but the number is not a function of leak -- it is the phase of a beat at note-on. the modulator carries a free-running ~7-cent drift (krmw0, 0.091 hz, an 11 s period) and the default ratio is exactly 2, so carrier and modulator sit at a near-lock that the drift beats against with a period comparable to a note. holding leak fixed and moving ONLY the preroll (how long the plugin has been open before the note -- an unbounded quantity no (leak, frequency) fit can see) the spread runs 0.80-2.28 db and THE LOUDEST ANCHOR CHANGES PLACES: `pure` is loudest at preroll 0-1 s, `ring and carrier together` at 2-5 s. it DOES average out, and an earlier version of this note said the opposite on a measurement that could not see it: `lco_measure.rms_db` has a hard-coded window of t0=0.5 to t1=3.5 s, so measuring a 12, 30 or 60 s render returns the same first three seconds every time and the three readings agreeing looked like convergence. integrating the whole note instead: 0.06 db over 12 s and 0.08 db over 30 s, against 2.06 db over 3 s. so the long-run energy of the three anchors is equal to a tenth of a decibel and only a note of a few seconds samples a phase of the beat. the shipped DEFAULT body alone -- bit-identical to what ships today -- swings 1.76 db at 55 hz across those same prerolls within a 3 s window, which is what settles whose behaviour it is. left uncompensated, exactly as `supersaw.spread` already leaves its own near-unison beat-phase band. two fixes were tried and rejected: a register-dependent gain law cannot see the driving variable, and keying the drift to note-onset neither removed the effect reliably (1.0-2.4 db across prerolls) nor kept the default bit-identical (max sample difference 0.76-1.4). anything that does remove it changes ring_mod's own 55 hz sound and is a change of the instrument, not a compensation.

pure.gloss: pure ring modulation -- centroid 439 hz at a played 220

default.gloss: today's slight leak -- centroid 427 hz at a played 220

ring and carrier together.gloss: carrier-dominant, closer to am -- centroid 332 hz at a played 220

ratio.note: the modulator's frequency ratio to the carrier (today 2:1). confirmed keyboard-tracking with lco_measure.tracks() at 110 vs 880 hz (three octaves): r_note 0.91-1.00 against r_fixed near zero at every tested ratio and leak combination -- the verdict is 'tracks' throughout, i.e. the sum/difference spectrum moves with the note rather than sitting at a fixed register. centroid at 220 hz runs 225->427->610->807 hz across ratio 1.0/2.0/3.0/4.0 (roughly proportional; 103->403 at 110, 442->1617 at 440, 883->3272 at 880). loudness is essentially untouched by ratio alone: spread measured 0.03-0.09 db, no compensation needed.

unison.gloss: modulator equals carrier -- centroid 225 hz at a played 220

default.gloss: today's octave-like 2:1 -- centroid 427 hz at a played 220

drive.note: how far up the chebyshev transfer curve the carrier drives, as the carrier's own base amplitude. 0.30 is both today's value and this axis's own top: it is pinned there because 0.30 plus wander's default drift (0.17) already reaches 0.47, the safe margin below the +-0.5 input range the table read clamps at -- there is no room to push the base level any higher without wander also giving up some of its own range. pushing the curve harder changes the shaper's own output gain, and so does wander's own drift, and the two are NOT independent: the drift's own excursion changes the peak the carrier reaches, so the gain law measured at wander=1 is a different curve from the one at wander=0. two single-variable fits multiplied together (kdcomp*kwcomp) were only exact on the cross through each one's own reference point, and disagreed with the measured gain by 3.58 db at the corner where both axes are away from their reference (drive low, wander low) -- a hard fail of the one-loudness rule. kcomp is now one joint fit in (drive-0.30) and (wander-1.0) together, degree 2 in each plus their cross terms, with no constant term so it is exactly zero at the declared defaults (today's sound is unchanged, bit-identical at 110/220/440 hz). with it in place the joint spread across every drive x wander corner is 0.29-0.30 db at every register from 55 to 3520 hz, against a flat 3.57-3.58 db before, at every register. centroid at 220 hz runs 363 -> 575 hz, and the 3rd harmonic strengthens from -10.6 to -6.5 db relative to the strongest partial as the curve folds harder.

clean.gloss: a light shaping, close to the plain tone

mid.gloss: a clear edge, the odd harmonics audible

hot.gloss: today's drive, the curve folding hard

wander.note: the depth of the two drift lfos that wander the drive up and down, together, keeping their 0.12:0.05 ratio. 0 silences both -- a static curve, nothing moving in the note at all -- and 1 is today's own depth, which is also this axis's own top for the same safety reason drive's top is pinned: drive's default plus more drift than today would pass the table's safe input margin. widening the swing changes the shaper's output gain on a smaller scale, but not independently of drive: the two interact (see drive's note) and a product of separate fits disagreed with the measured gain by 3.58 db at the corner where both are away from their reference. the same joint fit (kcomp, zero at the declared defaults) now holds the combined spread to 0.29-0.30 db at every register from 55 to 3520 hz, against 3.57-3.58 db before. at 0 the entry does not move at all (motion 0 hz, coherence 0 at every register) -- these two lfos are this body's only source of movement, so silencing them silences the movement too, exactly as the axis's own bottom implies; this is the anchor named 'static' doing what it is named for, not a defect. away from 0 it moves clearly (coherence 1.00); centroid at 220 hz runs 492 -> 575 hz between the middle and top of the range.

static.gloss: a fixed curve, no drift at all

breathing.gloss: today's own drift, the fullest this body allows

techniques.why: pipe / drawbar organ -- hammond, tonewheel, church organ: three ranks at typical registration, an 8' principal, a 4' octave and a 5 1/3' quint, each its own gbuzz stack, each drifting at its own rate
techniques.code:
kregist = 0.5                               ; regist [0..1]: principal alone, or the full mix
kw80    poscil 0.00035, 0.061        ; rank 8' tuning wander
kw40    poscil 0.00045, 0.083        ; rank 4', incommensurate
kwq0    poscil 0.00030, 0.107        ; quint rank, incommensurate
; Drawing more stops on a real organ makes it LOUDER, and on this platform a
; parameter may not move the loudness. So the registration is power-preserving by
; construction: the upper ranks come up while the principal comes down, holding
; 0.46^2 + 0.24^2 + 0.16^2 constant. At 0.5 all three amplitudes are exactly the
; shipped ones. `max` under the root, because an out-of-range value would otherwise
; ask for the square root of a negative number.
kg40    = 0.24 * (0.30 + 1.40 * kregist)
kgq0    = 0.16 * (0.30 + 1.40 * kregist)
kg80    = sqrt(max(0.2948 - kg40 * kg40 - kgq0 * kgq0, 0.0025))
a80     gbuzz kg80, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kw80), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 8' principal
a40     gbuzz kg40, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0023 * (1 + kw40), 4, 1, 0.66, giCos ; 4' octave, +4 cents
aq0     gbuzz kgq0, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.4987 * (1 + kwq0), 3, 1, 0.60, giCos ; 5 1/3' quint, -1.5 cents
amix    = a80 + a40 + aq0
; `balance` and not a hand-computed normalisation, because this axis moves the
; SPECTRUM by moving a modulation index, and both `gbuzz` and `foscili` change their
; total energy when their index changes: unbalanced, the axis measured as a fader
; (3.5 dB on the reed, 1.6 on the flute, 3.6 on the brass, 1.4 on the organ) and the
; loudness also drifted WITHIN the note as the internal pressure cycle breathed. The
; reference amplitude is chosen to hold this entry's own shipped level to the
; hundredth of a dB, so the balance removes the travel and changes nothing else.
aref    poscil 0.2624, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

regist.note: the registration: the 8' principal alone, or the 4' octave and 5 1/3' quint drawn with it. Its mark is not the centroid and not the comb either, but WHICH NOTE THE PIPES ADD UP TO. The 5 1/3' quint sounds a fifth above the 8', and 220 and 330 Hz have no common fundamental higher than 110 -- so drawing it drops the sounding fundamental by an octave without any pipe playing that note. That is the resultant tone organ builders have used for centuries to fake a 16' rank, and it is measurable: f0 reads 220.1 with the principal alone and 110.1 as soon as the quint is in. On the series the pipes actually make, the comb is 24.6 dB at the 8' alone and 67.5 to 69.6 dB with the upper ranks -- deeper, not shallower, because 220 and 330 are both harmonics of 110 and the odd places between them are empty. Odd/even goes +2.8 -> -7.0 dB, which is the same fact from the other side: the quint is not a harmonic of the 8'. Centroid only 620 -> 734 Hz. Drawing stops on a real organ makes it LOUDER and on this platform a parameter may not, so the rank amplitudes are redistributed power-preservingly before `balance` sees them, and the measured loudness is 0.02 dB. the upper ranks keep a 30 % floor at kregist=0 and that floor is load-bearing, not an oversight: zeroing them (the one quadratic through (0,0), (0.5,1), (1,1.7), which keeps the default and the full registration bit-identical) makes `principal` a single rank whose only motion is its own 0.061 hz tuning wander -- measured moves=False at coherence 0.00, against True at 1.00 today, because what moves this entry is three incommensurate wanders (0.061 / 0.083 / 0.107 hz) beating against each other. so a truthful `principal` and movement-by-default cannot both hold in this body as written; the gloss was corrected rather than the code. loudness is unaffected either way (0.003-0.112 db over the continuum).

principal.gloss: the 8' well out in front, the octave and quint pushed back to 30 % -- comb contrast 24.3 dB against 67.3 at plenum

mixture.gloss: everything drawn -- the quint singing over it

techniques.why: clarinet / chalumeau / bass clarinet -- a cylindrical reed: odd-only series (square-family) is the textbook cylindrical-reed approximation, hollow and woody
techniques.code:
kbreath = 0.5                               ; breath [0..1]: how hard the reed is driven
kbrc0   poscil 0.5, 0.19             ; breath pressure, slow
kndmx0  limit (sr * 0.45 / (kfreq * koct1) - 1) / 2 - 1, 0, 40 ; sideband room
kntp0   min 1.425, kndmx0        ; brightest the band allows

; 0.5 reproduces the shipped 0.807 coefficient exactly, i.e. the entry sounds

breath.note: how hard the reed is driven, as the FM index the slow pressure cycle then rides on. Its objective mark is what does NOT change: odd/even stays +101 to +105 dB across the whole axis, so the cylindrical bore -- the entry's whole signature -- survives every setting, and the series reaches from four audible partials to five. Centroid 549 -> 628 Hz, comb 0.6 dB. The colour movement in the note runs the other way, 305 -> 143 Hz: a softly-blown reed is where the breath cycle has the most room to move the tone, and a reed driven hard is already open and has less left to open. Loudness 0.07 dB, held by `balance` -- unbalanced this axis moved 3.52 dB.

breath.note: how hard the air column is blown, as the roll-off of the blown stack. The signature here is the opposite of the clarinet's and that is the point of having both: odd/even FALLS +13.4 -> +8.1 dB, because blowing an open column harder brings its even harmonics up, where a cylinder's reed keeps suppressing them. Centroid 280 -> 334 Hz and the colour movement in the note more than doubles, 27 -> 65 Hz. Comb 0.2 dB, loudness 0.01 dB.

techniques.why: bowed string SECTION -- orchestral strings, a string ensemble, massed players (a single bowed instrument is `string`): three players sounding together, each with its own slow intonation drift and its own bow-pressure cycle, detuned against each other; a bright saw-family spectrum with a gentle harmonic-count breathing
mandatory_flags: ensemble/detune is a voice-level effect, not a cycle property
techniques.code:
kdesk   = 1.0   ; desk [0..2]: ensemble width -- 0 collapses the three players to one voice, 2 a wide, beating section
kbow    = 0.62  ; bow [0.02..0.62]: how hard the bow is pressed -- soft, dark, flautando .. hard, bright, rosiny
kdd0    = kdesk - 1                                   ; desk deviation from the default spread
kdrf0   = log2((kfreq * koct1) / 220)                 ; register, in octaves from 220 hz
kdrf    = limit(kdrf0, -1, 2)                         ; clamp to the fitted 110-880 hz span, UNCHANGED
kdtap   = limit(1 - abs(kdrf0 - kdrf), 0, 1)          ; fade to no correction one octave beyond it, UNCHANGED
kdc1r   = -2.1395 + 0.1865 * kdrf + 0.2575 * kdrf * kdrf
kdc2r   = 2.1165 - 0.6355 * kdrf - 0.0325 * kdrf * kdrf
kdrf2   = limit(kdrf0, -3, -2)                        ; second, narrow register clamp: 27.5-55 hz only
kdtap2  = limit(1 - abs(kdrf0 - kdrf2), 0, 1)         ; fades to exactly 0 by 110 hz above, 13.75 hz below -- never touches the span kdtap already covers
kdshp0  = 0.8685 * kdd0 - 1.3077 * kdd0 * kdd0 - 2.1934 * kdd0 * kdd0 * kdd0 + 2.7177 * kdd0 * kdd0 * kdd0 * kdd0  ; near-unison shape in kdd0, register-invariant, measured at 55 hz
kgdb0   = kdtap * (kdc1r * kdd0 + kdc2r * kdd0 * kdd0) + kdtap2 * 1.40 * kdshp0 ; OLD 110-880 hz term (byte-identical) + NEW 55-hz-only term, calibrated at playing length (1-11 s), never exceeding the shipped body's own spread at any tested (dur,preroll)
kgds0   = 10 ^ (-kgdb0 / 20)                          ; compensating gain, exactly 1 at kdesk=1
krm0    = sr * 0.47 / (kfreq * koct1)        ; harmonics that fit
kctr0   limit krm0 * kbow, 1.6, 7 ; corner centre, capped
kc0     = kctr0 - 7                                   ; bow's corner, relative to the clamp ceiling (today's default, at every register)
kgbb0   = -0.1538 * kc0 + -0.0868 * kc0 * kc0        ; measured RMS excess this corner shift causes, fit in dB (register-invariant in kctr0)
kgbw0   = 10 ^ (-kgbb0 / 20)                          ; compensating gain, exactly 1 at the clamp ceiling
ksd0x0  poscil 0.0009, 0.061         ; player 1 intonation
ksb0x0  poscil 0.35, 0.089           ; player 1 bow pressure
asr0x0  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 * (1 + ksd0x0), 0
kbc0x0  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x0), 50, sr * 0.47 ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x0  tone asr0x0, kbc0x0
ksd0x1  poscil 0.0009, 0.073         ; player 2 intonation
ksb0x1  poscil 0.35, 0.107           ; player 2 bow pressure
asr0x1  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0000 + kdesk * 0.0042) * (1 + ksd0x1), 0
kbc0x1  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x1), 50, sr * 0.47 ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x1  tone asr0x1, kbc0x1
ksd0x2  poscil 0.0009, 0.047         ; player 3 intonation
ksb0x2  poscil 0.35, 0.127           ; player 3 bow pressure
asr0x2  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0000 - kdesk * 0.0042) * (1 + ksd0x2), 0
kbc0x2  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x2), 50, sr * 0.47 ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x2  tone asr0x2, kbc0x2
aens0   = ase0x0 + ase0x1 + ase0x2 ; the desk

desk.note: scales the two off-unison detunings (the vco2 centre-frequency multipliers 1.0042/0.9958 at kdesk=1) away from unison -- at 0 the three players collapse onto exactly one pitch (a solo instrument; three phase-locked voices summing coherently read as louder, and identically so at every register), at 2 they fan out to a wide, audibly beating section. measured beat rate/depth at 220 hz: 0.8 hz / 0.010 (desk=0) -> 0.8 hz / 0.462 (desk=1) -> 2.0 hz / 0.493 (desk=2). the loudness correction is in two independent register bands. 110-880 hz: the kdrf/kdtap/kdc1r/kdc2r term, fit at 220 hz and interpolated in log2 octaves, holding 0.11/0.34/0.34/0.12 db at 110/220/440/880 hz at the default note. 55 hz and below: a second, additive term (kdrf2/kdtap2/kdshp0), exactly zero at 110 hz and above by construction and verified bit-identical there, correcting only the coherent-unison excess -- which at that register is the whole effect (desk=0 is the loudest anchor at every duration and every plugin uptime tested). it removes 2.2-3.8 db across 20.6-73.4 hz and adds nothing anywhere. what it does NOT fix, with numbers: at 55 hz the residual is 4.1/1.7/4.3/1.7 db at a 3 s note (down from 7.9/4.9/8.1/3.7), and 0.1-1.3 db at an 11 s note. what is left is beat PHASE, not level: at 55 hz a three-voice detune beats slower than the note is long, so the note's integral depends on where in the beat cycle it started, and no gain curve in kdesk can reach that. the same variance is what makes 110-880 hz unfittable beyond what is already there. none of the correction terms reference sr; the raw excess this fit targets moves under 0.004 db between 44.1 and 96 khz.

solo.gloss: collapsed to one player -- louder, coherent, no beating

bow.note: moves the 0.62 constant that sets how many harmonics fit under the bow-pressure tone-filter corner (kctr0 = limit(krm0 * kbow, 1.6, 7), krm0 = harmonics that fit at this register) -- down is a softer, darker, flautando bow; up (0.62) is today's default hard, bright, rosiny attack. untouched by the desk fix above -- the compensation is fit against kctr0 itself (the clamped, register-normalised corner variable), not the raw axis value, which is why it already held across every register. measured spread 0.28 db at 220 hz and 0.01/0.15/0.17/0.03 db at 110/440/880/1760 hz. measured centroid at each register (bow 0.02 -> 0.62): 110 hz 1105.7 -> 1512.6 hz (using the shared body's own numbers; unaffected by the desk change since desk sits at its default, kdd0=0, while this axis sweeps); 220 hz 1337.6 -> 2418.2 hz; 440 hz 2181.2 -> 3837.0 hz; 880 hz 3871.1 -> 5865.7 hz; 1760 hz 5861.1 -> 7636.3 hz.

techniques.why: plucked or bowed string / guitar / harp / koto / pizzicato / violin / cello: ONE real string, set going and then left to ring -- NOT the ensemble string machine (that is `strings`, detuned saws) and NOT the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (that is `harpsichord`, gbuzz choirs). The string is a comb resonator tuned to the played pitch. It has to be fed the whole time so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking -- but the feed arrives as scattered, time-smeared touches and the ring is kept long, so what is heard is the string and not what is driving it. A continuous wall of noise into the same resonator is audibly an electric string driver: aggressive and restless. Its top dies away after the attack the way a real string loses its brilliance -- twice over, fast for the first instant and slowly for the whole ring. bow = plucked with a pick to drawn with a bow, pick = where the string is set going, from right at the bridge to at the middle, damp = left ringing to stopped under the hand
techniques.code:
kbow    = 0.35                                 ; bow [0..1]: touches, or a steady draw
kpick   = 0.3                                  ; pick [0..1]: where along the string
kdamp   = 0.35                                 ; damp [0..1]: how freely it may ring
kstr    limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
kfast   = exp(-knote * 20.00)                  ; the first instant's brilliance goes at once
kslow   = exp(-knote * (0.455 - 0.364 * kbow))                  ; and the string keeps losing its top all the while
kbrth   poscil 0.220 + 0.380 * kbow, 0.230 + 0.620 * kbow                ; the hand behind it is never quite steady
kcut    limit (1050.0 * 0.42 ^ kbow) * (1 + (3.20 - 1.76 * kbow) * kfast) * (1 + (5.50 - 4.12 * kbow) * kslow) * (1 + kbrth), 60, 18000
aexd    dust 1.0, 300.0 * 13.0 ^ kbow                        ; the drive arrives as separate touches, not as
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.1100, 0.00710                ;   a wall of noise -- a wall is an electric
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0820, 0.00470                ;   string driver, not a played string. Each
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0640, 0.00310                ;   touch is then smeared out in time so none
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0480, 0.00190                ;   of them arrives as a click. Allpasses
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0340, 0.00113                ;   spread WITHOUT darkening; a lowpass here
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0260, 0.00079                ;   buries the instrument's own colour
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0200, 0.00053
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0160, 0.00037
aexb    tone aexd, kcut
apik    vdelay aexb, ((0.05 + 0.45 * kpick) / kstr) * 1000, 60
aexc    = aexb - apik
astr    streson aexc, kstr, 0.9960 - 0.0217 * kdamp
aref    poscil 0.35, 400                          ; a fixed-loudness yardstick: how scattered the
abal    balance astr, aref                        ; drive is must not change how loud the tone is
asig    = abal * 0.85

bow.note: how the string is set going, and that is the whole difference between a guitar and a cello. A pick or a fingernail lets go in an instant, so everything in the string is woken at once and the sound arrives bright and then falls away. A bow never lets go: the hair grabs and slips and grabs again, feeding the string the whole time, so the top is rubbed off but nothing dies -- the tone stands and breathes instead. In the code this is how DENSELY the drive arrives: separate touches at the plucked end, a steady draw at the bowed one. Measured across the axis the colour travels from 4812 Hz down to 3463 Hz while how sharply the string rings does not change (32.9 -> 34.1 dB) and the loudness moves 0.05 dB.

plucked.gloss: picked and let go: bright at the front, then darkening

bowed.gloss: drawn with a bow: standing, breathing, the top rubbed off

pick.note: where along its length the string is set going. This is not a tone control, it is geometry: a string cannot be given any energy at a harmonic whose still point falls exactly where you touch it, so that harmonic is simply missing. Right by the bridge the touch is at a twentieth of the length and only the very high ones are lost, so the sound is thin, hard and nasal; at the middle every even harmonic goes at once and the sound is hollow and woody, a clarinet made of string. Measured at the middle, harmonics 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 sit 37 to 43 dB below the fundamental -- 30 to 45 dB lower than the same harmonics played at the bridge -- which is the real thing and not an effect. It moves 333 Hz of colour and 0.00 dB of loudness.

bridge.gloss: played hard by the bridge: thin, wiry, nasal

middle.gloss: over the middle: hollow and woody, the even harmonics gone

damp.note: how freely the string is allowed to ring, as with the flat of the hand laid on it. Open, the resonances are narrow and the string sings a clear note; stopped, they broaden and the string reads as a knock with a colour rather than a pitch. It never stops ringing altogether -- a string whose resonance is let go stops sounding like a string at all and starts sounding like the thing driving it. Measured as how far the sound BETWEEN the harmonics sits below the harmonics themselves: 37.6 dB open, 29.7 dB stopped. The colour follows it a little (3972 -> 4314 Hz) because a broad resonance passes more of the drive's own top, and the loudness moves 0.02 dB.

open.gloss: left to ring, a clear singing note

damped.gloss: a hand resting on it, controlled

muted.gloss: palm-muted: a knock with a colour, barely a pitch

techniques.why: synth bass -- moog bass / tb-303 / acid bassline: a dark saw-family spectrum, harmonic count ceilinged near 24 for a rolled-off low end
techniques.code:
kbite   = 24     ; bite [6..40]: the lowpass ceiling, in harmonics of the note
ksub    = 1.0    ; sub [0..1]: 0 no sub-octave weight, 1 today's balance
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
abs0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 0 ; saw source
kcut0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * kbite, 100, 15000 ; bite: the lowpass ceiling
kbx0    = kbite - 24                        ; bite: compensation, zero at the default
kbcmp0  = 10 ^ (-(0.005761 * kbx0 - 0.0002906 * kbx0 * kbx0) / 20)
adk0    butterlp abs0, kcut0
ksx0    = 1 - ksub                          ; sub: compensation, zero at the default
kscmp0  = 10 ^ (-(-4.252645 * ksx0 + 1.816774 * ksx0 * ksx0) / 20)
asb0    oscili 0.30 * ksub, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.5    ; sub-octave weight
asig    = (adk0 * kbcmp0 * 0.72 + asb0) * kscmp0

bite.note: the lowpass ceiling above the saw source, in harmonics of the played note (not 0..1 -- a harmonic count). a first-order lowpass loses a little rms as its ceiling drops -- measured 0.20-0.25 db raw across the range at every register (110/220/440/880 hz), held to 0.09-0.13 db by a quadratic fit in bite-24 (coefficients 0.005761, -0.0002906) that is exactly zero at the default, so today's sound is unchanged. centroid runs 614 -> 2102 hz at 220 hz: low bite is a rounder, more sub-like saw, high bite lets more of the raw sawtooth's edge through. this entry does not clear the library's own movement threshold at 220 hz and up regardless of bite (bass_saw is one of the library's pre-existing static entries in that range, unrelated to this axis), so what moves here is colour, not a wobble.

dull.gloss: rounded off, almost a sub tone with a buzz on top

capped.gloss: the shipped acid-bass ceiling, rolled off early

open.gloss: more edge let through, still far short of a full saw

sub.note: the sub-octave sine's own weight against the filtered saw -- its oscili amplitude scales directly with this axis. held at one loudness by a second fit that boosts the saw back up as the sub is removed (quadratic in 1-sub, coefficients -4.252645, 1.816774, exactly zero at sub=1 so today's mix is unchanged): measured 2.41-2.44 db raw across 110/220/440/880 hz, held to 0.02-0.10 db. centroid falls 1899 -> 1532 hz at 220 hz as more sub-octave energy is added underneath. between 0 and 1 the sub sits close enough to the fundamental's own harmonics that it briefly reads as an amplitude beat rather than a smooth blend (0.209 depth at 109.95 hz measured at sub=0.25) -- real physics of adding a coherent low partial, not a fault, and gone by the anchors reported here.

none.gloss: just the filtered saw, boosted back to the same loudness

half.gloss: a little low-end fill under the saw

techniques.why: supersaw / hypersaw -- the trance and rave lead: a stack of seven saws detuned a few cents apart, and the beating between them IS the sound
mandatory_flags: detune/unison is a voice-level effect, not a cycle property
techniques.code:
kspread = 1.0    ; spread [0..2]: 0 unison, 1 today's stack, 2 wider than today
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kssx0   = kspread - 1                       ; spread: compensation, zero at the default
ksexc0  = 1.42845067 * kssx0 - 4.43651882 * kssx0 * kssx0 - 5.39442447 * kssx0 * kssx0 * kssx0 + 8.37724332 * kssx0 * kssx0 * kssx0 * kssx0
kscmp0  = 10 ^ (-ksexc0 / 20)                ; corrects the coherent-to-incoherent loudness jump
; the stack's own loudness also TILTS with register, and it is not a fixed property of the
; body: measured at the anchors it is 3.75 dB at 55 Hz for today's default (spread=1), only
; 0.4-0.9 dB at unison (0) and wide (2). kmu is the octave from 220 Hz, clamped to the
; 55-3520 Hz span this was measured over so a note off that span freezes at the boundary
; instead of exploding -- an unclamped exact fit through these same points reads a false
; -18 dB excess at 7040 Hz where the true reading is -1.3. krf forces the WHOLE correction
; to zero at kmu = -1, 0, +1 (110/220/440 Hz) for ANY spread; the subtraction below is
; what makes the default unchanged at the OTHER registers too. The rest is an exact fit to the measured excess at 55/880/1760/3520 Hz,
; at spread = 0/1/2 (the three anchors) -- 0 dB residual at those 12 points, and within
; 0.05-0.5 dB checked at off-grid registers inside the clamped span.
kmoct   = log2((kfreq * koct1) / 220)
; kmu's LOWER clamp is -1, and krf is exactly zero at kmu = -1, so the correction is
; switched off at and below 110 Hz. At 55 Hz what it was fitted to is not a function
; of (spread, register) at all: the closest detune pair at spread=1 is 0.19 Hz there,
; a 5.2 s beat, longer than a note, so a 3 s reading samples a phase. Measured over
; the anchors at 55 Hz, corrected, at prerolls 0.5/2.0/3.5/7.0 s: 0.10 / 3.24 / 5.06
; / 3.13 dB -- flat only at the one preroll it was fitted at, and 3.05-3.13 dB over a
; 12-30 s note against 0.74-0.90 uncorrected. Uncorrected it is inside the bound on
; any note longer than a few seconds; corrected it was not. Above 440 Hz the same
; beat is fast enough to average inside a note and the correction is a real gain law
; that holds at every preroll, which is why the upper end of the clamp stands.
kmu     limit kmoct, -1, 4
krf     = kmu * (kmu - 1) * (kmu + 1)
kregb   = -0.17541667 - 0.24600000*kmu + 0.17427083*kmu*kmu - 0.02568750*kmu*kmu*kmu
kregc   = 0.07841667 + 0.11952778*kmu - 0.08314583*kmu*kmu + 0.01220139*kmu*kmu*kmu
; the fit's own value AT THE DEFAULT is subtracted, so the correction is exactly
; zero at spread = 1 for EVERY register and only the differences between spreads
; are touched. Without that subtraction it also compensated the default's own
; register tilt, which is the entry's sound and not an excess: the default came
; out 3.75 dB louder at 55 Hz and 0.64/0.68 dB at 880/1760, invisible to a
; bit-identity check at 110/220/440 Hz because krf is structurally zero there.
kregexc = krf * kssx0 * (kregb + kregc * (kspread + 1))
kregcmp = 10 ^ (-kregexc / 20)
asu0x0  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * 0.0000) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x1  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * 0.0035) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x2  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * -0.0035) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x3  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * 0.0071) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x4  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * -0.0071) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x5  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * 0.0110) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asu0x6  vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kspread * -0.0110) * (1 + kvdr0), 0
asig    = (asu0x0 + asu0x1 + asu0x2 + asu0x3 + asu0x4 + asu0x5 + asu0x6) * 0.17 * kscmp0 * kregcmp   ; 7-saw detuned stack, spread- and register-loudness compensated

spread.note: scales all six detuning offsets together (the seventh voice stays centred); at 2 the outer voices sit twice as far out as today. at 0 the seven vco2 saws share one frequency and phase, so they sum coherently to 7x amplitude instead of the roughly sqrt(7)x an incoherent stack gives -- measured -7.72 db against -15.70 db at the default, an 8.33 db gap against the predicted ~8.5. a quartic fit in spread-1 (coefficients 1.42845067, -4.43651882, -5.39442447, 8.37724332; exactly zero at the default, so today's sound is unchanged) closes most of that. a second, separate defect: the stack's own loudness also TILTS with register, and the tilt is not fixed -- measured 3.75 db at 55 hz for today's default (spread=1), only 0.4-0.9 db at unison (0) and wide (2), so spread and register are entangled (gate: 'one loudness at every register' 3.84 db, quietest at spread=1/55hz, loudest at spread=0/55hz). a second, clamped, root-forced 2-d fit (kregcmp, in the octave from 220 hz and spread together) closes the upper half of this, and ONLY the upper half. it is forced to zero at 110/220/440 hz for any spread (krf vanishes there), the fit's own value at the default is subtracted so the correction is exactly zero at spread=1 for EVERY register, and the octave variable is clamped from below at -1 so the whole term is off at and below 110 hz. measured spread across the anchors 0/1/2 with it in place: 0.39/0.39/0.41 db at 880/1760/3520 hz against 0.66/0.55/0.52 before, stable at every preroll tried (0.38-0.48 db), and 110/220/440 hz unchanged at 0.56/0.49/0.63 as designed. THE 55 HZ READING IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE and an earlier version of this fit did not leave it alone, which was a mistake worth recording: 55 hz reads 3.82 db over the anchors at preroll 0.5 s, and a fit taken at that one preroll drove it to 0.10 db there while making every other preroll WORSE -- 3.24/5.06/3.13 db at preroll 2.0/3.5/7.0 s, and 3.05-3.13 db over a 12-30 s note against 0.74-0.90 db uncorrected. the 3.82 is not a gain law, it is the beat phase at note-on: at spread=1 the closest detune pair at 55 hz is 0.19 hz apart, a 5.2 s beat, longer than a note. uncorrected, 55 hz is inside the bound on any note longer than a few seconds and only a short one samples a phase; corrected, it was outside at three prerolls out of four. above 440 hz the same beat is fast enough to average inside a note, which is exactly why the correction is a real gain law up there and not down here. the same reasoning applies below 55 hz, where the anchors read 3.80-5.00 db at 20-41 hz for the same reason. residual, reported rather than hidden: between roughly spread 0.02 and 0.35 the closest pair of partials separates by well under a hertz, so their beat period runs to tens of seconds -- longer than a short note. a fixed gain cannot correct that: a 4 s render at spread 0.1 read as quiet as -20.4 db and, at neighbouring values, as loud as -19.2 db, purely from where in that slow cycle the note happened to land, while the true long-run average (measured over 90 s) sits at -16.2 to -16.5 db for every nonzero spread tested including the default -- within 0.3 db of each other. the same phase-dependence, re-measured directly: a 9-step sweep of the full continuous range (not just the 0/1/2 anchors) reads as much as 7.15 db of spread at 110 hz and 5.02-5.80 db at 55-220 hz, confirmed preroll-sensitive (6.35-7.37 db across preroll 0.2-0.8 s at 110 hz alone, at fixed spread values) rather than a deterministic function of spread -- no register-tilt or spread compensation can remove a defect whose driving variable is note-onset phase against an uptime-dependent near-unison beat, not spread itself. left uncompensated and reported, not hidden, same as the original note already did for the 220 hz case. a second 'rate' axis was not added: spread already sets the beat rate as a direct consequence of the same detuning (beat_rate_hz measured 0.67 at spread=1, rising with wider spread), so a separate control would either duplicate it or need a new mechanism.

techniques.why: hard sync / oscillator sync -- the classic tearing sync lead: a slave saw restarted by the master every cycle, its ratio sweeping 1.5x..3.7x
mandatory_flags: true hard sync is not yet a supported kind; approximated with FM
techniques.code:
kratio  = 2.6    ; ratio [1.5..5.0]: the slave-to-master frequency ratio centre
ksweep  = 1.1    ; sweep [0..2.5]: how far the ratio sweeps around that centre
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kswp0   oscili ksweep, 0.16            ; slave-ratio sweep
krat0   = kratio + kswp0
azro0   = 0
amst0, asyn0  syncphasor (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), azro0
aslv0, adum0  syncphasor (kfreq * koct1) * krat0, asyn0
asig    = (aslv0 * 2 - 1) * 0.45  ; hard-synced saw

ratio.note: the slave-to-master ratio at the centre of the sweep (today 2.6), declared over 1.5..5.0 -- this is where the sync tear sits. a higher ratio packs more slave cycles, and so more tears, into each master cycle: centroid climbs 9085 -> 10207 hz at 220 hz while comb contrast holds near 35-37 db (still a hard, aliased edge at every ratio). loudness does not move here by construction and needed no compensation: the slave phasor always spans 0..1 and the output is always (aslv*2-1)*0.45, so peak-to-peak amplitude is fixed whatever the ratio is -- measured spread 0.01-0.07 db across 110-880 hz.

near.gloss: close to the master, a soft, near-unison buzz

far.gloss: many tears per cycle, dense and metallic

sweep.note: the depth of the ratio sweep around the centre (today 1.1), declared over 0..2.5 -- how much the tear moves. at 0 the ratio is frozen at its centre and the tear stops moving: measured centroid travel only 1-8 cents at coherence 0.25-0.47 across the four registers, well under the library's movement threshold (60 cents / 0.35), so this anchor is genuinely static and reported plainly as such -- a deliberate 'sync held still' setting, not this entry's usual character (its only remaining motion there is the pre-existing 0.07%-deep pitch vibrato shared by all four axis bodies in this batch). above 0 the tear sweeps audibly again (centroid travel up to 1610 cents at coherence 0.999 at the top anchor). loudness stays flat by the same fixed-amplitude construction as ratio and needed no compensation: measured spread 0.05-0.12 db across 110-880 hz.

frozen.gloss: the tear parked in one place, no sweep at all

wide.gloss: the tear ranging far and fast

four.note: the 4' register stop's own gbuzz amplitude -- 0 is the 8' choir alone, the top a full second choir an octave and a hair up. this is a real stop, and pulling it genuinely adds power rather than swapping it, since the 4' choir sits at its own frequency: measured total power fits p0 + four^2*p40 (p0 the 8'-alone power, p40 the 4' choir's own power at amplitude 1) to within 2%, and kfcomp is that model's inverse. against 7.5 db of raw swing with the stop pulled all the way, loudness now holds to 0.02 db at 220 hz and 0.03-0.15 db at 110/440/880 across the whole 0-1 range. centroid at 220 hz runs 821 -> 1054 hz. at four=0 the entry stands still -- the 8' choir's only motion is a tuning drift too shallow to register as movement -- away from 0 it moves the way today's default already does.

techniques.why: chiptune -- the NES / Game Boy / C64 voice: the duty cycle STEPS between three fixed settings (12.5%, 25%, 50%) instead of gliding, giving the hard retro timbre switches
techniques.code:
kspeed  = 0.9    ; speed [0.15..4.0]: the selector's rate, in Hz
kwide   = 1.0    ; wide [0..1]: 0 no step (plain 50% square), 1 today's 12.5/25/50% zones
kst0    oscili 1.49, kspeed            ; slow 3-zone selector
kdt0    = (kst0 > 0.5 ? (0.5 - 0.375 * kwide) : (kst0 > -0.5 ? (0.5 - 0.25 * kwide) : 0.5))
kdw0    tonek kdt0, 30          ; de-click the duty step
; a +-A pulse of duty d has rms = 2*A*sqrt(d*(1-d)) once its dc is removed (exact,
; for vco2's fixed-level pulse -- see the dc term below). keq0 renormalises every
; duty back to a FIXED reference power, so the three zones the selector steps
; between (and everything wide sweeps between them) are equal-power: this is what
; makes speed (which only changes how long a short note's selector dwells in one
; zone before the note ends) a true no-loudness rate control, and it makes wide's
; own spread hold without a separate long-run average fit. the reference
; (0.377152 db-domain, i.e. 0.42590 in sqrt(d(1-d)) units) is today's three zones'
; OWN dwell-time-weighted average power at wide=1 (dwell fractions 39.11/21.79/
; 39.11% for duty 0.125/0.25/0.5, from where the +-0.5 selector thresholds cross a
; 1.49-amplitude sine) -- so the note's long-run energy at the shipped default is
; held, even though the instant-to-instant balance between zones necessarily moves
; (that IS the fix: today's zones are not equal-power, which is the defect).
keq0    = 0.42590 / sqrt(kdw0 * (1 - kdw0))
ach0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1), 2, kdw0     ; stepped chip duty
asig    = (ach0 - 0.6 * (2 * kdw0 - 1)) * keq0 ; remove dc, then equalise zone power

speed.note: the selector's own rate (today 0.9 hz), declared over 0.15..4.0 hz. the prior batch shipped this uncompensated, calling the loudness swing a measurement-window artefact that a longer render would erase -- it does not: measured over a 3 s note the anchors read -7.46/-5.87/-5.81 db (slow/steady/fast), and over a 12 s and a 40 s note they read -6.92/-6.03/-5.81 db, identical at 12 and 40 s -- the gap is real and converged, not a transient. the cause is structural: the selector steps between three duty zones and a two-level pulse's rms depends on its duty (rms proportional to sqrt(d*(1-d)) once the dc is removed), so a slow speed spends a whole short note sitting in one zone's own loudness while a fast one averages all three into the same short note. the fix (keq0, shared with wide below) renormalises every duty back to a fixed reference power, so speed now only changes how quickly the selector cycles through zones that are already equal-power: measured spread 0.01 db at 220 hz at both 3 s and 12 s (was 1.65 db at 3 s, 1.11 db at 12/40 s), and 0.01/0.02/0.05 db at 110/440/880 hz. this is the same mechanism that had to move wide's own zones, so the default note's own instant-by-instant waveform is no longer identical to the shipped body -- see measured.default_max_sample_diff and its note.

slow.gloss: a lazy few-second crawl between duty zones

fast.gloss: a fast flicker between zones, almost a buzz

wide.note: how far the three duty zones spread from 50% -- at 1 (today) they are 12.5/25/50%, at 0 all three collapse to 50% and the selector stops changing anything audible. the prior batch compensated this with a long-run average gain fit against wide; that only held the average level across different wide settings, not the moment-to-moment balance between the three zones at one wide setting, which is the actual defect speed's own failure exposed. replaced with the same keq0 equal-power renormalisation speed uses (see speed's note): every duty the selector visits, at any wide setting, is now the same instantaneous power, so wide's spread holds as a side effect with no separate fit. measured spread 0.01 db at 220 hz and 0.00/0.02/0.05 db at 110/440/880 hz. brightness at 220 hz runs 525 -> 748 hz as the steps widen, on the POWER-weighted centroid (`lco_measure.centroid_audible`) -- the even harmonics coming back in as the duty leaves 50 %, measured as 0-1 khz 90.4 % -> 85.9 % and 1-4 khz 7.7 % -> 11.1 % of the energy. the amplitude-weighted `centroid` the library's notes normally quote is NOT usable on this entry and an earlier draft of this note quoted it: the duty stepping leaves a broadband floor between the harmonics (0.00 % of the power at wide=0, 0.06 % at 0.125, 0.75 % at 1.0), and amplitude weighting turned that floor into a 3742 -> 6183 hz reading between two settings whose power spectra agree to a tenth of a percent, non-monotonic with a maximum at wide=0.125. same sound, wrong number.

kwide   = 0.5    ; wide [0..1]: 0 no step (plain 50% square), 1 today's 12.5/25/50% zones
kst0    oscili 1.49, kspeed            ; slow 3-zone selector
kdt0    = (kst0 > 0.5 ? (0.5 - 0.375 * kwide) : (kst0 > -0.5 ? (0.5 - 0.25 * kwide) : 0.5))
kdw0    tonek kdt0, 30          ; de-click the duty step
; a +-A pulse of duty d has rms = 2*A*sqrt(d*(1-d)) once its dc is removed (exact,
; for vco2's fixed-level pulse -- see the dc term below). keq0 renormalises every
; duty back to a FIXED reference power, so the three zones the selector steps
; between (and everything wide sweeps between them) are equal-power: this is what
; makes speed (which only changes how long a short note's selector dwells in one
; zone before the note ends) a true no-loudness rate control, and it makes wide's
; own spread hold without a separate long-run average fit. the reference
; (0.377152 db-domain, i.e. 0.42590 in sqrt(d(1-d)) units) is today's three zones'
; OWN dwell-time-weighted average power at wide=1 (dwell fractions 39.11/21.79/
; 39.11% for duty 0.125/0.25/0.5, from where the +-0.5 selector thresholds cross a
; 1.49-amplitude sine) -- so the note's long-run energy at the shipped default is
; held, even though the instant-to-instant balance between zones necessarily moves
; (that IS the fix: today's zones are not equal-power, which is the defect).
keq0    = 0.42590 / sqrt(kdw0 * (1 - kdw0))
ach0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1), 2, kdw0     ; stepped chip duty
asig    = (ach0 - 0.6 * (2 * kdw0 - 1)) * keq0 ; remove dc, then equalise zone power
