techniques.why: theremin / ondes martenot / musical saw -- the breathing, near-vocal purity of a swept heterodyne tone: an almost pure tone whose odd harmonics waver slowly under a heterodyne nonlinearity
mandatory_flags: theremin's character is continuous pitch/amplitude glide, not a fixed spectrum; approximated as a pure tone
techniques.code:
kpurity = 0.42   ; purity [0.0..1.0]: the heterodyne index centre -- near a plain tone at the bottom, a thicker heterodyne buzz at the top
  kbreath = 0.9    ; breath [0.2..3.0]: the slow timbre-waver's own rate
  kwv0    poscil 0.5, kbreath              ; slow timbre waver
  kpurexc = 14.804794210822694*kpurity^3 - 20.23768448609437*kpurity^2 + 2.4679026609101387*kpurity + 1.4365508322733567
  kampcomp = 0.55 * 10 ^ (-kpurexc / 20)
  kndx0   = kpurity + 0.34 * kwv0       ; heterodyne mix depth
  asig    foscili kampcomp, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2, kndx0, giSine ; heterodyne nonlinearity

purity.note: the centre of foscili's own heterodyne index (kndx0), which also wavers +-0.17 around whatever this is set to. raising it moves the tone from near the plain carrier (index 0, a sine at the carrier frequency) toward a thicker heterodyne buzz: centroid at 220 hz runs 258->361->552 hz across 0.0/0.42/1.0, doubling over the full range at every register (129->276 at 110, 513->1104 at 440, 1028->2173 at 880). foscili's own output level is not constant with index -- raw excess reaches -2.2 db uncompensated -- so a cubic fit of the excess, zeroed at the shipped default, holds level flat: loudness spread measured 0.15-0.38 db (worst at 880 hz).

plain.gloss: near the bare carrier -- centroid 258 hz at a played 220

default.gloss: today's heterodyne -- centroid 361 hz at a played 220

thick.gloss: thickest buzz -- centroid 552 hz at a played 220

breath.note: the slow timbre-waver's own rate (the poscil driving kndx0's wobble); its amplitude is untouched. loudness is unaffected by rate alone (spread measured 0.15-0.16 db, floor-level, at every register), but comb contrast moves clearly: at 220 hz, 108.3->99.5->95.1->88.8 db across breath 0.2/0.9/1.5/3.0, a real colour change as the waver speeds up.

slow.gloss: a long, slow waver -- comb 108.3 db at a played 220

default.gloss: today's waver -- comb 99.5 db at a played 220

fast.gloss: a quick flutter -- comb 88.8 db at a played 220

techniques.why: sub bass -- the 808-style low pair: a pure fundamental with a divider octave beneath it
mandatory_flags: 'sub' is a register/mix role, not a distinct spectrum; approximated as a pure sine
techniques.code:
kweight = 0.249                        ; weight [0..1]: 0 pure fundamental .. 1 pure sub octave, equal-power crossfade -- default is today's balance
kgf     = cos(kweight * 1.5707963268)
kgs     = sin(kweight * 1.5707963268)
; the sub octave's own 2nd harmonic sits exactly at the fundamental's frequency, so the
; two interfere: measured at 220 Hz, a symmetric dip up to 1.8 dB deep centred on the
; crossfade's middle, shallower at other registers (0.6-1.1 dB). kwcomp is 78% of a
; degree-4 fit of the 220 Hz dip's inverse -- full correction there would overcorrect
; the shallower registers past their own bound; 78% is the balance that clears all of
; 110/220/440/880 Hz. Referenced to today's default so the default point is untouched.
kwx     = kweight - 0.249
kwexc   = -3.41150534*kwx + 4.26624332*kwx*kwx + 9.90519506*kwx*kwx*kwx + -9.78084940*kwx*kwx*kwx*kwx
kwcomp  = 10^(-kwexc/20)
ksbw0   poscil 0.0006, 0.067         ; divider drift
asb0    gbuzz 0.7344614176 * kgs, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.5 * (1 + ksbw0), 2, 1, 0.55, giCos ; sub octave (divider)
afn0    poscil 0.5408448694 * kgf, (kfreq * koct1)          ; fundamental
asig    = (afn0 + asb0) * kwcomp

weight.note: the balance between the fundamental and the divider sub-octave, as an equal-power crossfade (0 pure fundamental, 1 pure sub) so it stays a colour rather than a fader by construction -- except that the sub's own 2nd harmonic (gbuzz knh=2) sits exactly at the fundamental's own frequency, so the two interfere: measured a symmetric dip up to 1.8 db deep at 220 hz in the middle of the crossfade, shallower (0.6-1.1 db) at other registers. kwcomp is a fitted, partial (78%) correction -- a full correction at 220 hz would overcorrect the shallower registers past their own bound -- which holds the spread to 0.34-0.82 db across 110/220/440/880 over the whole range, against 1.06-1.81 db uncompensated. centroid at 220 hz runs 220 -> 171 hz as the balance moves to the sub. default 0.249 (not the crossfade's own midpoint) is where the two channels' fixed gains reproduce today's exact 0.50/0.28 amplitude pair.

fundamental.gloss: a plain sine, no sub at all

default.gloss: today's balance, fundamental with a sub floor beneath it

sub.gloss: the sub octave alone, an octave-down hum

techniques.why: analogue oscillator / vco / minimoog / juno / prophet / analogue synth: wave morphs continuously triangle to saw to square to pulse; drive is the mixer pushed past unity into a soft limiter (careful: it makes a saw ROUNDER and darker, only a triangle brighter); fat = detuned unison, age = analogue instability

wave.note: which waveform the oscillator runs, as one continuous axis through four shapes rather than a switch: a hollow triangle, then a bright saw, then a hollow reedy square, then a thin narrow pulse. the waveform is fixed when the orchestra is compiled, so the two halves are separate oscillators and the axis crossfades them between the saw and the square anchors -- a value in that gap is genuinely both at once. measured at the four anchors: the colour sits at 689, 2211, 5686 and 4557 Hz, at one loudness within 0.01 dB.

drive.note: counter-intuitive, and this is the real behaviour of the hardware this models: what a soft clipper does first is round off the waveform's own sharp edge, so on a saw drive DARKENS the tone before it brightens it (measured: colour 1999 -> 2056 -> 3134 Hz across the axis). on a triangle it strengthens the third harmonic by 4.8 dB while the centre of gravity FALLS from 525 to 343 Hz -- more edge, not more brightness. never describe drive as simply 'brighter'. the gain out of the stage is measured per waveform branch, so the loudness holds within 0.2 dB at every anchor.

fat.note: how many oscillators there are and how far apart they sit. at 0 there is one; above it a second one runs up to 1 % sharp and wanders slowly against the first, which is what two analogue oscillators sound like when they are not perfectly in tune. it is width, not volume: measured, the beating goes from nothing to 3.2 Hz at a depth of 0.27 while the loudness moves 0.22 dB.

worn.gloss: gentle analogue life -- pitch, level and shape all drifting slightly

old.gloss: unstable, wandering pitch and level, worn-in gear

age.note: how worn the instrument is: pitch, level and shape all drifting. at 0 it is a pristine oscillator that never moves, at 1 an old one that will not sit still. all three instabilities scale from this one number and their depths at 0.35 are the ear-approved ones. honest limit: two of the three run at 0.043 and 0.057 Hz, so within ONE held note this reads as a fixed offset rather than an audible wander -- it is a difference across a phrase.

techniques.code:
kwave   = 0.45   ; wave [0..1]: triangle, saw, square, narrow pulse
kdrive  = 0.0    ; drive [0..1]: the clean oscillator, to a fully saturated stage
kfat    = 0.0    ; fat [0..1]: one oscillator, to a wide detuned pair
kage    = 0.35   ; age [0..1]: pristine, to worn-in gear that drifts
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
; `age` is three slow instabilities, all scaled from one axis. Their depths at 0.35
; are the ear-approved ones. Two of them run at 0.043 and 0.057 Hz, so on a single
; held note this axis is a static offset rather than an audible wander -- known, and
; the fix BJ deferred is a second FASTER layer, not more depth.
kvdr0   poscil 0.0070 * kage, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0  ; age: pitch drift
kdty0   poscil 0.0120 * kage, 0.057     ; age: shape/duty wobble on kpw
kagw0   oscili 0.0300 * kage, 0.7       ; age: amplitude wobble
kpwr    = limit(0.5 - 1.066667 * kwave, 0.02, 0.5) + kdty0        ; ramp: triangle -> saw
kpwp    = limit(0.5 - 0.888889 * (kwave - 0.55), 0.1, 0.5) + kdty0 ; pulse: square -> narrow
kmix    = limit((kwave - 0.45) / 0.10, 0, 1)     ; the two branches meet between the anchors
kdet    = 0.010 * kfat                  ; fat: the second oscillator sits up to 1 % sharp
kdwn    poscil 0.004 * kfat, 0.13       ; and wanders against the first, so the pair breathes
aao0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 4, kpwr, 0
aao1    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), 2, kpwp, 0
aao2    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0) * (1 + kdet + kdwn), 4, kpwr, 0
aao3    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0) * (1 + kdet + kdwn), 2, kpwp, 0
acln0   = aao0 * (1 - kmix) + aao1 * kmix * 0.578    ; the player's waveform
acln1   = aao2 * (1 - kmix) + aao3 * kmix * 0.578    ; and the same one, detuned
acln    = (acln0 + acln1 * kfat * 1.4) / sqrt(1 + (kfat * 1.4) ^ 2) ; two of them, one loudness
; A saturating stage, and on a saw or a narrow pulse it makes the tone ROUNDER and
; DARKER, not brighter: what a soft clipper does first is round off the waveform's
; own discontinuity. The gain into it is the drive, and the gain out of it holds one
; loudness across the axis -- `drive` is a colour control, not a fader.
adrv    = tanh(acln * (1.0 + 5.0 * kdrive))
; The saturator's own gain, measured per branch and blended by the same `kmix`: a
; soft clipper raises RMS by up to 8.9 dB, and drive is a colour control.
acmp    = exp(-0.1151293 * ((3.1926 + (+0.7990) * kmix) * kdrive + (12.4220 + (+2.7997) * kmix) * kdrive * kdrive + (-7.8673 + (-2.4744) * kmix) * kdrive * kdrive * kdrive))
asig    = (acln * (1 - kdrive) + adrv * kdrive) * acmp * (1 + kagw0)

techniques.why: struck glass / a glass pad -- a bright inharmonic sheen: six `mode` resonators at glass ratios (1, 2.71, 3.83, 5.17, 6.61, 8.09) at very high Q (1400-2000) under a continuous noise exciter, so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking. Not a harmonic series: that is the substance of glass, not a detail. Measured on this build: the spectrum follows the keyboard exactly, and like every noise-driven `mode` bank it gets about 1.8 dB quieter per octave upward, because a noise-driven resonator emits power ~ Q/f. Two axes: `strike` is how far up the wall it is hit (centroid 505 -> 1329 Hz, comb 42.3 -> 24.4 dB) and `ring` how long it is left to sound (T60 3.45 s to 56 s). This is the DIGITAL glass -- the pitched, playable glass-bell of late-eighties sample-plus-synthesis machines (the D-50 lineage), and its lowest mode sits exactly ON the note played, which is what makes it play like an instrument. For real, physical, struck glass, which has no note at the pitch played, use `struck_glass`.
techniques.code:
; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE
; A noise-rung resonator bank, not a sustained tone with a rate.
; Its liveness is the exciter's dither through six Q-1400+ modes: the colour
; travels 900-1900 cents over a note and does so INCOHERENTLY, which is what
; being alive means here -- there is no rate to find. Declared by BJ 2026-07-25
; for this family, after the same reading on all four of its members.
kstrike = 0.45     ; strike [0..1]: how far up the wall of the glass it is struck
kring   = 0.50     ; ring [0..1]: how long the glass is left to ring
aexq0   rand 0.05, 0.5, 1          ; continuous exciter -> the metal is driven, a held note stands (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
; `strike` re-tilts the mode gains geometrically and `ring` scales every Q. Both are
; exactly 1 at their defaults, so this entry still renders the sound it shipped with.
; The trailing `balance` is what makes both of them colour and not level: it holds the
; RMS against a fixed reference whatever the modes do, at every register.
kstk    = 0.55 + 1.00 * kstrike               ; 0.55 (the middle) .. 1.55 (the edge)
krng    = 4.0 ^ (2 * kring - 1)               ; a quarter of the Q .. four times it
k0qf0   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000, 20, 15000
k0qg0   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 < 15000 ? 1.000 : 0)
a0q0   mode aexq0, k0qf0, 1400 * krng      ; mode 1 @ x1.00, Q 1400, Q x krng
k0qf1   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 2.7100, 20, 15000
k0qg1   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 2.7100 < 15000 ? 0.620 * kstk : 0)
a0q1   mode aexq0, k0qf1, 1520 * krng      ; mode 2 @ x2.71, Q 1520, Q x krng
k0qf2   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 3.8300, 20, 15000
k0qg2   = ((kfreq * koct1) * 3.8300 < 15000 ? 0.440 * kstk ^ 2 : 0)
a0q2   mode aexq0, k0qf2, 1640 * krng      ; mode 3 @ x3.83, Q 1640, Q x krng
k0qf3   limit (kfreq * koct1) * 5.1700, 20, 15000

techniques.why: white noise -- `rand`, a flat full-spectrum hiss with no pitch at all. The keyboard does NOT change it (measured: identical at 110 and 880 Hz); it is a bed, and pitch has to come from whatever it is filtered or ring-modulated with. The raw material every other bed here is built from.

Withheld by BJ 2026-07-25 with `noise`, on the same reasoning. Note that `hiss` is NOT withheld -- it is `atone` at 6000 Hz over noise, only the top left, and all three of the synth's colours are flat or falling, so hiss could only be built by spending the user's own filter, which is the thing this withholding protects.

techniques.why: wind / breeze / gust -- a wide `reson` band walking up and down over noise, driven by two incommensurate slow oscillators (0.071 and 0.113 Hz) so the gusts never fall into a pattern: the band rises from 380 to about 1420 Hz as it blows AND gets louder at the same time, which is what makes it read as air moving rather than as a filter sweep. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it. `speed` is how hard it is blowing: the aeolian tone rises with the wind (f = St * v / d) and takes its whole gust sweep with it, and the band widens faster than it rises, so a light breeze is a nearly pure whistle at 745 Hz and a gale a broadband roar at 3046.
techniques.code:
kspeed  = 0.45                              ; speed [0..1]: how hard it is blowing
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
kgsa0   poscil 0.5, 0.071            ; gust, slow
kgsb0   poscil 0.3, 0.113            ; second, incommensurate
kgst0   = 0.5 + kgsa0 + kgsb0  ; gust strength
; An aeolian tone rises with the wind: f = St * v / d, so a stronger wind whistles higher
; through the same gap. The width goes up FASTER than the centre, because turbulence
; intensity rises with speed -- a light breeze through a gap is a nearly pure whistle and a
; gale is a broadband roar, so 69 Hz of bandwidth at one end and 1177 at the other. Both are
; free of level: `reson` with iscl=2 measures -4.8 dB on white noise at a 171 Hz centre and
; at 760, at 180 Hz of width and at 800, so this stays a colour axis on a bed whose loudness
; already swells. The width has to move: held at 400 Hz it is nearly a flat filter under a
; 171 Hz centre, the centroid stops tracking the resonance and the light-breeze corner reads
; as standing still (coherence 0.335 against the 0.35 the meter asks for).
kwsp    = 1 + 1.30 * (kspeed - 0.45)         ; exactly 1 at the default
awd0    reson anz0, (380 + 520 * kgst0) * kwsp, 400 * kwsp * kwsp, 2 ; higher when it blows
asig    = awd0 * (0.30 + 0.42 * kgst0) ; and louder

speed.note: how hard it is blowing. An aeolian tone rises with wind speed -- f = St * v / d, so a stronger wind whistles higher through the same gap -- and this scales the whole band the gust already sweeps, from 158-417 Hz at a light breeze to 652-1722 at a gale. Its WIDTH goes up as the square of that, 69 Hz to 1176, because turbulence intensity rises with speed: a light breeze through a gap is very nearly a pure whistle and a gale is a broadband roar. Centroid 745 -> 3046 Hz, motion 204 -> 826 Hz, and the envelope smooths as it rises (roughness 0.375 -> 0.152) because a faster air stream is a steadier one. Loudness 0.14 dB across all of it, which it can be because `reson` with iscl=2 holds its level whatever its centre or width -- measured -4.8 dB on white noise at a 171 Hz centre and at 760, at 180 Hz of width and at 800. The width HAS to move, and this is the reason the exponent is 2 and not 1: held at 400 Hz it is nearly a flat filter under a 158 Hz centre, the centroid stops tracking the resonance and the light-breeze corner reads as standing still -- coherence 0.335 against the 0.35 the meter asks for, where the shipped body reads 0.528.

techniques.why: surf / ocean / the sea -- two bands of noise moved by one swell: a low body (`tone` 700) that is always there and a bright break (`atone` 1800) that only arrives at the top of the swell, and arrives as the SQUARE of it, so the crest breaks instead of fading in. Two incommensurate swells (0.055 and 0.083 Hz, ~18 s and ~12 s) keep the sea from repeating. No pitch; the keyboard does not change it. `water` is how big the body of water is: a choppy lake has nothing below a few hundred hertz, an ocean swell is mostly down there.
techniques.code:
kwater  = 0.45                              ; water [0..1]: how big the body of water is
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
kswa0   poscil 0.5, 0.055            ; swell
kswb0   poscil 0.22, 0.083           ; second, incommensurate
kswl0   = 0.5 + kswa0 + kswb0  ; 0 .. 1.2
; A lake's chop has no energy below a few hundred hertz; an ocean swell is mostly down
; there. So the size of the water IS where the body's weight sits. `tone` passes power in
; exact proportion to its corner -- measured +3.70 dB from 300 to 700 Hz against +3.68
; predicted -- so 1/sqrt of it holds the level exactly, and this stays a colour axis on a
; bed whose loudness already swells. The break is left alone: `atone` obeys no such clean
; law (it loses 4.33 dB from 600 to 5200 Hz where the analytic model says 1.05), and a
; fitted exponent in a body is a number nobody can re-derive.
kbf     = 700 * 6.0 ^ (0.45 - kwater)        ; 1571 Hz (a choppy lake) .. 262 (an ocean swell)
asfl0   tone anz0, kbf               ; the body of the wave
asfb0   atone anz0, 1800             ; the break, bright
asig    = asfl0 * sqrt(700 / kbf) * (0.35 + 0.35 * kswl0) + asfb0 * 0.30 * kswl0 * kswl0

techniques.why: thunder / a distant storm / rumble -- low broadband body (`tone` 400) rolled by three incommensurate slow oscillators (0.037, 0.061, 0.091 Hz) so the rumble keeps folding over itself and never pulses. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it. `distance` is how far away the storm is: air absorbs the highs, so a strike overhead cracks and one across the county is a rumble with no edge left on it.
techniques.code:
; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE
; A stochastic event texture, not a sustained tone.
; Its liveness is where and when the events fall, which no statistic in
; `lco_measure` can tell from a static noise bed (see `declares_texture`).
kdist   = 0.40                              ; distance [0..1]: how far away the storm is
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
krla0   poscil 0.5, 0.037            ; the roll
krlb0   poscil 0.28, 0.061
krlc0   poscil 0.16, 0.091
; Air absorbs the highs, and the further the sound travels the less of them arrive: a
; strike overhead cracks, one across the county is a rumble with no edge left on it. So
; distance IS the corner frequency. A one-pole lowpass passes power in proportion to its
; corner, so the amplitude carries 1/sqrt of it -- otherwise moving the corner is a volume
; control, and a distant storm is just a quiet near one.
kfc     = 400 * 8.0 ^ (0.40 - kdist)         ; 919 Hz overhead .. 115 Hz miles off
athl0   tone anz0, kfc               ; low broadband body
asig    = athl0 * sqrt(400 / kfc) * (0.80 + 0.61 * (krla0 + krlb0 + krlc0))

techniques.why: hiss / static / tape hiss -- `atone` over noise: the top of the spectrum and nothing else, the sound of a dead channel. No pitch; the keyboard does not change it, and the entry declares `; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE` because it is stationary noise by construction -- the class no measurement in this project can tell from a swept saw (a static narrowband bed reads 1005 cents of colour travel, more than a real sweep's 959). One axis, `brightness`: the highpass corner in Hz, 500 to 16000, shipping at 6000. Reach for it when a prompt wants tape hiss, radio static, a dead channel, the noise floor of something. Do NOT reach for it for a dark or low noise bed: `atone` is one-pole at -6 dB per octave and white noise's energy is in its top octaves by bandwidth, so even the axis's lowest corner still has 75.3 % of its energy above 6 kHz, and the whole axis moves the power-weighted centroid only 11346 -> 14614 Hz. What it does move is what sits under that -- 2-6 kHz from 18.4 to 5.7 % of the energy, 0.5-2 kHz from 5.8 to 0.3 % -- which is the difference between a broad rush and a distant sizzle. For dark noise the library has `rain`, `surf` and `wind`; for a full-spectrum bed `noise` and `pink_noise` exist in the lexicon but are withheld from the library because the synth's own `NoiseGenerator` already gives the player both.

brightness.note: the corner of the one-pole highpass, in Hz: how much of the top is left. The shipped sound is 6000 Hz and stays exactly that -- the compensation below is 1.0 there to fifteen places, so the default renders bit-identical to what shipped (max|a-b| = 0.0 at 110/220/440 Hz). Measured at 220 Hz, preroll 2 s: power-weighted centroid 11346 Hz at 500, 11931 Hz at 1500, 13530 Hz at 6000, 14386 Hz at 12000, and the share of energy above 6 kHz 75 %, 80 %, 90 %, 94 %. How far that travels is worth being honest about, because `atone` is a ONE-POLE highpass at -6 dB per octave and white noise's energy sits in its top octaves by bandwidth alone: even at the lowest corner the band above 6 kHz still holds 75.3 % of the energy, so no setting here makes a dark or low sound. What the axis really moves is everything below that -- the 2-6 kHz share falls 18.4 -> 5.7 % and the 0.5-2 kHz share 5.8 -> 0.3 % from `full band` to `thin sizzle`, which is the difference between a broad rush and a distant sizzle. For a dark noise bed the library has `rain`, `surf` and `wind`; this entry is the top of the spectrum by construction. Moving the corner moves the LEVEL, by 11.47 dB over 500..16000 Hz raw, so the axis carries a compensation -- and two things about it are worth knowing. First it is measured, not derived: `atone` is not the ideal one-pole highpass its analytic power ratio describes, which predicts only 4.85 dB over that range and is wrong by +3.39 dB at the bottom and -3.23 dB at the top. Second it is written in fc/sr and not in Hz, because the level of noise through a one-pole digital filter is a function of the NORMALISED corner and of nothing else -- measured, same fc/sr at 44100 and 96000 Hz agreeing to 0.008 dB at four points across the range. `tools/lco_measure.py` renders at 44100 while the host's `%SR%` is the oversampled rate, so a gain fitted in Hz would have been the wrong gain in the plugin by 3.0 dB at the default corner alone. What the compensation deliberately does NOT do is make the entry's absolute level rate-independent: this body is 2.8 dB louder at 96 kHz than at 44.1 kHz because more of the band passes a fixed corner, that is how it has always shipped, and an axis is not the place to change it. Degree 6 in ln(fc/sr), worst fit residual 0.041 dB, monotone over every corner reachable at any host rate (fc/sr 0.0026..0.363). Resulting spread over the anchors 0.075 dB at 44.1 kHz, 0.062 at 48 kHz, 0.066 at 96 kHz, and 0.078 dB worst over all six registers x preroll 0.5/2.0/5.0 s x duration 1/3/11 s -- the body has no pitch in it, and the register-independence is measured rather than assumed (three corners x six registers, identical to 0.000 dB). Worst whole-note peak 0.598 against the 2.523 bound.

techniques.why: crackle / fire / a campfire -- the same particle architecture as `rain` at a hundredth of the rate: `dust2` fires about 22 pops a second and each rings wood (`reson` 1600 Hz, wide), over a fine sizzle that breathes at 0.13 Hz. Sparse enough that individual events are heard, which is the difference between fire and rain. No pitch, and the keyboard does not change it. `blaze` is how big the fire is, and it is the POP RATE: a bigger fire pops more often, it does not pop louder.
techniques.code:
; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE
; A stochastic event texture, not a sustained tone.
; Its liveness is where and when the events fall, which no statistic in
; `lco_measure` can tell from a static noise bed (see `declares_texture`).
kblaze  = 0.40                              ; blaze [0..1]: how big the fire is
anz0    rand 1.0, 0.5, 1         ; broadband noise source (31-bit: no 1.365 s loop)
; A bigger fire pops MORE OFTEN, it does not pop louder. As in `rain`, the amplitude carries
; 1/sqrt of the rate, because a Poisson impulse train's RMS goes as its square root --
; without that the axis is a fader with a crackle attached.
kpop    = 22 * 30.0 ^ (kblaze - 0.40)        ; 5.7 (embers) .. 170 (a bonfire) pops/s
acrk0   dust2 0.8 * sqrt(22 / kpop), kpop
apop0   reson acrk0, 1600, 1200, 2 ; each pop rings the wood
kbed0   poscil 0.5, 0.13             ; the fire breathes
absd0   atone anz0, 3000             ; fine sizzle between pops
asig    = apop0 * 1.90 + absd0 * (0.34 + 0.20 * kbed0)

blaze.note: how big the fire is -- which is the POP RATE, from under six a second in embers to 170 in a bonfire. A bigger fire pops more OFTEN, it does not pop louder, so the amplitude carries 1/sqrt of the rate: a Poisson impulse train's RMS goes as the square root of its rate, and without that the axis is a fader with a crackle attached. Its mark is the crest factor, 8.94 -> 3.47 monotone, and the motion 3441 -> 1483 Hz -- individual pops merging into a continuum -- at 0.02 dB of loudness. The centroid moves 54 Hz and nothing else the spectral meter has can see this axis at all, which is why the crest is quoted: more of the same event is not a different spectrum.

techniques.why: a sung human voice on an open 'ahh' -- real formant synthesis, not an additive sketch: a `vco2` glottal source tilted by `tone`, through three `reson` formants at 600 / 1040 / 2250 Hz, with three-rate period jitter and two-rate amplitude shimmer so it is never a steady tone. The pitch follows the keyboard and the formants do NOT, which is what makes it a voice -- and also its ceiling: measured on this build it is level within 3.3 dB from 110 to 660 Hz and then falls 13.8 dB at 880, because above the first formant no harmonic can land in it any more. Usable up to roughly its own F1.
techniques.code:
kjit    = 1.0   ; jitter [0..5]: pitch and amplitude unsteadiness, dead-steady to a wide, strained voice
kpress  = 200   ; press [120..330]: glottal source slope cutoff, hz -- low is soft, relaxed, breathy; high is pressed, bright, strained
kjta0   poscil 0.0022 * kjit, 7.3           ; jitter: period, 3 rates
kjtb0   poscil 0.0014 * kjit, 11.7
kjtc0   poscil 0.0009 * kjit, 19.1
ksha0   poscil 0.030 * kjit, 5.1            ; shimmer: amplitude, 2 rates
kshb0   poscil 0.018 * kjit, 8.9
asrc0    vco2 0.5, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kjta0 + kjtb0 + kjtc0), 0
aglt0   tone asrc0, kpress           ; glottal slope, -6 -> -12 dB/oct
kpx     = log2(kpress / 200)                          ; press deviation from the default cutoff, in octaves
kprf0   = log2((kfreq * koct1) / 220)                 ; register, in octaves from 220 hz
kprf    = limit(kprf0, -1, 2)                         ; clamp to the fitted 110-880 hz span
kprtap  = limit(1 - abs(kprf0 - kprf), 0, 1)          ; fade to no correction one octave beyond it
kpc1r   = 3.5124 + 1.7090 * kprf + 0.1968 * kprf * kprf - 0.2481 * kprf * kprf * kprf
kpc2r   = -0.8958 + 0.2337 * kprf + 0.3407 * kprf * kprf - 0.1387 * kprf * kprf * kprf
kgpb0   = kprtap * (kpc1r * kpx + kpc2r * kpx * kpx)  ; measured RMS excess, fit in dB, per register
kgpr0   = 10 ^ (-kgpb0 / 20)                          ; compensating gain, exactly 1 at kpress=200
kfw0x0  poscil 0.011, 0.23            ; formant wander, formant 1
a0f0   reson aglt0, 600 * (1 + kfw0x0), 60, 1 ; formant 1 @ 600 Hz
kfw0x1  poscil 0.011, 0.31            ; formant wander, formant 2
a0f1   reson aglt0, 1040 * (1 + kfw0x1), 80, 1 ; formant 2 @ 1040 Hz
kfw0x2  poscil 0.011, 0.19            ; formant wander, formant 3
a0f2   reson aglt0, 2250 * (1 + kfw0x2), 120, 1 ; formant 3 @ 2250 Hz
asig    = (a0f0 * 1.000 + a0f1 * 0.600 + a0f2 * 0.320) * 10.7 * kgpr0 * (1 + ksha0 + kshb0)

jitter.note: scales all five of the source's existing jitter/shimmer generators together -- the three pitch-jitter poscils (rates 7.3/11.7/19.1 hz) and the two amplitude-shimmer poscils (rates 5.1/8.9 hz) -- from a perfectly steady formant tone to a wide, strained voice. short-window pitch wander at 220 hz (150 ms window, 75 ms hop) measures 0.03 cents at 0 (steady), 5.74 cents at 1.0 (today's voice) and 31.44 cents at 5.0 (the top); amplitude beat depth over the same span is 0.001 -> 0.028 -> 0.141. rms stays within 0.15 db of its default at every register (110/220/440/880 hz) across the whole range -- this axis recolours steadiness, it does not change loudness. the top of the range was picked as the point where the tone still reads as a strained voice rather than a warble, by the cents-spread and beat-depth figures above.

voice.gloss: today's default -- a natural, mildly live voice

strained.gloss: wide, unsteady, strained -- an old or effortful voice, still tonal, not a warble

press.note: replaces the rejected tract axis (a formant-centre scale that swung by tens of dB and could not be fit -- moving a narrow resonance across a sparse harmonic source is real vocal physics, and its sign flips with register, which is why sopranos tune formants to harmonics and why it cannot be a colour control here; measured on this body's tract: 1.94/5.8/8.22 dB at 110/440/880 Hz, compliant only at 220 Hz where it was fitted). press instead moves the glottal source's own one-pole slope cutoff (aglt0 tone asrc0, kpress -- the '-6 -> -12 dB/oct' comment already on this line) before the formants: low is a soft, relaxed, breathy voice, high is a pressed, bright, strained one -- physically vocal effort, the thing a singer actually changes. this is broadband, not resonant, so it cannot land on one harmonic the way tract did: it moves loudness a lot but smoothly, monotonically and with the same sign at every register, which is what makes it fittable. the compensation (kgpr0) adds a register term (kfreq*koct1, log2 octaves from 220 hz, clamped to the fitted 110-880 hz span and faded to no correction one octave beyond it), the same construction as additive's bright and strings' desk. the coefficients are shared line-for-line across voice/voice_ee/voice_oo (fit against the worst-case vowel at each register, since the three vowels' raw excess agrees to within a few tenths of a dB but not exactly) -- measured spread 0.34 db at 220 hz and 0.05/0.38/0.07 db at 110/440/880 hz. the range 120-330 hz was picked empirically: at 100-400 hz (symmetric in octaves around the 200 hz default) the shared fit's worst vowel exceeded the 220 hz bound (0.60-0.76 db); narrowed to 120-330 hz it clears every bound with margin (worst case 0.94 of the 0.5 db budget) while still moving the centroid by roughly a quarter at 220 hz. centroid at every anchor (120/200/330 hz cutoff): 110 hz 384.5 -> 424.0 -> 475.8 Hz; 220 hz 513.8 -> 536.8 -> 576.5 Hz; 440 hz 670.7 -> 680.2 -> 702.2 Hz; 880 hz 1243.9 -> 1248.8 -> 1260.6 Hz.

techniques.why: a bright, thin, nasal 'eee' vowel -- the same formant bank as `voice` moved to 270 / 2290 / 3010 Hz: a very low first formant and a very high second, which is the whole reason 'eee' sounds pinched. Its first formant is also its ceiling, and this one is LOW: measured level to 220 Hz, then -6 dB at 330, -21 dB at 440 and gone by 660. A bass and baritone vowel, not a soprano one.

jitter.note: scales all five of the source's existing jitter/shimmer generators together -- the three pitch-jitter poscils (rates 7.3/11.7/19.1 hz) and the two amplitude-shimmer poscils (rates 5.1/8.9 hz) -- from a perfectly steady formant tone to a wide, strained voice. short-window pitch wander at 220 hz (150 ms window, 75 ms hop) measures 0.08 cents at 0 (steady), 5.7 cents at 1.0 (today's voice) and 29.48 cents at 5.0 (the top); amplitude beat depth over the same span is 0.011 -> 0.028 -> 0.142. rms stays within 0.13 db of its default at every register (110/220/440/880 hz) across the whole range -- this axis recolours steadiness, it does not change loudness. the top of the range was picked as the point where the tone still reads as a strained voice rather than a warble, by the cents-spread and beat-depth figures above.

voice.gloss: today's default -- a natural, mildly live voice

strained.gloss: wide, unsteady, strained -- an old or effortful voice, still tonal, not a warble

press.note: replaces the rejected tract axis (a formant-centre scale that swung by tens of dB and could not be fit -- moving a narrow resonance across a sparse harmonic source is real vocal physics, and its sign flips with register, which is why sopranos tune formants to harmonics and why it cannot be a colour control here; measured on this body's tract: 5.99/25.51/3.94 dB at 110/440/880 Hz, compliant only at 220 Hz where it was fitted). press instead moves the glottal source's own one-pole slope cutoff (aglt0 tone asrc0, kpress -- the '-6 -> -12 dB/oct' comment already on this line) before the formants: low is a soft, relaxed, breathy voice, high is a pressed, bright, strained one -- physically vocal effort, the thing a singer actually changes. this is broadband, not resonant, so it cannot land on one harmonic the way tract did: it moves loudness a lot but smoothly, monotonically and with the same sign at every register, which is what makes it fittable. the compensation (kgpr0) adds a register term (kfreq*koct1, log2 octaves from 220 hz, clamped to the fitted 110-880 hz span and faded to no correction one octave beyond it), the same construction as additive's bright and strings' desk. the coefficients are shared line-for-line across voice/voice_ee/voice_oo (fit against the worst-case vowel at each register, since the three vowels' raw excess agrees to within a few tenths of a dB but not exactly) -- measured spread 0.34 db at 220 hz and 0.05/0.32/0.08 db at 110/440/880 hz. the range 120-330 hz was picked empirically: at 100-400 hz (symmetric in octaves around the 200 hz default) the shared fit's worst vowel exceeded the 220 hz bound (0.60-0.76 db); narrowed to 120-330 hz it clears every bound with margin (worst case 0.94 of the 0.5 db budget) while still moving the centroid by roughly a quarter at 220 hz. centroid at every anchor (120/200/330 hz cutoff): 110 hz 293.8 -> 325.0 -> 373.3 Hz; 220 hz 367.4 -> 388.0 -> 429.1 Hz; 440 hz 1314.0 -> 1341.2 -> 1401.3 Hz; 880 hz 2051.2 -> 2060.7 -> 2080.7 Hz.

voice.gloss: today's default -- a natural, moderately pressed voice

pressed.gloss: bright, strained, effortful -- a pressed, forward voice

techniques.why: a dark, rounded, hollow 'ooh' vowel -- formants at 300 / 870 / 2240 Hz, both lower ones close together and low, so the sound is all body and no edge. Measured ceiling around 330 Hz (level to 330, then -14 dB at 440), for the same reason as the other vowels: the formants stand still while the voice climbs into them.

jitter.note: scales all five of the source's existing jitter/shimmer generators together -- the three pitch-jitter poscils (rates 7.3/11.7/19.1 hz) and the two amplitude-shimmer poscils (rates 5.1/8.9 hz) -- from a perfectly steady formant tone to a wide, strained voice. short-window pitch wander at 220 hz (150 ms window, 75 ms hop) measures 0.05 cents at 0 (steady), 5.68 cents at 1.0 (today's voice) and 29.77 cents at 5.0 (the top); amplitude beat depth over the same span is 0.008 -> 0.028 -> 0.142. rms stays within 0.11 db of its default at every register (110/220/440/880 hz) across the whole range -- this axis recolours steadiness, it does not change loudness. the top of the range was picked as the point where the tone still reads as a strained voice rather than a warble, by the cents-spread and beat-depth figures above.

voice.gloss: today's default -- a natural, mildly live voice

strained.gloss: wide, unsteady, strained -- an old or effortful voice, still tonal, not a warble

press.note: replaces the rejected tract axis (a formant-centre scale that swung by tens of dB and could not be fit -- moving a narrow resonance across a sparse harmonic source is real vocal physics, and its sign flips with register, which is why sopranos tune formants to harmonics and why it cannot be a colour control here; measured on this body's tract: 4.8/28.89/20.28 dB at 110/440/880 Hz, compliant only at 220 Hz where it was fitted). press instead moves the glottal source's own one-pole slope cutoff (aglt0 tone asrc0, kpress -- the '-6 -> -12 dB/oct' comment already on this line) before the formants: low is a soft, relaxed, breathy voice, high is a pressed, bright, strained one -- physically vocal effort, the thing a singer actually changes. this is broadband, not resonant, so it cannot land on one harmonic the way tract did: it moves loudness a lot but smoothly, monotonically and with the same sign at every register, which is what makes it fittable. the compensation (kgpr0) adds a register term (kfreq*koct1, log2 octaves from 220 hz, clamped to the fitted 110-880 hz span and faded to no correction one octave beyond it), the same construction as additive's bright and strings' desk. the coefficients are shared line-for-line across voice/voice_ee/voice_oo (fit against the worst-case vowel at each register, since the three vowels' raw excess agrees to within a few tenths of a dB but not exactly) -- measured spread 0.3 db at 220 hz and 0.07/0.38/0.08 db at 110/440/880 hz. the range 120-330 hz was picked empirically: at 100-400 hz (symmetric in octaves around the 200 hz default) the shared fit's worst vowel exceeded the 220 hz bound (0.60-0.76 db); narrowed to 120-330 hz it clears every bound with margin (worst case 0.94 of the 0.5 db budget) while still moving the centroid by roughly a quarter at 220 hz. centroid at every anchor (120/200/330 hz cutoff): 110 hz 274.9 -> 298.1 -> 329.6 Hz; 220 hz 363.1 -> 379.9 -> 411.1 Hz; 440 hz 862.5 -> 870.6 -> 888.0 Hz; 880 hz 958.2 -> 959.3 -> 961.7 Hz.

relaxed.gloss: soft, breathy, relaxed -- low vocal effort

voice.gloss: today's default -- a natural, moderately pressed voice

pressed.gloss: bright, strained, effortful -- a pressed, forward voice

techniques.why: a real Rhodes tine piano that RINGS AND FADES BY ITSELF -- Csound's own `fmrhode` model, re-struck on each note through `changed2(ktrig)`/`reinit`: a bell-like metallic attack over a woody body, and the note dies whether or not the key is held. Measured on this build: half-life 566-599 ms and peak flat at 0.57 from 110 to 1760 Hz. For the version that STANDS as long as the key is held -- the spectrum source, with the synth's envelope doing the striking -- use `fm_ep` instead; that is the same instrument as a standing tone.
techniques.code:
kbark   = 1.0    ; bark [0.0..1.0]: the FM modulation index and output crossfade (kc1, kc2) -- mellow and pure at the bottom, brighter and harder at the top
  ktrem   = 0.01   ; tremolo [0.0..0.5]: the model's own vibrato depth -- the tine's slow wobble
  ; --- osc 0: rhodes -- struck instrument, decays on its own ---
  if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
    reinit strike0
  endif
strike0:
  ; tremolo raises the model's own output level as it moves away from the shipped
  ; default; undo it with its measured quadratic fit of the excess, zeroed exactly
  ; at the default so the correction vanishes there. `bark` carried one too, and it
  ; is REMOVED: it was fitted against `lco_measure.rms_db`, whose 0.5-3.5 s window
  ; opens after 80 % of this note's energy has already gone. Against that window it
  ; read 0.010 db at every register; against the note's own whole-array integral it
  ; read 1.70 db, and 2.34 db over the first 400 ms -- worse than no correction at
  ; all, which is 0.13 db and 0.76 db on those two meters. The shipped default
  ; (bark = 1.0) is unaffected either way: the quadratic was zero there by
  ; construction.
  kdepthexc = 1.57317198 * ktrem * ktrem + 1.08273457 * ktrem - 0.01098466
  kampcomp = 0.7821 * 10 ^ (-kdepthexc / 20)
  asig    fmrhode kampcomp, (kfreq * koct1), kbark, kbark, ktrem, 6, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1
  rireturn

bark.note: fmrhode's own kc1/kc2 (modulation index and output crossfade), moved together. comb contrast falls from about 90 db at 220 hz down to about 18 db as bark goes 0 to 1, the same shape at every register (78.6->18.3 at 110, 102.9->18.0 at 440, 114.7->18.4 at 880), so the sound goes from a plain, pure tone to today's harder bark. loudness over the axis's whole continuum, whole-note integral: 0.14-0.15 db at every register, and 0.76-0.78 db over the first 400 ms. it carried a quadratic compensation until 2026-07-25 and that compensation was the defect: fitted against lco_measure.rms_db, whose 0.5-3.5 s window opens after 80 % of this note's energy has gone, it held THAT window to 0.010 db while the audible note read 1.70 db whole-note and 2.34 db over the first 400 ms -- worse than no correction at all. removed. the shipped default (1.0) is unchanged either way; the quadratic was zero there by construction, so what moved is the mellow end, which is now 1.57 db louder and level with the default.

mellow.gloss: plain, pure tone -- comb contrast about 90 db at 220 hz

default.gloss: today's bark -- comb contrast about 18 db at 220 hz

tremolo.note: the model's own vibrato depth (kvdepth); rate stays fixed at the shipped 6 hz -- 6 hz is too fast to read as a discrete pulse on a 3 s note, so depth, not rate, is the axis a meter and an ear both catch. amplitude modulation at 6 hz measures 0.006 at depth 0.0 (the model's own small intrinsic decay-beat, present even at zero) rising to 0.156 at depth 0.5. loudness spread measured 0.03 db at every register.

wobble.gloss: the tine breathing, unmistakable but not seasick

wide.gloss: a full wobble, the amp working

techniques.why: a real Wurlitzer reed piano that RINGS AND FADES BY ITSELF -- Csound's own `fmwurlie`, re-struck per note: reedier and barkier than a Rhodes, its brightness sitting ON the odd harmonics rather than off the comb, and it rings longer. Measured: half-life 676-718 ms, peak flat at 0.55 across the register. `fm_ep` is the standing-tone counterpart.
techniques.code:
kbark   = 1.0    ; bark [0.0..1.0]: the FM modulation index and output crossfade (kc1, kc2) -- reedy growl grows in from a plain tone at the bottom to today's bark at the top
  ktrem   = 0.01   ; tremolo [0.0..0.5]: the model's own vibrato depth -- the reed's slow wobble
  ; --- osc 0: wurlitzer -- struck instrument, decays on its own ---
  if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
    reinit strike0
  endif
strike0:
  ; both axes raise the model's own output level as they move away from the
  ; shipped default; undo each with its own measured fit of the excess (a
  ; cubic for bark -- its range moves 6 db and a quadratic left 0.04 db of
  ; residual -- and a quadratic for tremolo), each zeroed exactly at the
  ; default so the two corrections vanish there
  kbarkexc = -0.94988345 * kbark * kbark * kbark - 0.61713287 * kbark * kbark - 4.4504662 * kbark + 6.01748252
  kdepthexc = 1.70557949 * ktrem * ktrem + 0.76797365 * ktrem - 0.0078503
  kampcomp = 0.9839 * 10 ^ (-(kbarkexc + kdepthexc) / 20)
  asig    fmwurlie kampcomp, (kfreq * koct1), kbark, kbark, ktrem, 6, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1
  rireturn

techniques.why: a real struck aluminium bar that RINGS AND FADES BY ITSELF -- Csound's `vibes` model, re-struck per note: a soft mallet, sweet and round rather than clangorous, and short. Measured: half-life 284-315 ms. The model's own 15 dB register tilt is undone in the code by a 0.73 exponent below 440 Hz, so peak runs 0.42 to 0.62 across the register instead of 3.5 to 0.6. Two structural limits of the model, both measured and neither tunable: it collapses about 10 dB above ~4 kHz, and its pitch freezes at the strike, so a glide is not followed within a note. `struck_bar` is the standing-tone mallet counterpart.
techniques.code:
kmallet    = 0.9    ; mallet [0.6..1.0]: the stick hardness (ihrd) -- soft felt at the bottom, hard rubber at the top
  kstrikepos = 0.5    ; strikepos [0.3..0.7]: where the bar is struck (ipos) -- the centre voices the fundamental, off-centre wakes the higher bar modes
  kmotor     = 0.01   ; motor [0.0..1.0]: the rotating-disc tremolo's depth (kvamp)
  ; --- osc 0: vibraphone -- struck instrument, decays on its own ---
  if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
    reinit strike0
  endif
strike0:
  kvtl0   limit (kfreq * koct1) / 440, 0.001, 1   ; 1.0 at and above 440 Hz
  kvamp0  = 0.1863 * kvtl0 ^ 0.73   ; undo the model's 15 dB register tilt
  ; mallet's excess is not just a function of mallet -- the SHAPE differs by
  ; register, so its fit is 2-d. An EXACT cubic-in-octave interpolant through
  ; only four registers (110/220/440/880) diverges outside that span (measured
  ; 2026-07-25: unclamped 1.29 db at 1760 hz, 3.07 db at 3520 hz; clamping the
  ; octave makes it WORSE -- 2.61 db at 1760, 14.24 db at 3520 -- because
  ; vibes's own loudness response keeps changing shape above 880 hz, so a
  ; frozen boundary value undershoots what is actually needed there). A
  ; second, deeper problem: `vibes`'s kamp argument is NOT a linear multiplier
  ; on its own output above about 880 hz -- measured a +1.00 db kamp change
  ; producing +1.63 db of actual output change at 1760 hz (+1.07 db at 220 hz,
  ; close to linear). A compensation fit against the RAW measured excess and
  ; then applied as a plain 10^(-exc/20) gain therefore overshoots at the
  ; upper registers even with a perfect fit -- refitting the CURVE alone was
  ; not enough. So kihrdexc below is fit against a CLOSED-LOOP calibration:
  ; for each (mallet, register) the actual exc value that, applied as the
  ; real gain into vibes, reproduces the mallet=0.9 reference (solved by
  ; secant search against real renders, not inferred from a linearity
  ; assumption) -- then a least-squares regression, not an exact interpolant,
  ; over six registers, 55-1760 hz, the span this instrument is actually
  ; played over (a real vibraphone tops out around F6, about 1397 hz). Degree
  ; 3 in both mallet (kmx = mallet - 0.9, structurally zero at the shipped
  ; default for any register) and octave (kmu), over-determined by 24 points
  ; (6 registers x 6 mallets against 12 coefficients) instead of an exact fit
  ; through 4 -- residual 0.14 db worst against the calibrated target, at
  ; every fitted register. 3520 hz is NOT in the fit: it sits past this
  ; instrument's own compass and the calibrated excess there (measured -4.60
  ; db at mallet=0.6) is a genuine collapse in the model's own response, not
  ; a smooth continuation of the fitted shape -- no polynomial asked to also
  ; fit 55-1760 well can reach it. Accepted, not chased: see the measured
  ; report for that entry.
  kmoct     = log2((kfreq * koct1) / 220)
  kmx       = kmallet - 0.9
  kmC0      = 3.8779046183318386 - 4.420592400104296*kmoct - 0.4707051941242594*kmoct*kmoct + 0.38480941154997844*kmoct*kmoct*kmoct
  kmC1      = 0.48979211224557856 + 2.9662788353888487*kmoct - 0.09223187450486608*kmoct*kmoct - 0.3782089210431889*kmoct*kmoct*kmoct
  kmC2      = -4.640802244745363 - 3.0773822350347046*kmoct + 1.4162144139169361*kmoct*kmoct + 0.12892330220401607*kmoct*kmoct*kmoct
  kihrdexc  = kmx*kmC0 + kmx*kmx*kmC1 + kmx*kmx*kmx*kmC2
  ; strikepos's excess is register-dependent, and it is fit against the WHOLE
  ; NOTE. The meter mattered more than the curve here. `lco_measure.rms_db`
  ; integrates 0.5-3.5 s, and 89 % of this instrument's energy is already gone by
  ; 0.5 s (measured at every register: 88.98-89.30 %), so a fit against that
  ; window equalises the last inaudible tenth of the decay and lets the strike
  ; itself drift. The fit before this one hit that window to 0.006 db and left
  ; the strike 2.50 db loud at strikepos 0.7 at 440 hz, where doing nothing at
  ; all had been 0.36 db out. So the calibration here is closed-loop against the
  ; note's own integral over the whole array: for each (strikepos, register) the
  ; exc value that, applied as the REAL gain into vibes, reproduces the
  ; strikepos=0.5 reference's whole-note rms, found by secant search against real
  ; renders -- 88 points, 8 strike positions x 11 half-octave registers from 55
  ; to 1760 hz, worst 0.004 db from target -- then least squares over all 88.
  ; Closed-loop for the same reason mallet's is: vibes's kamp is not a linear
  ; multiplier on its own output above about 880 hz.
  ;
  ; The calibrated surface is rank 2 to 0.048 db (an svd of the 11 x 8 grid puts
  ; 99.92 % of its energy in two components), and it has a CORNER near 440 hz
  ; that no polynomial in the octave can follow -- hence `kphng`, a hinge in the
  ; register basis. Do NOT read that corner as kvtl0's clamp boundary, which is
  ; what the previous fit's fourth power was justified by: rendered at 96 khz the
  ; corner sits an octave higher, near 880 hz, so it tracks the SAMPLE RATE and
  ; not the fixed 440 hz clamp. Everything here is a 44100 hz calibration and is
  ; claimed only there.
  ;
  ; kmoct is CLAMPED to the fitted span, not extrapolated past it. Unlike
  ; mallet's, this axis's shape is nearly flat at both ends of the span, so the
  ; frozen boundary value IS the right answer outside it: anchor spread
  ; 0.058/0.040/0.099/0.089/0.051/0.132 db at 27.5/41.2/2093/3520/4186/7040 hz,
  ; against 1.56/1.56/1.65/1.79/1.75/1.74 db with no correction. The unclamped
  ; quartic it replaces read 2.25 db at 7040 hz -- worse than no correction.
  ;
  ; Every term carries kspn, so the shipped default renders bit-identical.
  ; kspn is FROZEN outside the fitted 0.3-0.7 span, for the same reason kpoct is
  ; frozen outside the register span -- and here it is also a safety: kspn enters
  ; at the sixth power, so an out-of-range strike position would not merely
  ; extrapolate, it would explode. Measured at strikepos 0 and 1: the body this
  ; replaces rendered NaN at both, and 2.23 peak at 0.15 against the host's 2.523;
  ; frozen, the worst peak over 0..1 is 0.641 and nothing is silent or non-finite.
  kspn0     = (kstrikepos - 0.5) * 5      ; -1 at 0.3, 0 at 0.5, +1 at 0.7
  kspn    limit kspn0, -1, 1
  kpoct   limit kmoct, -2, 3              ; FROZEN outside the fitted 55-1760 Hz span
  kphng   limit kpoct - 1, 0, 2           ; the measured corner, at 440 Hz at 44100
  kpC1      = -0.0247720726906 - 0.0760762610748*kpoct - 0.023251755062*kpoct*kpoct + 0.459725665052*kphng - 0.0986152379978*kphng*kphng
  kpC2      = 1.68799122557 + 3.45923958974*kpoct + 1.11161432474*kpoct*kpoct - 10.5347749514*kphng - 0.495661031649*kphng*kphng
  kpC3      = 0.318261126021 + 0.336618009353*kpoct + 0.0974612401977*kpoct*kpoct - 1.38615955462*kphng + 0.127327362118*kphng*kphng
  kpC4      = -4.38472694714 - 5.35223138406*kpoct - 1.84982728135*kpoct*kpoct + 18.1000506082*kphng + 0.298037529596*kphng*kphng
  kpC5      = -0.215792950409 - 0.202783077191*kpoct - 0.0577405689055*kpoct*kpoct + 0.771120939171*kphng - 0.046655522773*kphng*kphng
  kpC6      = 1.85637275848 + 2.54899701966*kpoct + 0.914157937482*kpoct*kpoct - 8.66853749738*kphng - 0.150579772556*kphng*kphng
  kiposexc  = kspn*kpC1 + kspn*kspn*kpC2 + kspn*kspn*kspn*kpC3 + kspn*kspn*kspn*kspn*kpC4 + kspn*kspn*kspn*kspn*kspn*kpC5 + kspn*kspn*kspn*kspn*kspn*kspn*kpC6
  kmoctclip = (kmoct > 1 ? kmoct - 1 : 0)
  kmdamp    = 1 - 0.12 * kmoctclip * kmoctclip
  kmotorexc = kmdamp * (-0.7126452412530796*kmotor^3 + 1.8946907660388002*kmotor^2 + 1.508710357644792*kmotor - 0.01527586000781156)
  kampcomp  = kvamp0 * 10 ^ (-(kihrdexc + kiposexc + kmotorexc) / 20)
  asig    vibes kampcomp, (kfreq * koct1), i(kmallet), i(kstrikepos), 4, 6, kmotor, 1, 0.5
  rireturn

mallet.note: vibes's own stick-hardness (ihrd). the model's loudness response to ihrd genuinely differs in shape by register (not just level), so this is a 2-d compensation. an EXACT cubic-in-octave interpolant through only four measured registers (110/220/440/880) was found to diverge outside that span: unclamped, 1.29 db spread at 1760 hz and 3.07 db at 3520 hz; clamping the octave to the fitted span made it WORSE (2.61 db at 1760, 14.24 db at 3520), because vibes's own loudness response keeps changing shape above 880 hz and a frozen boundary value undershoots what is actually needed there. a second, deeper problem underneath: vibes's kamp argument is not a linear multiplier on its own output above about 880 hz -- measured a +1.00 db kamp change producing +1.63 db of actual output change at 1760 hz (close to linear, +1.07 db, at 220 hz), so a compensation fit against the raw measured excess and applied as a plain 10^(-exc/20) gain overshoots at the upper registers even with a perfect curve fit. the compensation actually shipped here was calibrated closed-loop: for each (mallet, register) the exc value that, applied as the real gain, reproduces the mallet=0.9 reference was found by direct search against real renders, not inferred from a linearity assumption -- then fit by least squares (not an exact interpolant), degree 3 in both mallet and octave, over six registers, 55-1760 hz, the span this instrument is actually played over (residual under 0.14 db at every fitted register). the full [0..1] range vibes itself accepts is narrowed to [0.6..1.0] for a separate reason: below 0.6 the needed correction outgrows what a linear-in-db gain can deliver against vibes's own non-linear response to amplitude. within [0.6..1.0] centroid still moves 288->307 hz at 220 hz and 904->962 hz at 880 hz across the range. loudness spread measured 0.03-0.22 db at every register from 55 to 1760 hz (worst at 220 hz), against 1.85/0.13/0.12/0.10/0.94/1.29 db at 55/110/220/440/880/1760 hz before this fit. 3520 hz is explicitly NOT covered: it sits past this instrument's own compass (a real vibraphone tops out around F6, about 1397 hz) and past where the model's response is smooth -- the calibrated excess there is a genuine collapse (-4.60 db at mallet=0.6), not a smooth continuation of the fitted shape, and no polynomial asked to also fit 55-1760 well can reach it. the spread at 3520 hz is 3.86 db with this fit in place (worse than the 3.07 db before, because the fit was not asked to cover that register) -- an accepted, stated degradation above the instrument's own playing range, not a silently narrowed claim. the top of the keyboard, measured 2026-07-25 on the shipped body and on three alternatives, so that nobody reaches for a clamp a fourth time: mallet's own anchor spread at 220/880/1760/2093/2794/3520/4186 hz is 0.22/0.05/0.04/0.09/0.28/3.86/12.45 db as it ships (the fit's octave variable left unbounded, so the cubic extrapolates); freezing that variable at the fitted boundary gives 0.22/0.05/0.04/1.05/4.32/11.32/23.16; fading the correction out to zero over one octave past the span gives 0.56/2.95/9.18/20.98 at 2093 and up; and the instrument with NO mallet compensation at all gives 0.88/2.33/9.18/20.98 there -- so above about 3 khz the runaway extrapolation is the BEST of the four, because what it is tracking is `vibes`'s own collapse. 21 db of raw spread at 4186 hz is the opcode's, not this axis's, and no gain law fitted over 55-1760 hz can reach it. inside the compass the axis holds: 0.03/0.16/0.22/0.07/0.05/0.04 db at 55-1760 hz. a related consequence of the same unbounded variable, left alone for the same reason: kmdamp = 1 - 0.12*kmoctclip^2 crosses zero at 3254 hz and inverts the motor correction's sign above it, which is real but costs nothing measurable -- motor's own spread up there is 0.06-0.11 db, because what dominates at those registers is mallet.

soft.gloss: softest mallet in the safe range -- centroid 904 hz at a played 880

default.gloss: today's mallet -- centroid 956 hz at a played 880

hard.gloss: hardest mallet -- centroid 962 hz at a played 880

strikepos.note: vibes's own strike position (ipos). the centre (0.5) voices the fundamental most purely; off-centre wakes the higher bar modes -- comb contrast at 440 hz swings roughly 90 db between centre and off-centre, and centroid at 440 hz moves from about 490 hz at the centre to the mid-600s off-centre (untouched by this fit, which only sets the loudness compensation, not vibes's own ipos argument). the compensation was refit 2026-07-25 against the WHOLE NOTE, and the meter is the whole point: lco_measure.rms_db integrates 0.5-3.5 s while 89 % of this instrument's energy is gone by 0.5 s (88.98-89.30 % at every register from 55 to 1760 hz), so every earlier number for this axis described the last inaudible tenth of the decay. the fit before this one drove that window's spread to 0.003-0.071 db and, on the note a player actually hears, left strikepos 0.7 at 440 hz 2.50 db loud at the strike and 1.65 db loud over the whole note -- where the axis with NO compensation at all had been 0.36 db out. calibration is closed-loop, as mallet's is and for the same reason (vibes's kamp is not a linear multiplier on its own output above ~880 hz): for each (strikepos, register) the exc value that, applied as the real gain, reproduces the strikepos=0.5 reference's whole-note rms, by secant search against real renders -- 88 points, 8 strike positions x 11 half-octave registers 55-1760 hz, worst 0.004 db from target. the surface is rank 2 to 0.048 db, with a corner near 440 hz, so the register basis carries a hinge there, and the strike offset is scaled to kspn = (strikepos-0.5)*5 and taken to the sixth power (30 coefficients over 88 points). measured anchor spread, whole-note: 0.015/0.010/0.015/0.044/0.007/0.066 db at 55/110/220/440/880/1760 hz, against 1.547/1.445/1.056/0.356/0.513/1.451 uncorrected and 0.309/0.425/0.808/1.650/1.259/0.419 for the fit it replaces; on max-400 ms loudness 0.035/0.082/0.114/0.181/0.189/0.136 db, against 1.501/1.387/0.954/0.389/0.342/1.394 uncorrected. over the whole travel (17 positions, 8 of them off the fit grid) 0.026/0.023/0.061/0.222/0.071/0.092 db. the register variable is CLAMPED to the fitted span rather than extrapolated, which is the opposite of mallet's choice and is right for this axis because its shape is nearly flat at both ends: 0.058/0.040/0.099/0.089/0.051/0.132 db at 27.5/41.2/2093/3520/4186/7040 hz, against 1.56/1.56/1.65/1.79/1.75/1.74 uncorrected -- the unclamped quartic this replaces read 2.25 db at 7040 hz, worse than no correction. the default renders bit-identical (max|a-b| = 0.0 exactly, byte-equal, at all twelve registers), and mallet and motor are byte-identical. NOT claimed away from 44100 hz: vibes is strongly rate-dependent, and the register where the uncorrected excess collapses moves from 440 hz to 880 hz between 44100 and 96000, so the corner is the RATE's and not the 440 hz kvtl0 clamp's. at 96 khz this fit reads 0.065/0.162/0.520/0.932/0.286/1.055 db against 1.548/1.525/1.400/0.942/0.349/0.413 uncorrected -- better at four registers, level at 440 and WORSE at 1760. no 44100 hz fit can hold there; that needs its own per-rate calibration. outside the declared 0.3-0.7 range the correction is frozen, not extrapolated: kspn enters at the sixth power, and the body this replaces rendered NaN at strikepos 0 and 1 and peaked 2.23 at 0.15 against the host's 2.523 ceiling. frozen, 0..1 is finite and quiet everywhere (worst peak 0.641); strikepos 0 and 1 read about 13 dB down, which is the bar being struck at a node and is what the model should do.

default.gloss: centre -- comb 134.1 db, centroid 493 hz at a played 440

toward one edge.gloss: toward one edge -- comb 45.8 db, centroid 654 hz at a played 440

toward the other edge.gloss: toward the other edge -- comb 46.9 db, centroid 680 hz at a played 440

motor.note: the rotating-disc tremolo's depth (vibes's kvamp); rate stays fixed at the shipped 6 hz, for the same reason as the rhodes and wurlitzer. amplitude modulation at 6 hz measures about 0.001 at depth 0.0 rising to 0.032-0.033 at depth 1.0, the same at every register. loudness spread measured 0.18-0.54 db (worst at 880 hz, where the correction is deliberately damped to avoid the overshoot a full-strength correction produces there).

half speed.gloss: the discs turning slowly: a gentle pulse

full.gloss: the discs at full speed: the vibraphone's own pulse

techniques.why: accordion / harmonium / bandoneon / melodica -- a FREE reed: a tongue of metal beating in a slot, driven by bellows. Three `gbuzz` stacks, one at pitch and two spread +21 and -16 cents, so the reeds BEAT against each other -- that beat is what a musette is, and it is measured, not decorative: depth 0.04 with one reed and 0.28 with three, at 2.3 Hz. The bellows are the instrument's gesture and never hold still, so a slow lean at 0.19 Hz opens the harmonic series and pulls the reed slightly sharp together; that lean, not the beat, is what keeps a single-reed setting moving. `gbuzz` normalises to PEAK, so the closed-form `knrm` holds one loudness while the harmonic count travels: measured 0.07 dB across the whole parameter cube and 0.4 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz. Reedier and buzzier than `clarinet`, which is a cylindrical BEATING reed with only odd harmonics; this one keeps the full series (odd/even balance +5.1 dB).

musette.note: one reed or three. Above 0 two more reeds sound +21 and -16 cents away and the three BEAT: measured depth 0.01 -> 0.29 at 2.3 Hz. This is an amplitude beat, so it is deliberately almost invisible to the colour meters (centroid moves 1796 -> 1434 Hz as the beat fills in); `lco_measure.beat` is what reads it.

single.gloss: one reed, dead straight -- a harmonium, no beat at all

slight.gloss: a second reed just audible, the tone starting to shimmer

wet.gloss: three reeds full up -- the widest, most seasick tuning

press.note: how hard the bellows lean on the reed, as harmonic richness. It deepens the harmonic comb (44.0 -> 49.0 dB) rather than simply brightening: measured centroid 1513 -> 1702 Hz, loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

soft.gloss: barely leaning -- a thin, sweet, almost flute-like reed

gentle.gloss: an easy, singing tone with the buzz held back

full.gloss: the ordinary playing weight, reed clearly audible

hard.gloss: pushed -- the reed's full harmonic series, brash

forced.gloss: the bellows crushed down, the reed at its harshest

rattle.note: the reed's own mechanical noise: a `dust` puff per half cycle through a 2600 Hz resonance, rising and falling with the bellows so it is part of the note and not a separate hiss. The widest of the three axes -- centroid 585 -> 2435 Hz, comb 96.2 -> 35.4 dB, loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

clean.gloss: a pure reed tone, no mechanism audible

breathy.gloss: the slot audible under the note

rattly.gloss: the tongue clearly buzzing in its slot

wheezing.gloss: an old bellows -- as much air and clatter as tone

techniques.code:
kpress  = 0.45                              ; press: how hard the bellows lean on the reed
kmus    = 0.55                              ; musette: one reed, or three spread apart
krat    = 0.30                              ; rattle: the reed's own mechanical buzz
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 24   ; harmonics the band can hold
; The bellows are the instrument's gesture and they never hold still. This cycle
; has to drive the movement, because the musette beat cannot: at kmus=0 there is
; only one reed and nothing to beat against, and the note would then stand.
kbcy    poscil 0.5, 0.19                    ; the bellows lean and ease over ~5 s
kmul    = 0.40 + 0.38 * kpress + 0.09 * kbcy ; pressure opens the series
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kbel    = 0.0011 * kbcy                     ; the same lean pulls the reed slightly sharp
ar1     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kbel), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
ar2     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm * kmus, kf0 * 1.0122, knh, 1, kmul, giCos   ; +21 cents
ar3     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm * kmus, kf0 * 0.9908, knh, 1, kmul, giCos   ; -16 cents
knmus   = 1 / sqrt(1 + 2 * kmus * kmus)     ; detuned reeds are incoherent: power adds
abuz    dust 1.0, kf0 * 2                   ; one puff per half cycle of the reed
anz     rand 0.6, 0.71, 1
arat    reson abuz * 0.35 + anz * 0.12, 2600, 1600, 2
asig    = (ar1 + ar2 + ar3) * knmus * 2.05 \
          + arat * krat * 0.30 * (0.55 + 0.90 * (0.5 + kbcy))

ar3     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm * kmus, kf0 * 0.9908, knh, 1, kmul, giCos   ; -16 cents

techniques.why: harmonica / blues harp -- a free reed played inside cupped hands, and the hands are the point. The breath drives a `gbuzz` stack; a `reson` cavity that moves with the cupping hand sits FIXED in Hz (380 to 1830, plus a 5.1 Hz hand tremolo), because a cavity is a cavity whatever note is played -- the same reason a vowel's formants do not follow the keyboard. The air hissing past the reed plate rises and brightens with the breath cycle rather than sitting under it as a constant: a steady hiss under a pulsing reed reads as a separate noise generator, and measured, its own variance then swamped every coherent movement in the note (three of eight corners stopped moving). Level held by `balance` against a fixed 400 Hz yardstick: 0.02 dB across the parameter cube, 0.01 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz. Brighter and thinner than `free_reed`; the cavity is what distinguishes them.

cup.note: the hand closed over the shell or opened away from it: a cavity resonance from 380 Hz (closed, dark, muffled) to 1830 Hz (open, bright), with a 5.1 Hz hand tremolo on it throughout. FIXED in Hz, so it colours the same band at every pitch. Centroid 1700 -> 1922 Hz, comb 41.2 -> 37.6 dB, loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

open.gloss: hands away -- the bare reed, bright and direct

cupped.gloss: hands closed -- the hollow, vocal wah of a blues harp

press.note: how hard the breath drives the reed. Deepens the harmonic comb (38.9 -> 42.7 dB) at a nearly constant centroid, which is what a harmonica does when you blow harder -- it gets reedier, not simply brighter. Loudness constant to 0.01 dB.

soft.gloss: a light breath -- sweet and almost whistle-like

overblown.gloss: forced past the reed's comfort -- raw and edgy

breath.note: air past the reed rather than through it. The widest axis: centroid 600 -> 2227 Hz, comb 70.0 -> 31.7 dB. It rises and brightens with the breath cycle, so it moves WITH the note (coherence stays above 0.7 at every corner) instead of adding a static hiss. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

clean.gloss: pure reed, no air audible -- almost an organ

airy.gloss: the breath audible around the note

breathy.gloss: as much air as tone -- intimate, close-miked

gasping.gloss: mostly air, the pitch only just holding through it

techniques.why: bagpipe -- a cane reed chanter plus DRONES, which is the whole architecture: a `gbuzz` chanter at pitch, a tenor drone an octave down and a bass drone two octaves down, each detuned from the chanter so all three beat. Measured, the drones take the beat depth from 0.04 to 0.21 and the detune holds that depth while moving the RATE from 1.0 to 4.0 Hz. A piper's bag pressure is steady but not constant, so a 0.13 Hz arm wander opens the series slightly -- without it the note stands perfectly still wherever the drones are turned off, which is how nine of twenty-seven corners failed the movement rule before it was added. Darker than the other reeds here (centroid 571 Hz at 220, against `sax` 1696) because the drones put most of the energy two octaves below the note. Loudness 0.12 dB across the cube, 0.24 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz.

drone.note: the parallel pipes beside the chanter, an octave and two octaves down. Beat depth 0.00 -> 0.21. Centroid 876 -> 500 Hz as the low pipes fill in. What it moves is the sounding fundamental, exactly as pipes an octave and two octaves down should: f0 reads 220.0 with the drones out, 110.0 halfway and 55.0 with them full in. The comb stays deep throughout on the series each setting actually plays -- 102.5 -> 99.9 dB -- so this is not the wide comb axis it was once recorded as. It read 10.7 dB at the top only because the comb was measured on the asked 220 while the body was sounding 55, which puts a real harmonic in every valley. Power-summed (`knmix`), because detuned pipes are incoherent -- adding them as amplitudes would make this a volume control. Loudness constant to 0.10 dB.

chanter.gloss: the melody pipe alone, no drones -- a solo cane reed

one.gloss: the drones behind the chanter, present but under it

full.gloss: the ordinary balance -- drones as loud as the tune

droning.gloss: the drones dominant, the chanter riding on top

reed.note: how hard the bag pressure drives the cane reed. The brightness axis here, and a wide one: centroid 353 -> 1026 Hz. The comb barely moves with it (101.5 -> 96.7 dB), because the drones hold the low series steady whatever the chanter does -- the earlier 18.7 -> 13.4 was that series read on the asked pitch instead of the 55 Hz the body sounds. Loudness constant to 0.01 dB.

soft.gloss: an underblown reed -- woody, almost recorder-like

strong.gloss: the reed well up, the characteristic hard edge

screaming.gloss: a highland chanter at full pressure

beat.note: how far out of tune the drones sit. A RATE control, not a depth one: measured, the beat depth stays at ~0.20 while the rate goes 1.0 -> 1.7 -> 2.3 -> 3.3 -> 4.0 Hz. It therefore moves almost no colour at all (centroid 576 -> 577 Hz) and is invisible to every spectral meter; `lco_measure.beat` is what reads it. Loudness 0.10 dB.

tuned.gloss: drones dead on -- a slow 1 Hz swell, nearly still

close.gloss: a gentle 2 Hz beat, the pipes breathing together

loose.gloss: 3 Hz -- audibly untuned, the folk sound

sour.gloss: 4 Hz, the drones fighting the chanter

kdrone  = 0.60                              ; drone: the parallel pipes beside the chanter
kbeat   = 0.45                              ; beat: how far out of tune the drones sit
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 22   ; harmonics the band can hold
; A piper's bag pressure is steady, not constant -- the arm loses and regains it
; slowly, and this small wander is the only movement the chanter has of its own.
; Without it the note stands still wherever the drones are turned off.
kbag    poscil 0.5, 0.13                    ; the arm eases and leans, ~8 s
kmul    = 0.52 + 0.30 * kreed + 0.07 * kbag ; a cane reed under near-constant pressure
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kwob    poscil 0.0010, 6.3                  ; the cane reed chatters
ach     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kwob), knh, 1, kmul, giCos    ; the chanter
knhd    limit int(sr * 0.45 / (kf0 * 0.5)), 1, 22
knrd    = ((1-kmul^knhd)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knhd))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kdt     = 0.004 + 0.014 * kbeat             ; drones are never quite in tune with the chanter
ad1     gbuzz 0.17 * knrd, kf0 * 0.5 * (1 + kdt), knhd, 1, kmul, giCos    ; tenor drone, an octave down
ad2     gbuzz 0.17 * knrd, kf0 * 0.25 * (1 - kdt), knhd, 1, kmul, giCos   ; bass drone, two octaves down
knmix   = 1 / sqrt(1 + 2 * kdrone * kdrone) ; the drones beat against the chanter: power adds
asig    = (ach + (ad1 + ad2) * kdrone) * knmix * 1.95

techniques.why: saxophone -- a single beating reed on a CONICAL bore, and the cone is what separates it from `clarinet`: a cone keeps all harmonics, a cylinder keeps only the odd ones. Measured odd/even balance +4.3 dB here against `clarinet`'s +113 dB, which is the objective signature of the difference. Two `reson` formants at 900 and 1750 Hz, FIXED in Hz, are what make a saxophone shout rather than merely buzz. A 0.68 Hz breath cycle opens the series AND slides the two bore formants with it, so the note moves at every setting: written with fixed formants the colour stood still at every honk above zero, since half the output was then a filter that could not move. The reed hiss rides the same breath rather than sitting under it as a constant -- held at a fixed 0.09 it carried nearly half the measured centroid, and a saxophone tone is not half hiss. Level held by `balance` against a fixed 400 Hz yardstick: 0.00 dB across the parameter cube, 0.00 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz, and 0.01 dB across the two crossed over 162 renders.

honk.note: how much the conical bore shouts: a crossfade onto two narrow `reson` formants at 900 and 1750 Hz. Measured, the centroid falls 1491 -> 1202 Hz monotonically -- the formants concentrate the tone in the middle instead of brightening it. FIXED in Hz, so it colours the same band at every pitch. Loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

veiled.gloss: no bore emphasis -- a plain reed, almost an oboe

round.gloss: the bore just colouring the tone

vocal.gloss: the saxophone's own singing formant, clearly there

shouting.gloss: the full conical honk, midrange forward

blow.note: how hard the reed is driven. It deepens the harmonic comb (39.7 -> 43.1 dB) and more than triples the colour movement in the note (115 -> 373 Hz), at a nearly constant centroid up to three quarters of the way (1341 -> 1417 Hz) -- the two bore formants hold the colour while the series behind them fills in. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

breathy.gloss: barely speaking -- soft, subtone, close to a sine

loud.gloss: pushed, the reed's whole series audible

honking.gloss: blown as hard as the reed takes

growl.note: the player humming against the reed, as amplitude modulation at 74 Hz -- sidebands, not vibrato. Measured, the sideband energy around the harmonics goes 0.0001 -> 0.174 of the carrier energy and the harmonic comb FILLS IN from 48.7 to 32.0 dB over the lower half of the axis as the sidebands crowd between the partials, which is exactly what turns tone into rasp. Past that the hum owns the sound: the sounding fundamental becomes the hum's own 74 Hz rather than the note (f0 73.4 at an asked 220), and the comb read on THAT series is 48.1 dB, because the note and its partials are all harmonics of it. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB.

clean.gloss: no growl -- a pure reed tone

edge.gloss: a trace of grit, the tone just roughened

growl.gloss: an audible hummed rasp under the note

roar.gloss: full-throated, the pitch buried in rasp

techniques.code:
kblow   = 0.45                              ; blow: how hard the reed is driven
khonk   = 0.50                              ; honk: how much the conical bore shouts
kgrowl  = 0.15                              ; growl: the hummed note that turns tone to rasp
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 26   ; harmonics the band can hold
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.68                    ; the breath opens and closes, ~1.5 s a lung
kemb    poscil 1.0, 5.3                     ; the embouchure is never still, and stiffness IS colour
kmul    = 0.42 + 0.30 * kblow + 0.26 * kbr + 0.028 * kemb
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kgr     poscil 1.0, 74.0                    ; the hummed note, a growl not a tremolo
klip    = 0.0012 * kemb                     ; the same motion, two cents of it in pitch
asr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + klip), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
asr     = asr * (1 + 0.60 * kgrowl * kgr)   ; humming AGAINST the reed: sidebands at +-74 Hz
; The bore formant is not a fixed filter: the player's throat and the reed channel
; are part of it, so it slides with the same breath that drives the reed. Without
; this the shout pins the colour in place at every honk above zero.
ahk     reson asr, 900 * (1 + 0.10 * kbr), 260, 1
ahk2    reson asr, 1750 * (1 + 0.17 * kbr), 400, 1
; Reed hiss rises and falls with the breath that makes it -- it is not a fixed
; pedestal. Held at a level it cannot pin the colour with: at 0.09 it carried
; nearly half the measured centroid, and a saxophone tone is not half hiss.
anz     rand 0.5, 0.37, 1
abr     reson anz, 1900, 700, 1
khs     = 0.042 * (0.35 + 1.30 * (0.5 + kbr))
amix    = asr * (1 - 0.80 * khonk) + (ahk * 2.10 + ahk2 * 0.95) * khonk + abr * khs
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: oboe / bassoon / shawm / zurna -- two blades of cane beating against each other, which is the narrowest, most pungent way to make a reed sound. A `gbuzz` stack with an unusually complete harmonic series (comb contrast 70.6 dB against the rest of the reed family's 15-46 dB, though a bare `vco2` waveform reads higher still) through a narrow `reson` cavity whose centre moves 480 Hz (bassoon-deep) to 1580 Hz (oboe-piercing), FIXED in Hz. A 0.23 Hz breath cycle opens the series, which is what makes it move: measured coherence +1.00 at the defaults, and every one of the 27 parameter corners moves. Darker at its default than `sax` (674 vs 1696 Hz) but far more combed -- the pungency is in the completeness of the series, not in the brightness. Level held by `balance` against a fixed 400 Hz yardstick: 0.08 dB across the cube, 0.03 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz.

throat.note: which double reed it is: the bore formant from 480 Hz (bassoon) to 1580 Hz (oboe), plus a weaker one at 2.15x it. FIXED in Hz. Centroid 544 -> 718 Hz, monotone. The formant's absolute prominence FALLS as it rises (the band around it goes 36 % to 2 % of the energy) because a 1580 Hz formant over a 220 Hz note has fewer harmonics to work with -- that is the physics, not a defect. Loudness 0.01 dB.

bassoon.gloss: the deep, hollow, slightly comic low double reed

cor anglais.gloss: between the two -- plaintive and covered

oboe.gloss: the bright, nasal, penetrating orchestral reed

shawm.gloss: the shrillest -- a zurna or suona, outdoors and loud

press.note: how hard the two blades are driven, and the widest axis here: centroid 472 -> 1218 Hz with the colour movement in the note rising from 37 to 172 Hz alongside it. Loudness constant to 0.00 dB through the closed-form `gbuzz` normalisation.

soft.gloss: the blades barely open -- hollow and dark

full.gloss: ordinary playing weight, the reed clearly speaking

pressed.gloss: driven hard -- the piercing double-reed cry

forced.gloss: as much as the blades take, shrill

bite.note: how narrowly the blades pinch the air: the crossfade onto the cavity formants. Measured, the 400-2000 Hz band goes 41 % to 55 % of the energy, monotonically. The centroid dips and returns (717 -> 671 -> 690 Hz) because the formant pulls energy inward from both ends rather than upward -- the band fraction is the honest reading of this axis. Loudness constant to 0.02 dB.

loose.gloss: an open embouchure -- broad and unfocused

pinched.gloss: tight -- the tone concentrated and reedy

biting.gloss: clamped down, all cavity and no body

kpress  = 0.50                              ; press: how hard the two blades are driven
kthroat = 0.55                              ; throat: bassoon-deep, or oboe-piercing
kbite   = 0.45                              ; bite: how narrowly the blades pinch the air

kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.23                    ; the breath opens and closes over ~4 s
