knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kwob    poscil 0.0014, 5.9                  ; the blades chatter a few times a second
adr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kwob), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
kcf     = 480 + 1100 * kthroat              ; bore formant, FIXED in Hz: 480 bassoon .. 1580 oboe
afm     reson adr, kcf, 230, 1              ; the reed cavity's shout, narrow
afm2    reson adr, kcf * 2.15, 480, 1       ; the second, weaker one
amix    = adr * (1 - 0.88 * kbite) + (afm * 2.30 + afm2 * 1.10) * kbite
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: mbira / kalimba -- a plucked steel tongue over a resonating board, and the one thing every additive imitation of it gets wrong is the overtone spacing. A uniform clamped-free bar has partials at 1 : 6.267 : 17.55, which is why a `mode` bank built from the textbook ratios sounds like a tuning fork and not like an mbira. A real tine is FORGED THINNER at the struck end, and that taper pulls the overtones down: the second partial sits at 6.27x with no taper, 5.70x at `taper` 0.22 (a commercial kalimba), 5.10x at 0.45 (the measured mbira dzavadzimu, 1 : 5 : 14) and 3.67x when hammered right down. Three `mode` resonators on a continuous `rand` exciter, so a held note stands rather than decaying -- and that standing is what makes movement hard here: at Q 520-900 the bank's centroid wanders 750 Hz on its own, which is a class the movement meter cannot resolve, so a deliberate motion has to stand clear of the wander to count. The player's hand does it, breathing on the board at 0.23 Hz and reaching the TINE and not only the caps -- as a spectral tilt, damping the first mode while freeing the third, plus the brightness of the thumb's own contact noise. Both together, because with only the tilt the interior taper values the 3-step gate never visits still read as standing still. Two things nothing else in the library has: the machachara -- loose bottle caps on the soundboard, a `dust` bed of small metal impacts that is emphatically not a tone -- and the deze, the calabash the whole board sits in. Loudness 0.13 dB across the cube, 0.81 dB crossed with the register, register tilt 0.69 dB.

taper.note: how far the tine is forged down towards its tip, which is the instrument's real timbre control. Centroid 2304 -> 1372 Hz, and the comb contrast is deliberately NOT monotone across the four anchors (29.9, 20.3, 26.4, 27.7 dB) -- as the partials slide they pass through and away from exact harmonic positions, so the tone alternates between hollow and clangorous. (This note carried five figures for four anchors until 2026-07-25, none of which reproduced; these are measured at 220 Hz.) Loudness 0.11 dB.

ideal bar.gloss: a uniform bar -- 6.3x and 17.6x, glassy and remote

kalimba.gloss: a commercial kalimba tine, 5.70x -- a 0.8 tip/root ratio

buzz.note: the machachara: how many caps are on the board and how loose. Centroid 1753 -> 2082 Hz with the comb barely touched (29.4 -> 28.9 dB), which is the signature of adding a non-pitched bed rather than changing the tone. The impact rate rises 320 -> 840 a second alongside. It does not touch the colour movement in the note (2019 Hz at every setting): the hand breathes on the board at 0.23 Hz whatever this is set to, and that breathing reaches the TINE, so no setting can make the instrument stand still. It used to reach only the caps, which this axis scales, so at 0 the movement was multiplied out and what remained was the bank's own noise wander. Loudness 0.00 dB.

clean.gloss: the caps taken off -- bare tines

shells.gloss: a few caps, the usual rattle

swarming.gloss: loose caps everywhere, more buzz than note

gourd.note: the deze the board sits inside, as a Helmholtz cavity from 340 Hz down to 175 Hz -- DOWNWARD, because a wider cavity resonates lower and the gain rises with the axis, so value 1 is the big calabash. Fixed in Hz, and that is the whole character of it: a box only answers notes near its own pitch, so this axis is strong in the register the deze lives in and nearly silent above it. Measured 0 -> 1: at 165 Hz centroid 1473 -> 1345 and comb 27.2 -> 29.2 dB; at 110 Hz 1067 -> 1003 and 24.0 -> 25.0; at 220 Hz only 1850 -> 1838 and 28.5 -> 28.1; at 440 Hz nothing at all. A small axis at the reference register BY PHYSICS, not by accident -- the earlier reading of a big calabash darkening every note came from the mapping running the wrong way. Loudness within 0.18 dB everywhere.

board only.gloss: no gourd at all -- thin and papery

big calabash.gloss: a wide 40 cm gourd, deep and boxy

techniques.code:
ktaper  = 0.55                              ; taper: a thick ideal bar, or a forged mbira tine
kbuzz   = 0.35                              ; buzz: the bottle caps rattling on the board
kgourd  = 0.45                              ; gourd: the calabash the whole board sits in
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A real tine is thinner at the struck end, and that taper is what pulls its
; overtones DOWN from the textbook clamped-free bar: 1 : 6.267 : 17.55 ideal,
; 1 : 5.7 : 15.6 at a 0.8 tip/root ratio (kalimba, measured 5.30-5.86),
; 1 : 5.11 : 13.47 at 0.6 -- which lands on the measured mbira dzavadzimu 1 : 5 : 14.
; Those two are tip/root ratios and NOT `taper` values: the code reaches them at
; taper 0.22 and 0.45, which is where the anchors of that name sit.
kr2     = 6.267 - 2.60 * ktaper
kr3     = 17.55 - 9.00 * ktaper
; The player's hand breathes on the board at 0.23 Hz, and it reaches the TINE, not
; only the caps. It used to reach `acap` alone -- which is scaled by `buzz` -- so at
; buzz 0 the movement the note promised "whatever this is set to" was multiplied out,
; and what was left was the mode bank's own noise wander: replacing the LFO with a
; constant changed the measured motion by 0.1 Hz out of 605. A hand pressing the board
; shifts which partials the tines give up, so it is a spectral tilt and not a level:
; the first mode is damped as the third is freed, which `balance` then holds level.
; Two mechanisms, because one was not enough to be SEEN: three `mode` resonators at
; Q 520-900 on a noise exciter wander on their own -- with the hand frozen, 833 Hz of
; centroid span and 1695 Hz of fast motion -- which is the class `moves`
; documents as beyond it, and a deliberate motion has to stand clear of that wander or
; it reads as more of the same. With the tilt alone at a modest depth, taper 0.70 and
; 0.75 -- interior values the 3-step gate never visits -- still measured coherence
; 0.10-0.15. Both together: every taper from 0.0 to 1.0 moves, worst coherence 0.39,
; and the loudness cost is 0.13 dB.
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.23
arw     rand 0.05, 0.5, 1                   ; a continuous exciter: a held note stands
aex     tone arw, 600 + 5000 * (0.5 + kbr)  ; the thumb's contact brightening and dulling
am1     mode aex * (1 - 0.90 * (0.5 + kbr)), kf0, 900
am2     mode aex * 0.62, kf0 * kr2, 700
am3     mode aex * 0.24 * (1 + 6.00 * (0.5 + kbr)), kf0 * kr3, 520
; the machachara: loose caps on the soundboard, a bed of small metal impacts and
; not a tone, breathing with the same hand
adu     dust 1.0, 320 + 520 * kbuzz
acap    reson adu * 0.30, 3200 + 900 * (0.5 + kbr), 2200, 1
; the deze: a 40 cm calabash is a Helmholtz cavity around 160-340 Hz, FIXED in Hz.
; DOWNWARD in the axis: a wider cavity resonates LOWER (f ~ (c/2pi)*sqrt(A/VL)), and the
; gain below is `adz * kgourd`, so value 1 is the big calabash and the mapping cannot be
; renamed to suit. It read `175 + 130 * kgourd` until 2026-07-25 -- the big gourd got the
; HIGH cavity -- and no meter caught it because the gourd's gain rises with the axis too,
; so the audible direction came out right for the wrong reason.
kdz     = 340 - 165 * kgourd
adz     reson (am1 + am2), kdz, kdz * 0.55, 1
amix    = (am1 + am2 + am3) * 1.0 + adz * kgourd * 0.85 + acap * kbuzz * 1.90
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

; overtones DOWN from the textbook clamped-free bar: 1 : 6.267 : 17.55 ideal,
; 1 : 5.7 : 15.6 at a 0.8 tip/root ratio (kalimba, measured 5.30-5.86),
; 1 : 5.11 : 13.47 at 0.6 -- which lands on the measured mbira dzavadzimu 1 : 5 : 14.
; Those two are tip/root ratios and NOT `taper` values: the code reaches them at
; taper 0.22 and 0.45, which is where the anchors of that name sit.

kr3     = 17.55 - 9.00 * ktaper
; The player's hand breathes on the board at 0.23 Hz, and it reaches the TINE, not
; only the caps. It used to reach `acap` alone -- which is scaled by `buzz` -- so at
; buzz 0 the movement the note promised "whatever this is set to" was multiplied out,
; and what was left was the mode bank's own noise wander: replacing the LFO with a
; constant changed the measured motion by 0.1 Hz out of 605. A hand pressing the board
; shifts which partials the tines give up, so it is a spectral tilt and not a level:
; the first mode is damped as the third is freed, which `balance` then holds level.
; Two mechanisms, because one was not enough to be SEEN: three `mode` resonators at
; Q 520-900 on a noise exciter wander on their own -- with the hand frozen, 833 Hz of
; centroid span and 1695 Hz of fast motion -- which is the class `moves`
; documents as beyond it, and a deliberate motion has to stand clear of that wander or
; it reads as more of the same. With the tilt alone at a modest depth, taper 0.70 and
; 0.75 -- interior values the 3-step gate never visits -- still measured coherence
; 0.10-0.15. Both together: every taper from 0.0 to 1.0 moves, worst coherence 0.39,

am3     mode aex * 0.24 * (1 + 6.00 * (0.5 + kbr)), kf0 * kr3, 520

; not a tone, breathing with the same hand
adu     dust 1.0, 320 + 520 * kbuzz

techniques.why: jaw harp / khomus / morsing -- a steel tongue plucked against the teeth, and the clearest case in the library of a source that never changes while the sound changes completely. The tongue gives one dense harmonic comb (68.8 dB contrast) at one pitch; everything the player does is done with the mouth cavity in front of it. That is measurable and is the entry's objective signature: the `vowel` axis moves the centroid 799 -> 1533 Hz while the comb stays constant to 1.0 dB. A filter that shifts the colour and leaves the series untouched is what a resonating mouth IS, and it is why this instrument belongs in a library the author reads for idioms. Loudness 0.03 dB across the cube, 0.12 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.07 dB over five octaves.

vowel.note: the shape of the mouth in front of the tongue, from `oo` to `ee`. Centroid 799 -> 1533 Hz with the comb contrast constant to 1.0 dB and loudness to 0.02 dB. The formants are FIXED in Hz -- a mouth does not transpose with the note -- so the same vowel colours every pitch. The colour movement is LARGEST at the dark closed vowel and smallest at the bright one (399 -> 70 Hz), because the mouth's own travel is a fixed number of hertz: the same swing is a large fraction of an 840 Hz band and a small one of a 2290 Hz band, and down there it also sweeps across a denser part of the series.

ah.gloss: the mouth wide, the classic twang

sweep.note: how far the mouth travels while the note sounds, which is what makes a jaw harp talk. This is the entry's motion axis: the colour movement in the note doubles, 155 -> 307 Hz, at an almost unchanged centroid (1112 -> 1190 Hz) and comb (0.9 dB). It has a floor -- the mouth is never still even at 0, so no setting stops the instrument moving -- and the floor is +-85 Hz rather than +-55 because the movement bound is in CENTS: at the bright vowel 55 Hz of a 2290 Hz band is 58 cents, and three corners measured as standing still while the closed vowel carried the axis. Loudness 0.01 dB.

drifting.gloss: a slow easing of the vowel

wailing.gloss: the mouth swept end to end, a talking wow

pluck.note: how hard the tongue is struck, as the reach of the comb rather than a level. Centroid 1148 -> 1240 Hz and comb 69.4 -> 65.1 dB: harder plucking fills IN the spectrum between the harmonics (the tongue rattles against the frame) instead of adding brightness. Loudness 0.00 dB -- it is not a velocity control; the synth owns that.

snapping.gloss: flicked hard -- the frame buzzing with it

techniques.code:
kvowel  = 0.45                              ; vowel: the mouth from 'ooh' to 'eee'
ksweep  = 0.55                              ; sweep: how far the mouth travels inside one note
kpluck  = 0.30                              ; pluck: the finger against the steel tongue
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; The tine's pitch never changes; what the player plays is which HARMONIC of it the
; mouth picks out. So the source is a dense comb and the melody is a filter.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 42   ; a low harp reaches into the 40s
kmul    = 0.86                              ; a steel tongue through a narrow slit: bright
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
atn     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The vocal tract's second formant is the one that does the work: measured across
; 76 speakers it runs 840 Hz ('ooh') to 2290 Hz ('eee'). FIXED in Hz -- a mouth is
; a mouth whatever the tine is tuned to, and that is the whole instrument.
; A mouth is never still, so the travel has a floor `sweep` adds to rather than
; being its only source -- at sweep=0 the note would otherwise stand.
; The floor is +-85 Hz and not +-55. At +-55 it was enough at the dark end and not at
; the bright one: `ee` puts the band at 2290 Hz, where 55 Hz is 58 cents and the note
; measured as standing still at three corners. The floor is in Hz and the bound is in
; cents, so the closed vowel was carrying it. The `sweep` axis is untouched by the
; change -- it still moves the colour 155 -> 307 Hz across its range.
kmo     poscil 0.5, 0.41                    ; the mouth walking the band: this is the melody
kf2     = 840 + 1450 * kvowel + (170 + 560 * ksweep) * kmo
kf1     = 270 + 460 * kvowel                ; the first formant follows, lower and weaker
af2     reson atn, kf2, kf2 * 0.11, 1
af1     reson atn, kf1, kf1 * 0.16, 1
; the pluck itself: a steel tongue released by a finger, a few times a second
adu     dust 1.0, 3 + 13 * kpluck
apl     reson adu * 0.22, 1500 + 1700 * (0.5 + kmo), 1500, 1  ; the plucks brighten as the mouth opens
amix    = af2 * 2.30 + af1 * 0.85 + atn * 0.10 + apl * kpluck * 0.40
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: didgeridoo / yidaki -- a lip-driven wooden drone, and it is in the library for one specific reason: its harmonics are EXACTLY harmonic even though the bore is a hollowed branch of no particular shape. The lips stay shut for a good part of every cycle, and that periodic closure -- not the bore -- sets the series. So the substrate's `gbuzz` is exactly right and a shaped-bore model would be wrong. What a player actually plays is the vocal tract's IMPEDANCE: where it is high the flow through the lips is choked and the radiated sound has a HOLE. That needs a real band-reject and not a subtracted bandpass -- `butterbr` measures -50 dB at its centre, while subtracting a `reson` moves its own band by 0.2 dB and `areson` is literally that same subtraction, with a shallow dip 200 Hz below where it claims to be. So: one open band with a real choke either side. Because the open band has to carry the tone, what the chain applies is a FORMANT rather than a pair of holes -- measured on white noise through the same chain, -1.7 / +9.2 / -3.3 dB at 1320 / 1650 / 1980 Hz, which is 10.9 and 12.5 dB of peak-to-shoulder contrast. Let the drone through unfiltered instead and the holes go -10.7 and -12.3 dB deep while `tongue` moves 14 Hz of colour: the depth and the axis are one trade, and the formant is the side of it that leaves a control. All three sit FIXED in Hz -- a mouth does not transpose. Humming into the drone is MULTIPLICATIVE, so it makes m*f1 +- n*f2 sidebands rather than a tremolo, and that is what turns the tone to a growl: the comb goes 70.4 dB (a clean harmonic drone) to 14.6 dB (rasp) across `voice`, the widest of this entry's three axes and the third widest in the library -- `pwm`'s rate spans 73.2 dB and `free_reed`'s rattle 60.8, each read against its own fundamental. The open band has to CARRY the tone rather than garnish it -- at a mix that let the unfiltered drone through, the two real chokes cancelled `tongue` to 14 Hz of colour, because moving the whole pattern up moves nothing net while the energy sits below it untouched. Loudness 0.02 dB across the cube, 0.08 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.03 dB.

voice.note: humming a second note into the drone, the way a player growls a didgeridoo. Multiplicative, so it does not sit on top of the tone but multiplies it into sidebands: comb contrast 70.4 -> 16.9 dB over the lower half of the axis and centroid 1068 -> 2523 Hz across it, the widest of this entry's three by both (and third in the library by comb, behind `pwm`'s rate and `free_reed`'s rattle). The comb is read against the body's OWN fundamental at each setting, which is not the asked pitch, and past about three quarters of the axis the sidebands halve that fundamental -- so the reading jumps to 46.3 and then 43.7 dB on the new series rather than continuing down. The axis end is 43.7; the 14.6 dB minimum sits at the `growl` anchor, 0.65. The hum runs at 97 Hz FIXED, so its sidebands stay where they are while the drone moves with the keyboard -- which is what a voice inside an instrument does, and the beat meter reads that 97 Hz back at a depth of 0.04 -> 0.54. Loudness 0.00 dB.

a hum.gloss: a voice just audible in it

roaring.gloss: hummed hard -- more rasp than note

tongue.note: where the tongue puts the tract resonance, from a closed low vowel to an open high one. The open band's centre sweeps 1150 -> 2150 Hz and the two chokes track it at 0.80 and 1.20 of that. Centroid 1630 -> 1845 Hz -- a much smaller number than the band's own travel, because a formant that moves trades one part of the series for another rather than adding anything, and because the tract only shapes the region above 1 kHz while the drone keeps its weight below. Comb 0.1 dB, loudness 0.02 dB.

open.gloss: the mouth open, the band up

wide open.gloss: the tract wide -- bright and shouting

breath.note: circular breathing, as a pressure pulse and not a level pulse. While the cheeks push, the pressure at the lips falls, so the comb shortens and the tone dulls once or twice a second -- the sound never stops, which is the whole point of the technique. Written as an amplitude pulse this axis moved 8 Hz of colour and 3 Hz of motion, i.e. it was a knob that did nothing while quietly modulating loudness; as a pressure pulse it moves the colour movement in the note 91 -> 481 Hz, a factor of five, at 0.00 dB of loudness and 0.1 dB of comb.

surging.gloss: hard circular breathing, the drone heaving

techniques.code:
ktongue = 0.50                              ; tongue: where the mouth chokes the sound
kvoice  = 0.30                              ; voice: humming into the drone
kbreath = 0.40                              ; breath: the pulse of circular breathing
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; The drone is EXACTLY harmonic even though the bore is not, because the lips stay
; shut for a good part of every cycle. So: a dense harmonic comb, then the mouth.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 30
; Circular breathing does not make the drone louder and softer -- the point of it
; is that the sound never stops. What changes is the PRESSURE at the lips while the
; cheeks push: it falls, so the comb shortens and the tone dulls, once or twice a
; second. Written as a level pulse this was a loudness control that moved 8 Hz of
; colour, which is to say a knob that did nothing.
kbp     poscil 0.5, 1.7
kmul    = 0.80 - 0.17 * kbreath * (0.5 + kbp)
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
adr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; What a player plays is the vocal tract's IMPEDANCE: where it is high, the flow
; through the lips is choked and the radiated sound has a HOLE there. A hole needs a
; real band-reject: `butterbr` measures -50 dB at its centre, where the two ways of
; faking one do not. Subtracting a `reson` -- which is what this body did -- moves its
; own band by 0.2 dB, and `areson` is literally that same subtraction (measured
; identical to the dB), with a shallow -3.5 dB dip that sits 200 Hz BELOW its stated
; centre. Neither notches. The old chain (`ffde6188`) subtracted two `reson` bands at
; kfc * 0.80 and kfc * 1.24, and neither landed: swept on white noise through the
; filters alone, its upper trough is deepest at kfc * 1.30, a hundred hertz past where
; it was aimed, and at kfc * 1.24 itself it is shallower still. How much shallower is
; deliberately not quoted -- that depends on the mix and on `balance`, and three
; reconstructions of it have given three different numbers.
; Now one open band with a real choke either side -- and because the open band has to
; carry the tone (see the mix below), what the chain applies is a FORMANT and not a
; pair of holes: measured on white noise through the same chain, -1.7 / +9.2 / -3.3 dB
; at 1320 / 1650 / 1980 Hz, so 10.9 and 12.5 dB of peak-to-shoulder contrast. At a
; mix that let the drone through unfiltered the holes are -10.7 and -12.3 dB deep,
; and `tongue` then moves 14 Hz of colour: the depth and the axis are the same trade.
; The tongue never stops moving, and it has to travel far enough to be heard at the
; TOP of its own axis: at +-210 Hz the band swept 1940-2360 Hz, where a 220 Hz drone
; has barely any energy left, so `breath 0, tongue 1, voice 0` measured 21 Hz of travel
; and stood still. +-350 Hz crosses three harmonics there instead of one.
ktg     poscil 0.5, 0.37
kfc     = 1150 + 1000 * ktongue + 350 * ktg
achk    butterbr adr, kfc * 0.80, kfc * 0.30    ; the flow choked below the open band
achk    butterbr achk, kfc * 1.20, kfc * 0.42   ; and above it
apk     reson adr, kfc, kfc * 0.11, 1           ; the band the tongue opens
; humming against the drone is MULTIPLICATIVE, so it makes m*f1 +- n*f2 sidebands
khm     poscil 1.0, 97.0
; The open band has to CARRY the tone, not garnish it. With the through path at 0.80
; the two real chokes cancelled the `tongue` axis to 14 Hz of colour -- moving the
; whole pattern up moves nothing net while most of the energy sits below it, untouched.
; At 0.40/2.80 the fundamental is still the loudest partial and the band stands +5.4
; and +3.5 dB over its two neighbours, which is what a didgeridoo spectrum looks like.
amix    = (achk * 0.40 + apk * 2.80) * (1 + 0.55 * kvoice * khm)
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: overtone singing / sygyt -- one voice producing a melody out of its own harmonics, and the mechanism is specific enough to be worth an entry: the singer merges the second and third vocal formants into a SINGLE very narrow resonance and tunes it ONTO one harmonic of a dense buzz, so that harmonic alone is let through as a whistle above the drone. Two things are needed for that to be audible and both were missing at first. The window must SNAP to a harmonic -- left sliding it sat between two for most of every cycle and picked neither, measuring 6.8 dB BELOW its own neighbours. And the window must be NARROWER than the harmonic spacing, which at the bottom of the keyboard it was not: at 55 Hz it sat 152 Hz wide across a 55 Hz spacing with three harmonics inside it, and 26 of 162 corners fell under the +7 dB the entry exists for, three of them negative. Bounded by the spacing, the picked harmonic stands +10.2 to +41.4 dB with the melody frozen and +9.1 to +37.7 with it running over its neighbours over the whole cube and the whole keyboard, none under +7 -- covering the 15-35 dB measured on Tuvan singers. A lift against the drone's roll-off (a `gbuzz` falls kmul per harmonic, so the 8th to 12th overtone starts 13 to 18 dB under the 2nd) adds 3.9 to 5.1 dB on top of that. It is also where this entry's one open defect is: the lift changes the picked harmonic's LEVEL as the melody steps, so the worst corner of the cube travels 6.66 dB inside a single held note, which §4 does not allow. Every constant tried moves that number rather than removing it (see the code), so it needs a decision about the mechanism. Across `press` the centroid travels 356 Hz and the comb contrast falls 57.1 -> 50.3 -> 42.9 -> 32.1 dB, a span of 25.0 dB -- so this is NOT an example of colour without source change, which is what this entry claimed until 2026-07-25 on a figure of 2.1 dB. The `press` note had it right all along: a pressed voice has more harmonics for the window to find. What does change; only which harmonic escapes. Loudness 0.21 dB at its worst axis, 0.34 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.13 dB.

select.note: which harmonic the merged formant sits on, which is the melody the style is for. Centroid 1301 -> 2267 Hz. The window snaps to a harmonic, so this axis picks one and does not land between two: at 220 Hz it walks roughly the 5th to the 11th. Below a fundamental of about 330 Hz the resonance is FIXED in Hz and the drone tracks the keyboard, so which harmonic speaks changes with the note as it does for a singer; above that there is no harmonic left inside a vocal 1.0-2.4 kHz window at all, and it holds at the third rather than collapsing onto the fundamental. Loudness 0.21 dB.

low harmonic.gloss: just above the drone -- barely separate from it

high harmonic.gloss: far up the series -- a thin pure whistle

focus.note: how tightly the two formants are merged, as the Q of the resonance: 9 wide open to 45 at full focus. Almost no centroid change (1688 -> 1844 Hz) and a modest, non-monotone comb change (47.9 / 45.1 / 49.1 / 50.1 dB across the anchors, a 7.0 dB span), but the colour movement in the note goes 188 -> 310 Hz -- a narrow window makes the same stepping melody audible as a moving whistle, where a wide one averages it away. This is a motion control that looks nearly inert to a colour meter, which is the reason both are reported. Loudness 0.01 dB.

khoomei.gloss: the softer style, harmonic and drone together

sygyt.gloss: the whistling style, harmonic clearly separate

whistling.gloss: as narrow as it goes -- a flute over a drone

press.note: how pressed the voice is, which fills the buzz the formant has to work with. Centroid moves 299 Hz and the colour movement in the note 114 Hz, at 2.1 dB of comb across the whole axis -- a pressed voice has more harmonics for the window to find, not a different spectrum shape. The whistle's own contrast rises gently along it: +10.6, +12.3, +12.9 dB over its neighbours at 110 Hz, and flat within a dB at 220 and 880. Loudness 0.18 dB.

strained.gloss: pushed hard -- rasping, every harmonic there

techniques.code:
kselect = 0.45                              ; select: which overtone the mouth picks out
kfocus  = 0.60                              ; focus: how far the neighbours are pushed down
kpress  = 0.45                              ; press: an open throat, or the pressed drone
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; Sygyt: one drone, and ONE of its overtones standing far above its neighbours.
; Measured on Tuvan singers, the reinforced overtone is the 8th to the 12th and the
; two either side of it are 15-35 dB down, the next pair 35-65 dB. The mechanism is
; linear filtering: the second and third formants MERGE into one very narrow peak.
; No subharmonics -- that is what separates sygyt from kargyraa.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 24
kmul    = 0.62 + 0.30 * kpress              ; a pressed drone carries more overtones
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kjt     poscil 0.0009, 5.3                  ; a voice is never perfectly steady
adrone  gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + kjt), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The merged formant sits FIXED in Hz, between 1.0 and 2.4 kHz, so WHICH overtone
; it picks depends on the note -- exactly as it does for a singer.
; A singer TUNES the merged formant ONTO a harmonic -- that is how one overtone comes
; to stand out instead of the window falling between two -- and walks it in HARMONIC
; steps, which is why sygyt melodies are stepped and not glides. So the window snaps.
; Left sliding continuously it sat between harmonics for most of every cycle and picked
; neither: measured with the melody frozen, the aimed-at harmonic stood 6.8 dB BELOW its
; own neighbours at select 0. Snapped, and with the window narrower than the harmonic
; spacing, it stands +10.2 to +41.4 dB above them over all 162 corners of the cube and
; the keyboard, none under +7 -- which covers the 15-35 dB the note above cites. That is
; the whole note read at once with the melody frozen; read as the median of 0.25 s
; instants with the melody running it is +9.1 to +37.7, and still none under +7. Both
; methods belong here because a whistle that STEPS between harmonics is smeared by a
; whole-note FFT, and quoting one figure without its window is what let two passes over
; this entry disagree.
;
; The FLOOR is the awkward case, and it is honest about a physical impossibility: above
; a fundamental of about 330 Hz there is no harmonic left inside a vocal 1.0-2.4 kHz
; window at all -- an overtone singer's f0 is 70-400 Hz, and the keyboard goes far
; past that. Pinned at the 2nd, 27 of 27 corners stood still at 1760 Hz and 9 of 27 at
; 880. Held at the 3rd instead, the window has room to walk at every register and
; nothing is static. Below 330 Hz the floor never bites and the formant is fixed in Hz
; as a real tract is; above it, it tracks the note, because there is nothing else there.
; 0.55 Hz and not 0.31 -- and the reason is musical, not measured, which is worth saying
; because it was once the other way round. On an earlier body 0.31 Hz read as wander;
; on this one both rates move and by almost the same amount (travel 220 vs 215 Hz,
; coherence 0.874 vs 0.888), so the measurement no longer decides it. 0.55 stays
; because a sygyt melody is quicker than one step per three seconds. +-0.9 harmonics,
; so it always steps.
kmv     poscil 0.5, 0.55
kna     = (1000 + 1400 * kselect) / kf0     ; the harmonic the vowel aims at
kn      limit round(max(kna, 3) + 1.8 * kmv), 2, knh
kfm     = kf0 * kn
; `limit`ed away from zero: at kfocus 1.2366 the bracket crosses zero and `reson` gets
; a zero bandwidth, which is NaN out. The host cannot send more than 1, but this body
; is read as an idiom and copied.
; A window WIDER than the harmonic spacing cannot pick one harmonic out of the
; series, whatever its gain -- and at the bottom of the keyboard it was: at 55 Hz
; the window sits at the 24th harmonic, so 0.115 * kfm is 152 Hz against a 55 Hz
; spacing, and three harmonics stood inside it. Measured, 26 of 162 corners fell
; under the +7 dB this entry is FOR, the worst of them at +0.99 dB -- a harmonic level
; with its own neighbours, which is no whistle at all. (An earlier count claimed three
; were NEGATIVE. Nothing in the cube is, by either window: +0.99 is the floor frozen and
; +1.69 running.) Bounded by the spacing: 0 of 162, worst corner +10.2 dB. (The MEASUREMENT
; had to be fixed first: searching harmonics 3..knh for the best contrast excludes the
; top of the series, which is exactly where the window sits at 55 Hz, so a genuine
; +19 dB whistle at the 24th read as -0.5 dB. Search to Nyquist instead.)
kbw     limit kfm * (0.115 - 0.093 * kfocus), kfm * 0.020, min(kfm * 0.200, kf0 * 0.90)
; A `gbuzz` drone falls kmul per harmonic, so the 8th to 12th overtone -- the ones sygyt
; is ABOUT -- start 13 to 18 dB below the 2nd. A narrow formant in a real tract has high
; gain; this is that gain, cancelling the roll-off at whichever harmonic the window
; sits on. What it is NOT is the difference between audible and inaudible: with the
; window bounded by the spacing the whistle already stands +12.1 to +22.2 dB over its
; neighbours with no lift at all, and the lift adds 3.9 to 5.1 dB of that -- measured
; across `select` at 220 Hz. What it also does is move the level as the melody steps,
; which is the open problem recorded at the ceiling below.
; The ceiling is where a held note PUMPS, and it is left at 12 because nothing else
; measured better. Each step of the melody moves the picked harmonic's level
; wherever the lift cannot follow the roll-off, and `balance`'s 1 Hz tracker chases
; the step train instead of removing it: measured over the whole cube and keyboard,
; the worst corner travels 6.66 dB inside one held note, which is loudness moving
; inside a standing tone. Raising the ceiling to 30 takes the corner it was first
; found at (`press` 0, `select` 0.45, 220 Hz) from 6.08 dB to 1.03 -- and moves the
; worst case rather than removing it: 6.75 dB elsewhere, 6 corners of 162 over 5 dB
; against 5 before. Removing the lift outright is worse still (8.47 dB, and one
; corner's whistle drops to +6.9 dB). Bounding `kn` by where the lift reaches was tried
; too and measured worse than either, but the variant is not written down precisely
; enough to rebuild, so no figure for it is quoted here.
; The lift is what turns the step into a level change --
; with it off the level holds to 0.67 dB at that corner -- so this needs a decision
; about the mechanism and not another constant. Recorded in LCO_PARAM_AUDIT.md.
klift   limit kmul ^ (1 - kn), 1, 12
am1     reson adrone, kfm, kbw, 1
am2     reson am1, kfm, kbw, 1              ; twice, for the skirts the merge gives
af1     reson adrone, 520, 190, 1           ; the first formant, left where it is
amix    = am2 * 3.10 * klift + am1 * 0.75 + af1 * 0.55 + adrone * 0.08
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: cicada -- and the reason it is worth an entry is that a cicada has no voice at all. Each rib of the tymbal plate BUCKLES, each buckling is one impulse, and the RATE of the train is what is heard as pitch. Published rates run about 100-250 bucklings a second (Bennet-Clark & Young 1992, J. Exp. Biol. 173:123: ~230/s in Cyclochila australasiae), which puts the train's fundamental at 100-250 Hz -- NOT the 329-660 Hz this note used to claim, which is 3x the rate and cannot follow from it. The audible energy is somewhere else again: it sits in the sac band below, near 4.3 kHz. So the rate is the pitch and the sac is the loudness, and the two are decades apart. So the source is a pulse train -- a harmonic series -- and not an oscillator, and because a buckling is a click the series is nearly FLAT rather than rolling off. That is not a detail: built with a mid `kmul` the series was 26 dB down by 5 kHz and the sac axis inverted, making the sound darker as the resonance rose, because the higher band had less to pass. In front of the train sits the abdominal air sac, a Helmholtz resonator measured 3.0-5.3 kHz with the song near 4.3 kHz, FIXED in Hz -- so a cicada an octave up is not a bigger cicada but a brighter one. Loudness 0.01 dB across the parameter cube, 0.02 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.01 dB over five octaves.

ribs.note: how many ribs reach their buckling load, as the flatness of the pulse train. The widest axis here: centroid 1627 -> 3163 Hz and the colour movement in the note 210 -> 1348 Hz, at 0.00 dB of loudness. The comb barely moves (57.5 -> 51.2 dB) because a flatter train is still a train -- what changes is how far up the series reaches, not whether it is one.

few.gloss: only the first ribs go -- a soft tick

all.gloss: every rib buckling -- a shrieking wall of insect

sac.note: where the abdominal air sac resonates, 3000 to 5300 Hz, which is the measured range for real species. Centroid 2038 -> 2614 Hz with the comb untouched at 0.8 dB -- the signature of a resonator in front of an unchanged source. Fixed in Hz, so it colours every pitch the same way. Loudness 0.00 dB.

deep body.gloss: a large abdomen, 3 kHz -- rounder and further off

song.gloss: the measured song band near 4.3 kHz

small.gloss: a small insect at 5.3 kHz -- piercing

rasp.note: how irregular the buckling is, as jitter on the train's rate. Measured as a comb change and not as a colour one: 69.9 -> 44.6 dB of contrast while the centroid moves 611 Hz, i.e. the series smears into a band instead of moving. A real tymbal is not a metronome, and at 0 this reads as an implausibly clean electronic buzz. Loudness 0.00 dB.

insect.gloss: the ordinary unevenness of a real one

tearing.gloss: so irregular the pitch dissolves into noise

techniques.code:
ksac    = 0.50                              ; sac: the abdominal air sac's resonance
kribs   = 0.55                              ; ribs: how many tymbal ribs buckle at once
krasp   = 0.40                              ; rasp: how irregular the buckling is
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A cicada has no voice. Each rib of the tymbal plate BUCKLES, and each buckling is
; one impulse; the ribs go in a train, and the train's RATE is what is heard as pitch
; (measured 100-200 a second, perceived between 329 and 660 Hz). So the source here is
; a pulse train -- which is to say a harmonic series -- and not an oscillator.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 40
; the song swells and eases, and a swelling cicada gets BRIGHTER as well as louder --
; more ribs reach their buckling load. Gating the whole signal would change the level
; and nothing else, since a spectral centroid does not care about scale.
ksw     poscil 0.5, 0.41
; A rib buckling is a CLICK, so the train's series is nearly flat -- not the smooth
; rolloff a mid `kmul` gives. Built at 0.52 the series was 26 dB down by 5 kHz and the
; sac axis fought it: moving the resonance 3000 -> 5300 Hz made the sound DARKER,
; because the higher band had 26 dB less to pass and `balance` then let the tone
; dominate. A flat source is both physically right and what lets the sac speak.
kmul    = 0.80 + 0.13 * kribs + 0.05 * ksw
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
kjit    rand 0.006, 0.53, 1                 ; the buckling is not metronomic
atr     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0 * (1 + krasp * kjit), knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The abdominal air sac is a Helmholtz resonator, measured 3.0-5.3 kHz with the song
; frequency near 4.3 kHz. FIXED in Hz -- an insect's body does not transpose, which is
; why a cicada an octave up is not a bigger cicada but a brighter one.
kfs     = 3000 + 2300 * ksac
abd     reson atr, kfs * (1 + 0.14 * ksw), kfs * 0.30, 2
amix    = atr * 0.32 + abd * (1.10 + 0.80 * (0.5 + ksw))
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: cricket -- a scraper dragged along a file of teeth, and the tooth-strike RATE is the carrier. That is why the tone is famously almost a pure sine: the file's tooth spacing is tuned to the wing's own resonance (measured 4-5 kHz for a field cricket), so the two coincide by evolution instead of by filtering. The entry rests on a second fact that a distant recording hides: close to, a cricket is NOT one tone -- the scraper dragging over the teeth is audible as broadband noise well above the carrier. That matters mechanically as well as musically, because a pure tone has nothing to move: without the file this body stood still at 18 Hz of travel, and movement by default is not satisfiable by a sine. The file also has a FLOOR, since a cricket always drags it, so no setting can stop the sound moving. Loudness 0.01 dB across the parameter cube, 0.06 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.04 dB over five octaves.

scrape.note: how much of the file is heard against the wing tone. The widest axis here and the one the instrument moves on: centroid 1820 -> 2188 Hz, comb 33.9 -> 24.9 dB and the colour movement in the note 32 -> 221 Hz, at 0.01 dB of loudness. Its share follows the wing speed, so it breathes with the chorus drift at 0.31 Hz whatever this is set to.

clean.gloss: heard from far off -- almost only the tone

close.gloss: a few metres away, the file audible

grinding.gloss: more file than tone -- a dry mechanical scrape

chirp.note: wing closures a second, 12 to 50 -- a RATE, and no spectral meter can see one. Measured on the colour meters this axis moves 2 Hz of centroid and 0.5 dB of comb, which reads as inert and is not: on the beat meter it reads back 12.0, 21.7, 31.0, 40.3 and 50.0 Hz against the 12, 22, 31, 40 and 50 asked, at a pulse depth of 0.34 to 0.41. Dolbear's law is the reason it is a control at all -- an insect's rate tracks temperature -- though Dolbear counted chirp GROUPS per minute, where this is the pulse rate inside them. Loudness 0.01 dB.

cold.gloss: 12 a second -- slow, a cold night

hot.gloss: 50 a second -- almost a continuous tone

pure.note: how sine-like the wing tone rings, as the reach of its harmonic series. Centroid 1980 -> 2087 Hz and comb 31.1 -> 27.8 dB -- a small axis by design, because a cricket's tone is nearly pure at every setting and this only decides how nearly. It deliberately does NOT touch the file: when it did, two axes multiplied and seven corners of the cube stood perfectly still. Loudness 0.01 dB.

reedy.gloss: several harmonics -- a coarser, buzzier insect

whistle.gloss: as pure as the wing goes

techniques.code:
kscrape = 0.40                              ; scrape: how much of the file is heard
kchirp  = 0.50                              ; chirp: wing closures a second
kpure   = 0.60                              ; pure: how sine-like the wing tone rings
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A cricket rubs a scraper along a file of teeth, and the TOOTH RATE is the carrier --
; which is why the tone is nearly a pure sine: the file's tooth spacing is tuned to the
; wing's own resonance, so the two coincide by evolution rather than by filtering.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 10
; A chorus drifts in and out of step, and that slow waver is the only rate the colour
; CAN move at: the wing closures run 12-50 a second, well above what a centroid
; sampled 32 times a second resolves, so a per-pulse colour change is invisible.
kdr     poscil 0.5, 0.31
kmul    = 0.46 - 0.38 * kpure
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
ato     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; Dolbear's law: the chirp rate tracks temperature, about 2.4 Hz at 13 C rising to 5.6
; at 27 C for the snowy tree cricket. A wing closure is one pulse.
kwc     = 12 + 38 * kchirp                  ; wing closures a second
kpl     poscil 0.5, kwc
akg     interp 0.42 + 0.58 * (0.5 + kpl)
; Close to, a cricket is not one tone: the scraper dragging over the teeth is audible
; as broadband noise well above the carrier, and how much of it there is follows the
; wing speed. This is where the colour moves -- a pure tone has nothing to move, so
; without the file the instrument stands still (measured: 18 Hz of travel).
anz     rand 0.6, 0.61, 1
kfs     = kf0 * 5.5
asc     reson anz, kfs, kfs * 0.8, 1
; a floor, because a cricket ALWAYS drags its file: with none of it the instrument
; stood perfectly still (0.6 Hz of travel), and no axis may be able to stop the sound
; moving
; `pure` deliberately does NOT touch this. It did, and then two axes multiplied: at
; scrape 0 with pure 1 everything that moves shrank to nothing and seven corners stood
; still. A pure-toned cricket still drags its file; what `pure` shapes is the TONE.
kscl    = (0.34 + 0.66 * kscrape) * (0.30 + 1.40 * (0.5 + kdr))
amix    = ato * akg + asc * akg * kscl * 0.55
aref    poscil 0.35, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

techniques.why: frog -- and the point of the entry is that a frog does not code its species in pitch but in the PULSE RATE. The larynx makes a rough buzz and the call is chopped into pulses at 15 to 100 a second, and that rate is what another frog listens for; carriers for pulsed calls run 300 Hz to 2 kHz. So the two axes that carry the instrument are a rate and a depth, and both are invisible to a colour meter -- `pulse` moves 5 Hz of centroid and 50.8 dB of comb contrast, which is the objective signature of chopping rather than filtering. In front of the larynx sits the inflated vocal sac, modelled here as a resonator FIXED in Hz at 380-1530. Modelled, not explained: the sac is NOT a cavity resonator. Rand & Dudley 1993 (Physiol. Zool. 66:793, "Frogs in helium: the anuran vocal sac is not a cavity resonator") put calling frogs in helium and the call frequency did not move -- it is an impedance-matching radiator, and the pitch is set at the larynx. A fixed formant is a fair model of the RADIATED spectrum and a false account of the mechanism, so do not carry the cavity reading across to another animal. Loudness 0.01 dB across the parameter cube, 0.03 dB across cube and register together, register tilt 0.02 dB over five octaves.

pulse.note: pulses a second, 15 to 100 -- the species marker. On the beat meter it reads back 15.0, 57.7 and 100.0 Hz against the 15, 58 and 100 asked. On the colour meters it moves 5 Hz of centroid and 50.8 dB of comb, because chopping a series at an audio rate puts sidebands around every harmonic and fills the gaps between them -- that comb collapse IS the measurement of the pulsing, not a side effect of it. Loudness 0.01 dB.

slow.gloss: 15 a second -- a deep, countable croak

buzz.gloss: the pulses running into each other

rattle.gloss: 100 a second -- a hard dry rattle, barely pitched

sac.note: how inflated the vocal sac is, as a fixed formant from 380 to 1530 Hz -- a model of what the sac RADIATES, not of a cavity resonating (see the entry's note). The only colour axis here: centroid 358 -> 551 Hz and the colour movement in the note 68 -> 150 Hz at 0.00 dB of loudness. Fixed in Hz, so a big sac is a big sac at every pitch. It also sags and refills at 0.37 Hz, which is where the instrument's movement comes from at every setting.

bullfrog.gloss: a big taut sac -- hollow and booming

croak.note: how deeply the pulses cut into the call, from a smooth buzz to a hard chop. Comb 70.4 -> 63.1 dB over the first three quarters of the axis, and 43.4 dB at the top, where the chop is deep enough that the sounding fundamental drops to a quarter of the note (f0 55.0 at an asked 220) and the reading moves onto that series. 2 Hz of centroid -- like `pulse` it is a comb measurement and not a colour one, and reading it by centroid alone would call it inert. Loudness 0.01 dB.

clacking.gloss: chopped to near silence between pulses

techniques.code:
ksac    = 0.45                              ; sac: how inflated the vocal sac is
kpulse  = 0.50                              ; pulse: pulses a second in the call
kcroak  = 0.55                              ; croak: how deeply the pulses cut
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A frog codes its species in the PULSE RATE, not in the pitch: the larynx makes a
; rough buzz and the call is chopped into pulses at 15-100 a second, which is what
; another frog listens to. The inflated vocal sac is a resonator in front of it.
knh     limit int(sr * 0.45 / kf0), 1, 24
; the sac empties as the call runs and refills between calls; a fuller sac drives the
; larynx harder, so this is a colour motion and not only a level one
ksg     poscil 0.5, 0.37
kmul    = 0.60 + 0.16 * ksg
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
alx     gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
kpr     = 15 + 85 * kpulse                  ; pulses a second
kpu     poscil 0.5, kpr
kgt     = 1 - kcroak * (0.30 + 0.55 * (0.5 + kpu))
akg     interp kgt * (1 + 0.09 * ksg)
; the vocal sac, FIXED in Hz. A big sac is a Helmholtz resonator low down; a small

techniques.why: handpan / hang -- struck metal that is nonetheless PITCHED, and the only such body here. Every other struck entry in this library is inharmonic by construction: a free bar rings at 1 : 2.76 : 5.40, glass at 1 : 2.71 : 3.83, a cymbal at 1 : 2.19 : 3.41, so they read as metal and never as a sung note. A handpan's note area is HAMMER-TUNED until its three lowest modes are 1 : 2 : 3 -- the fundamental, the octave and the twelfth. Measured at 220 Hz the partials are h1 0.0, h2 -18.4, h3 -23.3 dB and then a cliff to -70, against `struck_bar`'s -54.0 / -42.7 and `glass`'s -57.3 / -52.3. Reach for it when a prompt wants a struck, ringing, metallic sound that still has a clear note in it -- and for the wide, blooming, chordal quality no other struck entry has, because the shell couples the note areas and striking one wakes the rest. The bloom is `sympathy`, the low breath under it is the `gu` port, and `shimmer` is how far the other areas sit from true. The pitch is the played note at every register (+1.3, 0.0, -1.6, -0.4, +2.6 and +7.7 cents over six octaves; the last is `mode`'s own warp, which reads +19 cents at 3520 Hz on a bare resonance and belongs to the opcode). The bare word "hang" is deliberately NOT one of its surface forms even though it is the instrument's own name: "let the sound hang in the air" is ordinary prose about sustain, and as a form it cut the author's whole library down to this one entry. "tongue drum" is left out too — a steel tongue drum is a different instrument, and carrying it here named `drum_head` and `handpan` together for a prompt that means neither.
techniques.code:
ksymp   = 0.45                              ; sympathy [0..1]: how much the shell rings with it
kgu     = 0.40                              ; gu [0..1]: how far the bottom port is opened
kshimmer = 0.35                             ; shimmer [0..1]: how far the other areas sit from true
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
aexw    rand 0.05, 0.5, 1                   ; continuous exciter, so a held note stands
; A hand on a metal shell is a SOFT contact: it puts energy into the low modes and almost
; none above them. Leaving the exciter flat to Nyquist is not neutral, it pours noise through
; every resonance at once -- and that noise, not the sound, is then what the shell's colour
; track is made of: at 1760 Hz it drowns the settle below and the note reads as static.
; A handpan is played with the hands ON it, and they never leave: where the palm rests
; and how hard decides which modes are damped and how bright the contact is. That is one
; slow motion reaching BOTH the drive's colour and the balance between the note's own
; three modes, so no setting of any axis can make the instrument stand still -- which is
; what `mbira` does with its thumb, and for the same reason.
kbr     poscil 0.5, 0.31
aex     butterlp aexw, limit(kf0 * (2.6 + 3.2 * (0.5 + kbr)), 200, 16000)
; A hang's note area is HAMMER-TUNED so its three lowest modes are 1 : 2 : 3 -- the
; fundamental, the octave and the twelfth (Fletcher/Rossing, holographic interferometry on
; a pentatonic HANG). That is the whole reason for a separate entry: everything else struck
; in this library is INharmonic by construction -- a free bar is 2.76 / 5.40 / 8.93, glass
; 2.71 / 3.83 / 5.17, a cymbal 2.19 / 3.41. Three isolated high-Q modes at exact 1:2:3 is
; neither a bell nor a harmonic buzz: the note is clean and pitched like a sung tone and
; still decays and shimmers like struck metal.
; An open port radiates, and a shell that radiates loses energy: its resonances broaden.
; So opening the port is not only the cavity note arriving, it is the whole shell going from
; a narrow, pure, bell-like ring to a broader and breathier one. Not further than 0.30,
; though, and that bound is measured rather than chosen: at 0.70 the bands are broad enough
; that the exciter's own wander outweighs the hand motion below, and nine corners of the
; cube read as standing still at 880 Hz. At 0.30 none of the 135 does, at any register.
kq      = 1 - 0.30 * kgu
kn1     limit kf0, 20, 15000
kn2     limit kf0 * 2, 20, 15000
kn3     limit kf0 * 3, 20, 15000
an1     mode aex, kn1, 1150 * kq
an2     mode aex, kn2, 1300 * kq
an3     mode aex, kn3, 1450 * kq
; …and the measured fact that makes a hang sound like one instrument rather than eight: the
; shell COUPLES the areas, so striking one wakes the others. In the published measurement a
; note area driven at 524 Hz set the area an octave below ringing in ITS second mode and the
; one a twelfth below in its third -- all three at 524 Hz at once. So the partners add
; energy AT the played pitch, from bodies of their own, and they also speak their own lower
; modes: an octave below at f/2 and 1.5f, a twelfth below at f/3 and 2f/3.
;
; Those partials at f/3, f/2 and 2f/3 are the point. Nothing else here rings BELOW the note
; it is playing, and they are simple ratios rather than a subharmonic mush, so the shell
; reads as a chord that the note is a member of. They have to stay FAR under the note: the
; played note must be the pitch you hear, and `mode` hands a resonance at f/2 twice the
; amplitude of one at f for the same drive, so every weight below carries its own ratio as a
; factor -- that is what makes these numbers read as the amplitudes they actually are.

sympathy.note: how much of the shell answers the note that was struck. This is the measured coupling and not an effect: driven at one note area, the area an octave below rings in its second mode and the one a twelfth below in its third, all at the played pitch, and each also speaks its own lower modes at f/2, 1.5f, f/3 and 2f/3. So the shell reads as a chord the note is a member of, which is the one thing a handpan does that no other struck body here can. Its mark is the COMB and not the centroid, and by a long way: 48.2 dB with a single area speaking, 19.4 dB with the whole shell in, because the partners fill the places between the note's own three modes. The centroid moves only 12 Hz across it -- every partner sits at or below the note, so adding them does not brighten anything. The partners must stay far under the note or they take the pitch: each weight below carries its own frequency ratio as a factor, because `mode` hands a resonance at f/2 twice the amplitude of one at f for the same drive. Loudness 0.06 dB.

single note.gloss: one area alone: dry, clean, almost a bell

quiet shell.gloss: the shell just audible behind the note

whole shell.gloss: every area answering: wide and chordal

gu.note: how far the port on the underside is opened, which on a real instrument is the spacing of the player's knees. Two things at once, and both are the same physics: the cavity note comes up (a Helmholtz resonance at 88-122 Hz, fixed in HERTZ, so it does not transpose with the keyboard), and the shell itself radiates more and therefore rings less narrowly. Its mark is the MOTION, which nearly doubles as the port opens -- 135 -> 212 Hz of colour travelling inside the note -- because broader resonances let more of the hand's own breathing through; comb 25.5 -> 23.7 dB and centroid 8 Hz. The broadening is deliberately bounded at 0.30 of the Q: at 0.70 the bands are wide enough that the exciter's wander outweighs the hand and nine corners of the cube stand still at 880 Hz, where at 0.30 none of 135 does at any register. The cavity is also taken away under a note lower than itself, because a Helmholtz resonator driven well below its own note does not resonate -- the air in the neck just moves with the shell -- and that is the only reason a bass note here keeps its pitch. Loudness 0.06 dB.

closed.gloss: knees shut on the port: pure and narrow

wide open.gloss: the cavity breathing under the note

shimmer.note: how far the other note areas sit from true. Hammer-tuning is never exact, so the partners' OWN free modes land a little off their ratios and the shell reads as a spread chord rather than a stack: comb 28.1 -> 21.3 dB, centroid 0 Hz, loudness 0.01 dB. A driven partial is AT its driver, and detuning those two put three components within a few cents of each other, which is a unison beat and not a shimmer -- it measured 16.0 dB of loudness travelling inside one held note.

true.gloss: every area exactly in ratio: clean and cold

techniques.why: tanpura -- the one string in this library that gets BRIGHTER AFTER the attack -- keyed to `knote`, so it does so on every note the plugin plays and not only when the instance happens to start there, and the only entry anywhere in it whose spectrum climbs on its own. A cotton thread, the jivari, is worked in between string and bridge until the string rolls on and off it during every cycle; each roll shortens the sounding length for part of the period and injects harmonics that were not in the pluck. So energy migrates UP the series after the note starts, then settles -- the halo, and the reason a tanpura is laid under a raga rather than played. Every other string here (`string`, `harpsichord`, `strings`, `supersaw`) is brightest at the attack and darkens from there. Reach for it when a prompt wants a drone that is alive, a shimmering or blooming or breathing string, a sustained bed that will not sit still, or anything Indian, tambura, sitar-adjacent or raga-like. `jvari` is how far the thread is pushed in (centroid 1519 -> 2210 Hz, comb 35.9 -> 43.3 dB) and `bloom` how far up the halo travels (centroid 1328 -> 2302 Hz, colour motion 384 -> 1343 Hz). The pitch is the played note at every register: -0.1, 0.0, 0.0, +0.4, +1.8 and +2.5 cents over six octaves.
techniques.code:
kjvari  = 0.50                              ; jvari [0..1]: how far the thread is pushed under the string
kbloom  = 0.45                              ; bloom [0..1]: how far up the halo travels
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A tanpura is tuned for a thing no other string instrument wants: a cotton thread (the
; jivari) is worked in between the string and the bridge until the string ROLLS on and off

close.gloss: the halo stays low: warm, contained

high.gloss: it climbs far up: glassy, shimmering, wide open

techniques.why: ocarina -- and it is NOT a small flute, which is the whole reason it is here. A flute is a PIPE with a full harmonic series of resonances, which is why it overblows to the octave and why `flute` has a full spectrum. A vessel flute is a HELMHOLTZ resonator: the pitch comes from the enclosed volume and the total open hole area, not from any length, and a Helmholtz resonator has exactly ONE resonance. So an ocarina cannot overblow at all, and its tone is very nearly a pure sine with a weak second partial from the jet's own nonlinearity and almost nothing above it. Nothing else in this library has that spectrum -- `flute`, `clarinet`, `brass` and every reed are built on a series. Reach for it for a simple, round, hollow, breathy, ancient or folk-toned wind; for a nearly pure tone that is still played rather than synthetic; and when a prompt wants a flute WITHOUT the brightness a pipe brings. `breath` is how hard it is blown, `chiff` how much wind is in the tone.
techniques.code:
kbreath = 0.45                              ; breath [0..1]: how hard it is blown
kchiff  = 0.40                              ; chiff [0..1]: how much wind is in the tone
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; An ocarina is not a small flute. A flute is a PIPE, with a whole harmonic series of
; resonances, which is why it overblows to the octave and why `flute` here has a full
; spectrum. A vessel flute is a HELMHOLTZ resonator: the pitch is set by the enclosed volume
; and the total open hole area, not by any length, and a Helmholtz resonator has exactly ONE
; resonance. So an ocarina cannot overblow at all, and its tone is very nearly a pure sine
; with a weak second partial from the jet's own nonlinearity and almost nothing above it.
; That is a spectrum nothing else in this library has: `flute`, `clarinet`, `brass` and the
; reeds are all built on a series.
; The second partial is the only harmonic there is, and how strong it is IS the blowing
; pressure -- a hard-blown vessel flute goes edgy without going up an octave, because there
; is no second resonance for it to jump to. It also BREATHES, because the jet's nonlinearity
; varies with the air that drives it.
kwan    poscil 0.5, 0.43                     ; the air wandering
kh2     = (0.070 + 0.28 * kbreath * kbreath) * (0.30 + 1.40 * (0.5 + kwan))
apure   poscil 0.34, limit(kf0, 20, 18000)
asec    poscil 0.34 * kh2, limit(kf0 * 2, 20, 18000)
; The breath noise is shaped by the SAME single resonance as the tone, because on a vessel
; flute there is only one, and its edge wanders as the player's air does.
anz     rand 1.0, 0.5, 1
kwf     = limit(kf0 * (1.7 + 2.6 * (0.5 + kwan) * (0.4 + 0.9 * kbreath)), 60, 16000)
awnd    reson anz, kwf, kwf * 0.75, 2
; A floor under the wind, because an ocarina is ALWAYS breathy: it is a fipple instrument
; with the jet a couple of millimetres from the edge, and no setting may make it a sine.
; The wind also has a CEILING, and where both sit was measured rather than chosen. At
; 0.05 + 0.34 the hiss sat only 3 dB under the tone and 16 of 27 corners read as having NO
; PITCH AT ALL -- unusable on an instrument whose whole character is a clear round note; at
; 0.03 + 0.14, still 6 of 27. It has to stay at or under about a third of the tone.
; That ceiling is why the colour motion here cannot come from the wind alone. At the clean
; corner (chiff 0) the tone is nearly a bare sine, and the two things that can move it were
; each too small on their own: the breathing second partial with the wind floor at 0.02
; failed the movement gate at that corner, and the 0.035 floor with a FLAT second partial
; failed it at all three breath settings. Together they carry it, and nothing here reads as
; unpitched at any of six registers.
kwl     = 0.035 + 0.085 * kchiff
amix    = (apure + asec) * sqrt(1 - kwl * kwl * 0.7) + awnd * kwl
aref    poscil 0.3000, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

breath.note: how hard it is blown. On a vessel flute there is only one resonance, so blowing harder cannot take it up an octave -- there is no second resonance to jump to. What happens instead is that the jet's own nonlinearity puts more into the second partial (0.061 to 0.289 of the fundamental, -24.3 to -10.8 dB) and pushes the breath noise's edge up. That is the whole difference between a soft and a hard ocarina note: it goes edgy without going up. That second partial also BREATHES with the air that drives it, and it has to: it is one of the only two things in this body whose colour can move at all.

soft.gloss: almost a pure sine, barely a second partial

hard.gloss: edgy and reedy, and still not an octave up

chiff.note: how much wind is in the tone. The breath noise is shaped by the SAME single resonance as the tone, because on a vessel flute there is only one, and its edge wanders as the player's air does. There is a floor of wind under every setting, which is true of the instrument too -- a fipple with the jet two millimetres off the edge is never silent -- and no setting may turn this into a sine. There is also a CEILING, and it is the reason this axis is narrower than it looks: the hiss stays at or under about a third of the tone, because louder than that it masks the note. Measured, at half the tone 16 of 27 corners read as having no pitch at all, on an instrument whose whole character is a clear round note. The tone and the wind are weighted so their powers sum, so this is colour and not level.

clean.gloss: the tone with only a trace of air

airy.gloss: soft, close, whispered, the air plainly audible

techniques.why: hurdy-gurdy -- a drone bowed by a WHEEL, so it never stops for a bow change or a breath, with a percussion instrument built into it. That second part is what nothing else in this library has: the chien, the dog, a tiny loose bridge under one string held down by nothing but a twist of thread. Accelerate the crank and the string's tension pulse lifts it off the soundboard so it slaps back down, and that rhythmic buzz -- keyed to the WHEEL and not to the note -- is how a hurdy-gurdy articulates. Reach for it for a rhythmic, buzzing, rasping, mechanical or medieval drone; for anything folk, cranked or street-organ-like; and whenever a prompt wants a sustained sound that nonetheless has a pulse in it without a sequencer. `chien` is how hard the buzzing bridge works, `press` how hard the wheel is loaded against the strings.
techniques.code:
kchien  = 0.45                              ; chien [0..1]: how hard the buzzing bridge works
kpress  = 0.50                              ; press [0..1]: how hard the wheel is loaded
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A hurdy-gurdy is bowed by a WHEEL, so it never stops: no bow change, no breath, a drone
; that runs as long as the crank turns. That much a bowed string here could do. What it has
; that nothing else in this library has is the chien -- the dog -- a tiny loose bridge under
; one string, held down only by a twist of thread. When the crank is accelerated the string's
; tension pulse lifts it off the soundboard and it slaps back down, and that RHYTHMIC BUZZ,
; keyed to the wheel and not to the note, is how a hurdy-gurdy articulates. It is a
; percussion instrument built into a drone.
; The wheel itself is not perfectly round and the rosin does not grip evenly, so the drone
; breathes at the crank's own rate. This is the coherent colour motion in the body and it is
; the crank, not an effect. Rate and depth are measured: at 0.83 Hz, with the crank reaching
; only the output level and not `kmul`, five corners read as variance rather than motion
; (coherence 0.00 to 0.35) -- the drone's BRIGHTNESS has to move, not just its loudness,
; and at chien 0 there is nothing else in the body that moves at all.
kcrk    poscil 0.5, 1.45                     ; the wheel coming round
kmax    = int(sr * 0.45 / kf0)
knh     limit kmax, 1, 26
; wheel pressure lights more of the series, exactly as bow force does on a string
kmul    = 0.42 + 0.34 * kpress + 0.11 * (0.5 + kcrk)
knrm    = ((1-kmul^knh)/(1-kmul)) / sqrt((1-kmul^(2*knh))/(1-kmul*kmul)*0.5)
adrn    gbuzz 0.17 * knrm, kf0, knh, 1, kmul, giCos
; The chien's buzz sits at the crank's coup rate, a few a second, and the SLAP is what is
; audible: a short broadband contact against the soundboard, not a tone. Written against
; phase, so the energy per second does not depend on the rate.
kcr     = 2.2 + 5.6 * kchien                 ; coups a second
kcp     phasor kcr * (1 + 0.11 * kcrk)
kslap   = exp(-16 * kcp)
anz     rand 1.0, 0.5, 1
kbf     = limit(kf0 * 4.4, 200, 12000)
abz     reson anz * a(kslap), kbf, kbf * 0.9, 2
; The drone's own brightness follows the wheel; its LEVEL follows the wheel only slightly, at
; about +-0.65 dB, and that small figure is deliberate and measured. At +-1.6 dB the wheel's
; own breathing was the loudest periodicity in the sound at every setting, so the dog -- the
; thing this entry exists for -- never became the pulse you hear. With the level breathing
; small, `chien` moves the dominant period from the wheel's 1.3 a second to the coup's 7.7.
kdb     = 0.78 * (0.92 + 0.16 * (0.5 + kcrk))
; The slap has a CEILING, because past it the drone stops being a note. A hard coup on a real
; instrument is very present, but at a slap as loud as the drone the pitch was unreadable at
; the two lowest registers -- and no band placement rescued it: measured at 4.4x, 6.5x, 8x
; and 12x the note, at bandwidths from 0.45 to 0.9 of centre, and with shorter sharper coups
; at constant slap energy, every one of them still lost the note. It is level, not position.
; At this ceiling the coup is still the dominant pulse and the note reads within 2 cents at
; all six registers.
kbl     = 0.30 + 0.35 * kchien
amix    = adrn * kdb * sqrt(1 - kbl * kbl * 0.55) + abz * kbl * 0.62
aref    poscil 0.3000, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

chien.note: how hard the buzzing bridge works -- the thread's twist, on a real instrument. It sets the coup rate, from just over two a second to nearly eight, and how much of the sound the slap is. The slap is a short broadband contact against the soundboard and not a tone, so it is shaped by a wide band well above the note. Its envelope is written against PHASE rather than time, which means each coup's duration scales as 1/rate, its energy as 1/rate, and the energy per second does not depend on the rate at all -- so this axis is not a volume control with a buzz attached, and no compensation is needed. What the axis does is measured: it moves the loudest periodicity in the sound from the wheel's 1.3 a second to the coup's 7.7. The slap stops short of the drone's own level on purpose, because louder than that the note itself stopped being readable at the two lowest registers.

silent dog.gloss: a plain wheel drone, the bridge quiet

hard coup.gloss: a fast rattling pulse over the drone

press.note: how hard the wheel is loaded against the strings, which lights more of the harmonic series exactly as bow force does on a string. Built on `gbuzz` with the closed-form normalisation this library uses, so the series can widen without the level moving. Note that the crank reaches this and not only the output: the wheel is not perfectly round and the rosin does not grip evenly, so the drone's BRIGHTNESS breathes at the crank's own rate. That is measured, not decorative -- with the crank touching only the level, five corners of the cube read as variance rather than motion, because at chien 0 there was then nothing in the body whose colour moved at all. Its level breathes too, but only slightly, so that the dog and not the wheel is the pulse you hear.

light.gloss: a thin, soft, almost recorder-like drone

leaning in.gloss: broad and reedy, the full series speaking

techniques.why: bubbles in water -- a brook, a spring, anything gurgling. A bubble is a mass of air on a spring of water and rings at the Minnaert frequency, f = (1/2pi R) sqrt(3 gamma P / rho), about 3.26/R hertz-metres: a millimetre bubble sings near 3.3 kHz, a centimetre one near 330 Hz. Each one is a damped sinusoid at Q about 15 whose pitch RISES over the pulse as the bubble contracts -- which is why a single bubble sounds like a plink and not a click. Three sizes at incommensurate release rates over the broadband sheet of water under them. The size distribution IS the pitch distribution, so fast water over stones sounds high and a slow spring sounds low and hollow, and that is what `size` moves. Reach for it for water, wet, liquid, underwater, gurgling, percolating, and for any sparse plinking texture that is not a mallet. `flow` is releases a second, `size` how wide the bubbles are.
techniques.code:
kflow   = 0.45                              ; flow [0..1]: how fast the water is running
ksize   = 0.50                              ; size [0..1]: how wide the bubbles are
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; MOVEMENT: TEXTURE
; A stochastic event texture, not a sustained tone.
; Its liveness is where and when the events fall, which no statistic in
; `lco_measure` can tell from a static noise bed (see `declares_texture`).
; A bubble in water is a mass of air on a spring of water and it rings at the Minnaert
; frequency, f = (1/2piR) * sqrt(3*gamma*P/rho), which comes to about 3.26/R hertz-metres:
; a bubble a millimetre across sings near 3.3 kHz, one a centimetre across near 330 Hz. It
; is a damped sinusoid at Q around 15, and its pitch RISES over the pulse as the bubble
; contracts. A brook is a train of them, and the size distribution IS the pitch
; distribution -- which is why fast water over stones sounds high and a slow spring sounds
; low and hollow. Nothing here made a pitched, granular water.
; Three sizes at incommensurate rates. `flow` is how often they are released, `size` moves
; all three together along the Minnaert relation. The rate range is bounded at BOTH ends
; and both bounds are measured. Below about eight a second the level of a note depends on
; which bubbles happened to land in it -- a window artefact, not a sound: the cube read
; 3.78 dB apart with a floor of three. Above about twenty-four the colour track cannot
; resolve the train at all, because it is sampled some 43 times a second, and every corner
; reads as variance rather than motion -- at 12-70 a second, seven of nine corners failed.
; This is the same limit `cricket` records for its wing closures.
krt     = 8.0 + 16.0 * kflow                 ; releases a second in the largest stream
; The wander in the rate is slow and deep rather than fast and shallow, and that is also
; measured: a fast jitter smears each local burst until the meter cannot find its rate
; (0.22 at 1.3 Hz left seven corners reading as variance), while a slow drift leaves the
; train locally periodic and globally aperiodic. Physically it is the flow finding and
; losing its channels. All nine corners move, at coherence 0.41 to 0.72.
; The seed is INSIDE the 0..1 range Csound wants. Written as `randi 0.14, 0.19, 2`
; it was out of range, so the generator seeded from the CLOCK and this body
; rendered differently every time -- which makes every measurement of it one
; draw rather than a property, and made a peak sweep read 4.03, 4.73 and 4.04 on
; three passes of the same grid.
kj      randi 0.14, 0.19, 0.5, 1
kp1     phasor krt * (1 + kj)
kp2     phasor krt * 0.577 * (1 - kj * 0.7)
kp3     phasor krt * 1.483 * (1 + kj * 0.4)
; What moves is the size the stream is throwing off: water running over stones does not
; hold one bubble size, it wanders as the flow finds and loses its channels. This is the
; coherent motion in the body -- a bubble train on its own reads as variance, because the
; centroid track of scattered blips is broadband and the meter asks for a rate it can find.
kwan    poscil 0.5, 0.23
kmn     = (3.4 - 3.0 * ksize) * (0.62 + 0.76 * (0.5 + kwan))   ; the Minnaert factor
; Each event's envelope is an exponential over its phasor's PHASE: the attack, the
; rising pitch inside one bubble, and the Q ~ 15 decay. Written against PHASE, so the
; energy per second does not depend on the release rate: each event's duration scales as
; 1/rate, its energy as 1/rate, and the product is constant.
kr1     = 1 + 0.16 * kp1
kr2     = 1 + 0.21 * kp2
kr3     = 1 + 0.12 * kp3
ab1     poscil exp(-11 * kp1) * 0.26, limit(kf0 * kmn * 1.00 * kr1, 20, 18000)
ab2     poscil exp(-14 * kp2) * 0.19, limit(kf0 * kmn * 1.94 * kr2, 20, 18000)
ab3     poscil exp(-9 * kp3) * 0.15, limit(kf0 * kmn * 0.53 * kr3, 20, 18000)
; Under the bubbles, the water itself: the sheet of it breaking over stones is broadband
; and it is what a listener hears as "running" rather than "dripping". It rises with the
; flow, and it is the only part of this that does.
anz     rand 1.0, 0.5, 1
awt     atone anz, 1800
amix    = ab1 + ab2 + ab3 + awt * (0.06 + 0.10 * kflow)
; `balance` holds both axes to one loudness across the cube and the keyboard. Safe here
; because this body STANDS -- a continuous train of releases, not a decay a follower
; could flatten.
aref    poscil 0.3000, 400
asig    balance amix, aref, 1

flow.note: how fast the water is running: 8 to 24 releases a second in the largest stream, with the other two sizes at incommensurate multiples of it so nothing ever lines up into a pulse. The broadband sheet under the bubbles rises with it, because faster water is both more bubbles and more sheet. The envelope is written against the phasor's PHASE and not against time, so each bubble's duration scales as 1/rate and its energy with it -- the energy per second does not depend on the rate, which is why this is a rate and not a volume. Written against time it was a 3.78 dB fader, because the level then depended on which bubbles happened to land inside the note.

trickle.gloss: the quietest brook this body has -- 24 releases a second across the three trains, not a drip: the rate floor is deliberate and measured (see the code)

rushing.gloss: fast water over stones, nearly continuous

size.note: how wide the bubbles are, all three sizes together along the Minnaert relation, so the ratios between them stay physical and only the scale moves. Wide bubbles ring low and hollow, narrow ones high and glassy -- the same fact that makes a deep pool sound different from a shallow rill, and the reason the axis reads DOWNWARD in pitch as it rises: `kmn = (3.4 - 3.0 * ksize)`, so at 0 the three trains sit at 246-2003 Hz for a 220 Hz note and at 1 they sit at 29-236. The anchors were named the other way round until 2026-07-25 and no colour meter caught it, because the broadband water sheet under the bubbles dominates the centroid and carries it UP across the axis (9378 -> 10182 Hz) while the bubbles themselves go down. It moves the colour and not the level, since each bubble's energy is set by its envelope and not by its frequency.

wide.gloss: big slow bubbles, low and hollow

techniques.why: cracking ice on a frozen lake, and the reason it sounds like science fiction rather than like a click is dispersion. Flexural waves in a thin plate have a phase velocity going as sqrt(f), so the high components of a single impulse outrun the low ones and arrive first: arrival time t(f) = d/(k sqrt(f)) inverts to f(t) proportional to 1/t^2, and what reaches you is a descending whistle from one instantaneous crack. Nothing else in this library has a dispersive source -- every other body here is modes or filtered noise. Two trains at incommensurate rates plus the dull water-loaded knock of the impact itself. Reach for it for ice, frost, glacial, brittle, alien, sci-fi, laser-like or ricocheting descending sounds, and for any sparse texture whose events GLIDE. `crack` is arrivals a second, `glide` how far above the note each dive starts.
techniques.code:
kcrack  = 0.45                              ; crack [0..1]: how busy the ice is
kglide  = 0.50                              ; glide [0..1]: how far each crack falls
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1)
; A crack in lake ice does not reach you as a click. Flexural waves in a plate are
; DISPERSIVE -- their phase velocity goes as the square root of frequency -- so the high
